| Condition | Changes |
|---|---|
| width ≤ 920px | The species bar wraps onto rows (flex-wrap, centred, row-gap 2px, overflow visible, radius 22px) instead of scrolling, so all seven options are always visible; the thumb follows rows because it uses offsetTop too |
| width ≤ 720px | Top bar spans left/right 12px (top = max(12px, safe-area top)), the bar may use 100% width; the Tweaks opener moves to the bottom-right (bottom = max(12px, safe-area bottom)); the open panel becomes a bottom sheet (left/right/bottom 12px, auto width, max-height 70vh); the hint sits at bottom max(22px, safe-area + 10px) |
| width ≤ 640px | Pills shrink to height 30px, padding 0 11px 0 9px, gap 6px, 12.5px text (thumb 30px) — two rows on a 375px phone |
| width ≤ 520px | The "Add tabs or files" label hides, leaving the round plus button (padding 0 9px) |
| width ≤ 360px | Pills padding 0 8px 0 7px, gap 5px, 12px text — still two rows at 320px |
| width ≤ 640px and height 521–700px | Avatar 48px, masthead gap 10px and margin 18px, stage centre pushed down 30px so the wrapped bar never touches the avatar |
| height ≤ 520px (landscape phones) | Avatar hidden, masthead gap 8px / margin 14px, greeting 22px, composer gap 10px and padding 12px 10px 10px 14px, top bar at max(8px, safe-area top), stage centre pushed down 24px |
| prefers-reduced-motion | All UI transitions off; the canvas draws a single settled still (see section 8) |

## 6. The canvas renderer (the ASCII grid)

The canvas is sized to its CSS box times devicePixelRatio (capped at 2) and redrawn every frame. It is a grid of character cells:

- Cell width cw = clamp(round(viewport width ÷ 124 ÷ detail), 5, 24) px, cell height ch = round(cw × 1.45). "detail" is the per-species "ASCII detail" tuning (1.3 by default; 1.7 for Rabbit and Eagle). At 1440 wide and detail 1.3 the cells are 9 × 13 px.
- Background layer (cached on an offscreen canvas, repainted only on resize, grid change or hue change): fill rgb(6,7,12), then 1px grid lines on every cell boundary in rgba(255,255,255, 0.055 × grid), where "grid" is a tuning (1.05 default).
- Each frame: copy the background, draw the trail layer, then draw every non-empty cell. Text is drawn centred in its cell with font "600 round(ch × 0.74)px" + the canvas font family, textBaseline middle, at y + ch/2 + 1.
- Cell states: empty, stroke (glyph only) and solid (a filled rectangle inset 1px — x+1, y+1, cw−1, ch−1 — plus a glyph on top). Solid cells win over strokes.

How an animal becomes cells: every animal is an implicit shape function of local coordinates (u along its heading, v across it, both in units of its "span" in pixels). For each cell inside a square of ± extent × span around the animal, the function is probed at the cell centre and at four sub-points (fractions .25/.30, .75/.30, .25/.72, .75/.72 of the cell). It returns false (outside) or a colour plus a "kind" and optional glyph set. Coverage = hits ÷ 5.

- If the centre is outside or coverage < 0.6 it is an edge cell: a stroke whose glyph is picked from ":;" (coverage ≥ .5) or ".',`" and whose colour is the cell colour faded toward the background by fog + .55 − .45 × coverage.
- Otherwise the cell is solid, with a fill and a glyph colour that depend on the kind:

| Kind | Fill | Glyph colour | Default glyphs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plain | colour (with fog) | 0.42 × fill | ".:;+=*%#" chosen by inverse luminance ± 1 jitter |
| Shine | same as Plain, but brightness × (1 − .4 × shimmer + shimmer × sin(2.2t + 9u + 6v + tilt + 2 × heading)) | 0.42 × fill | same ramp |
| Dark | colour | fill × 1.7 + (34,30,30) | "#%@" |
| Light | colour | 0.4 × fill | "o*" |
| Fur | colour | fill × 1.6 + (44,40,36) | "8#@" |
| Soft | colour faded by min(1, .62 + .38 × fog) | colour | ".:;+=*%#" |
| Bright | 0.58 × colour | colour × 1.05 + 50 | ".:*" |
| Line | no fill (stroke only, never over a solid) | colour | ".:+*" by luminance |

- Glyph choice is stable per animal: a hash of the animal id and the cell's rounded local position picks a character from the set, so patterns stick to the body as it moves instead of flickering.
- Every cell's brightness gets a tiny ±3% flicker that re-rolls 6 times a second. Sparkle: a per-cell hash re-rolled ~2.4 times a second turns the glyph pure white, light ice blue or pale cyan when below the "sparkle" tuning (full rate on Shine, a third on Plain, also on Soft and Bright).
- Depth fog: fog = (1 − depth) × "Distance fade" tuning; colours are mixed toward the background by that amount.
- Hue shift: all colours are passed through a standard luminance-preserving hue-rotation matrix by the "Hue shift" degrees.
- Lines: segments between two points are rasterised every half a cell, each cell getting a stroke glyph chosen from the segment angle ("-", "\\", "|" or "/"), optionally ending in a custom glyph. Dots put one glyph in one cell. Spots are single solid cells with their own fill and glyph (used for eyes, written as "●").

Trails: a per-cell energy field. Animals "shed" energy into the cell under a point (amount × "Trail" tuning, capped at 1.6); taps and landings "stamp" a round blob of radius r cells (rows weighted 1.4×). Each frame the field is diffused (new = (4 × self + 4 neighbours) ÷ 8) and decays by exp(−dt × "Trail fade"). It is drawn as small squares (size max(2, round(0.19 × cw)) px, one larger above 0.6 energy) centred at 50%/60% of each cell, in six alpha steps of the species' trail colour (alpha 0.85 × step/6), with a gentle per-cell twinkle (× 0.75 + 0.25 sin(5t + hash × 40)). Trail squares never draw over solid cells.

## 7. The flock (shared motion system)

- Fixed-step simulation at 60 Hz (accumulator, at most 4 steps per frame, dt capped at 0.1 s). Drawing happens every requestAnimationFrame; the loop pauses when the canvas is not intersecting the viewport and never runs under reduced motion.
- base size = clamp(min(viewport w, h) × 0.2, 80, 190) × species scale. Each animal has a random "roll" 0–1; depth = farthest + (1 − farthest) × roll^farBias; span = base × depth × size. Animals are kept sorted by roll so near ones draw last (on top).
- Population: target = clamp(round(w × h ÷ (area × (base ÷ scale ÷ 160)²) × density), 1, 200). Extra animals are removed at random; new ones spawn off-screen on the upwind edge (or, on first load and half of later spawns, anywhere on screen).
- Course: the travel direction in degrees (0 = right, 90 = up) from the species' "Direction", or, if "Corner to corner" is on, the bottom-left-to-top-right diagonal of the window. The group heading sways: course + sway × (sin(0.13t) + 0.5 sin(0.31t + 1.7)). Each animal has a bias in −1..1 multiplied by "Spread".
- Steering: acceleration toward (cos aim, sin aim) × speed minus current velocity, times a gain; separation pushes apart animals within (spanA + spanB) × reach whose depths differ by less than 0.18, strength = "Separation"; speed is capped (plus 300 px/s while startled). cruise speed = species speed × (0.55 + 0.45 × depth) × "Speed". The heading turns toward the velocity at a limited rate.
- Wrapping: when an animal has passed the downwind edge by one span (or is three spans off-screen anywhere) it re-enters on the upwind edge, placed along the edges in proportion to their exposure to the course.
- Tap / click (pointerdown on the canvas only, ignored under reduced motion): stamps a 6-cell trail burst of 1.4 at the point and startles every animal within 240 px with strength k = 1 − distance/240 (each species reacts in its own way below), unless the species overrides taps (Sea turtle drops food instead).

## 8. The seven species

Default travel directions: Moth, Sea turtle, Owl and Eagle 49° (toward the top-right); Squid and Flying fish 131° (toward the top-left); Rabbit 0° (straight left to right). All other tuning defaults are listed per species; unlisted values come from the shared defaults: density 1, speed 1, sway .04, spread .06, size 1, farthest .45, farBias 1.6, grip 2, separation 300, hue 0, shimmer .3, sparkle .12, fog .75, trail 1, trail fade 1.3, grid 1.05, detail 1.3.

White body ellipse (.17 × .062) with faint "v" chest bars; bright white head (252,252,255) Light "o." at u .215 (.075 × .048); gold (240,190,70) hooked beak "@" and "v"; a white fan tail from u −.14 to −.38 widening to ±.12 with notched tips; two gold talon lines under the tail. Gold-ringed eyes "●" at (.225, ±max(.026, cw/span)) when the bird is large enough. Lighting .82 + .18 × arm.

## 9. Tweaks panel

- Opener: a glass pill fixed at top 16px, right 16px (z-index 10), height 34px, padding 0 14px 0 12px, 13px weight 500, --text-soft (hover --text), --blur 10px, with a 15px sliders icon and the word "Tweaks". Under .liquid the Tweaks elements use plain blur, not the displacement filter. Dark background colour #0a0c148c behind the glass.
- Panel: glass aside, top 16px right 16px, width 288px, max-height 100vh − 32px, radius 20px, 12px text, --blur 18px, tint .1/.06. Header (padding 12px 10px 10px 16px, bottom border --chip-edge): title "Tweaks" (13px 500), "Copy" and "Reset" chip buttons (26px tall, radius 999px) and a 26px round close "×". Body scrolls (padding 4px 16px 14px, overscroll contained).
- Groups, each with an uppercase Geist Mono 600 10px header (letter-spacing .08em, --muted): "Movement" (Density 0.1–4; Corner to corner toggle; Direction 0–360°, disabled while Corner to corner is on; Speed 0.1–3; Sway 0–.6; Spread 0–.8; Size 0.3–2.5; Farthest depth 0.1–1; Far bias 0.3–3; Hold course 0.2–5; Separation 0–1000), then the species' own group(s) (Moth "Flight": Flutter, Glide, Flap rate; Rabbit "Hopping": Burst length, Pause length, Hop speed, Scare; Sea turtle "Swimming": Meander, Flipper beat and "Feeding": Food range; Squid "Swimming": Pulse rate, Pulse power, Pulse glow, Arm length; Owl "Flight": Hover time, Cruising, Swoop speed, Wingbeat; Flying fish "Leaping": How often, Leap length, Leap height; Eagle "Flight": Wingbeat, Glide, Folding flap toggle), then "Look" (Hue shift −180…180°, Shimmer, Sparkle, Distance fade, Trail 0–4, Trail fade 0.05–6, Grid 0–4, ASCII detail 0.5–2), then "Chat glass" (Blur 0–30 px default 3.5, Refraction 0–150 default 40 → the filter's displacement scale, Ripple 0.001–0.04 default .007 → turbulence baseFrequency "r r×1.5", Tint 0–3 default 0, Edge 0–2 default .55, Corner radius 0–48 default 24, Width 320–960 default 720 → the composer). Species that hide a control (Shimmer for Squid and Owl, Hold course for Flying fish) leave it out.
- Each row is a two-column grid: label and a Geist Mono 600 11px value (decimals from the step size), with the slider spanning beneath. Sliders: 18px tall, 4px track whose left part (up to the value, via a --fill percentage) is the accent colour and the rest --chip-edge; 14px white thumb with a faint border and shadow. Toggles: 30 × 18 px switch, accent when on, a 14px knob sliding 12px. Disabled rows fade to 40%.
- Hovering or focusing a row shows a tooltip to the left of the panel (max 240px, radius 12px, background #0e101aeb) with the hint text plus "Double-click the name to reset it." Double-clicking a label resets that value.
- Changes apply live. Detail triggers a resize; hue and grid repaint the cached background. Settings that differ from the species defaults are saved per species in localStorage under "wild-tab:tweaks:<species>" (tuning plus glass), and the open/closed state under "wild-tab:tweaks-open" (closed by default). Copy writes those changes as pretty JSON to the clipboard ("Copied", or "In console" if the clipboard is refused), reverting after 1.4 s. Reset asks "Reset all?" (red confirm styling) for 3 s and on a second click restores every default and clears storage. Another tab saving the same key reloads the page.
- Switching species rebuilds the flock with that species' defaults plus its saved tweaks, rebuilds the panel, clears the trail field and remembers the choice in localStorage "wild-tab:animal". A "?animal=<key>" URL parameter (moths, rabbits, turtles, squid, owls, flyingfish, eagles) picks the starting species, and "?count=N" fixes the number of animals.

## 10. Reduced motion and robustness

- Under prefers-reduced-motion the animation loop never starts: the flock is simulated silently for 4 s (240 steps) and one frame is drawn, re-drawn whenever a tweak changes, the window resizes or the preference flips; taps do nothing. Switching the preference off resumes animation.
- A ResizeObserver on the canvas re-sizes the grid and population; an IntersectionObserver pauses the loop when hidden. All localStorage access is wrapped in try/catch so the page works when storage is blocked.

## 11. Acceptance checklist

- One HTML file, no network requests beyond the embedded fonts, no console errors.
- At 1440×900: the species bar is centred at the top with Moth selected, the avatar, "Good … , Rosalie" and the 720px composer sit in the middle, Tweaks is top-right and the hint bottom-left; moths fill the grid flying toward the top-right.

- Clicking empty space scatters animals (moths kick away, rabbits bolt, owls swoop, squid jet, flying fish leap away, eagles are pushed), drops food for the sea turtles, and leaves a trail burst.
- On a 375px phone and a 320px phone all seven pills are visible on two rows, nothing overlaps, nothing scrolls sideways; Tweaks opens as a bottom sheet. On a landscape phone the avatar hides and everything fits. With reduced motion a single still frame shows.

# Recreate VEYRA — complete coding-agent prompt

You are an implementation agent with access to a terminal, filesystem and browser. Create and run the approved VEYRA automotive website in my local workspace. Complete the implementation and verification; do not stop at a plan.

## Objective and source of truth

Reproduce the finished interactive scene from this public release:

- Repository: https://github.com/amirmushichge/veyra-interactive-car
- Approved tag: `v1.0.0`
- Source ZIP: https://github.com/amirmushichge/veyra-interactive-car/archive/refs/tags/v1.0.0.zip
- Desktop reference: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amirmushichge/veyra-interactive-car/v1.0.0/docs/images/desktop.png
- Phone reference: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amirmushichge/veyra-interactive-car/v1.0.0/docs/images/mobile.png
- Asset base: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amirmushichge/veyra-interactive-car/v1.0.0/public/media/

The reference source, media and stylesheet are authoritative. This is a faithful reproduction task. Obtain the pinned release and reuse its implementation. Do not substitute a freshly invented landing page, a different car, a simulated video, a new UI system or newly generated imagery. Do not claim that a text-only generative reconstruction is identical to the reference.

If Git/network tools are unavailable, explain the precise blocker and ask me to provide the release ZIP. Do not make a visually unrelated placeholder and call the task complete.

## Bootstrap

1. Inspect the current directory. If it already contains this project, read its instructions and check the working tree before making changes. Preserve local work. If the directory contains a different project, create a clearly named child directory; do not overwrite it or reset its Git history.
2. In a clean workspace, clone the tag:

```sh
git clone --branch v1.0.0 https://github.com/amirmushichge/veyra-interactive-car.git
cd veyra-interactive-car
git switch -c my-veyra
```

3. Read `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/MEDIA.md` and `docs/VERIFICATION.md`. Inspect both reference screenshots.
4. Use Node.js 22 or later and pnpm 10.15.1. Install pnpm if needed with the environment's normal package-manager mechanism. Keep the release dependency versions and lockfile. Do not introduce new application libraries.
5. Run:

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm test
pnpm verify:reference
pnpm build
pnpm dev
```

6. Use http://127.0.0.1:5220/ as the local preview. If another process occupies it, identify the process and reuse it only if it serves this exact project. Do not kill unrelated processes. Use one deliberate alternate port only if necessary and report it clearly.

If adapting into another toolchain is explicitly required by my environment, first get the original Vite release running. Preserve the same React components, CSS, content and asset bytes; isolate framework plumbing from the reference behaviour. Report that the result is an adaptation if any reference files differ.

## Product and page

VEYRA is a fictional independent electric-vehicle design study. The page title is `VEYRA — Electric, inside out.` It is a single interactive scene with a lightweight header, title row, framed media, four hotspots, contextual menus, two technical detail views and a compact footer.

The header shows the `VEYRA` wordmark, `Electric vehicle design` on sufficiently wide screens, and `Independent concept`. The overview title is `Electric, inside out.` Supporting copy reads `Explore beneath the surface.` and `Select a point to begin.`

The footer has four aligned text groups: Electric drive, Battery architecture, Body finishes, Wheel designs. Preserve their exact text from App.tsx. A slim baseline shows `VEYRA — Design study` and the current scene's supporting sentence. Appearance menus temporarily replace the footer notes visually, leaving the car unobstructed.

Do not add buy buttons, prices, range estimates, performance specifications, brand claims, navigation sections, testimonials, cards or a contact form. Do not turn the page into a multi-screen marketing site. There is no runtime 3D model, no scroll-scrubbing timeline and no looping autoplay background.

## Visual contract

- Font: Space Grotesk, weight 400 only. Use the release font import. No synthetic bold.
- Primary colours: studio `#6b879d`, sky `#708fa2`, white `#ffffff`, muted text `#e1eaf0`, panel `#35586e`, electric green `#edff39`, dark accent text `#10190c`, thin white-alpha lines.
- The wordmark has restrained kerning. The title hierarchy comes from size and spacing, not heavier font weights.
- One shared image plane holds media and hotspots at a nominal 1672:941 ratio. Preserve the existing measurement formula and CSS variables.
- One white 3px outer frame encloses all media states; radius 16px on larger screens and 12px on phones. It must not alter media coordinates. No feather masks, background recolouring or duplicated blurred car silhouettes.
- Preserve the full visible car, both wheels, open hood and ground shadow.
- Hotspots are 48px interaction targets with compact electric-green discs, dark thin plus icons and restrained hover labels. Keep keyboard focus visible.
- Appearance panels use a consistent blue surface, 12px radius, thin border and readable labels. The panel stays outside the vehicle image, below the frame.
- Desktop header/title/media/footer align to the same measured width. At widths at most 900px, use the release stacked layout, 20px side margins and a two-column text footer.
- At desktop heights at most 780px, technical descriptions flow below the media. Do not shrink or move the image during entry/return to accommodate them.

Reuse `src/index.css` in full. These notes explain its intent; they do not replace the precise reference rules.

## Asset contract

Use the release's `public/media` directory with unchanged bytes. All assets are supplied. Keep filenames and nested paths case-exact.

Active exterior: `exterior-polished.png`.

Hover pairs:

- Drive: `hood-hover-forward.mp4`, `hood-hover-reverse.mp4`.
- Battery: `battery-hover-forward.mp4`, `battery-hover-reverse.mp4`.

Active technical images: `drive-blue.png`, `battery-blue.png`.

Paint: original exterior for Studio Silver; `config/electric-green.png`, `config/lime-green.png`, `config/sky-blue.png`, `config/graphite.png` for the remaining four choices.

Wheels: original exterior for Multi-spoke; `config/wheels-aero.png` for Aero Disc; `config/wheels-forged.png` for Sport Forged.

Keep earlier/dormant stills in the release too. `optics` and disabled detail-flight clip metadata in `content.ts` are not active features. Do not enable them or fabricate their missing videos.

Do not resize, recompress, retime, recolour or regenerate approved media. Do not send assets to an external generation provider during reproduction. Prefer local files served by Vite; do not leave playback dependent on temporary provider URLs.

## Interaction contract

There are exactly four overview points:

- Drive at x=25%, y=48%: hover/focus opens the hood; click enters the drive detail.
- Battery at x=64%, y=72%: hover/focus reveals the battery; click enters its detail.
- Paint at x=55%, y=51%: opens body-colour selection.
- Wheels at x=48%, y=71%: opens wheel selection.

Coordinates are image-relative. Do not position them against the whole screen.

### Hover playback

Retain `HoverVideo.tsx` exactly. It uses four off-DOM video elements and one canvas. Show frames only after decoding. Hold the last displayed frame at every handoff. Distinguish the currently settled pose from the latest desired hotspot.

Finish the active short forward clip before reversing. Finish its reverse before starting another system. Do not seek in the middle of independently retimed forward/reverse files to guess a matching pose. Rapid pointer changes update the desired target rather than starting overlapping playback.

On detail entry, freeze the currently visible hover frame until the opaque cutaway covers it. Reset only after that handoff. Preserve failure handling, the watchdog, cleanup and reduced-motion behaviour. Never introduce a black clearing frame.

### Detail navigation

Keep `overview → entering → detail → returning → overview` and the release's timing and guards. Do not trigger transitions while loading, already transitioning, or configuring appearance.

Drive and Battery each show their existing title, description, three component points/list entries and driver-oriented explanation. Click a point or list row to toggle its explanation. Keep the Back control and Escape return. Keep screen-reader status, focus handling and disabled states.

Click-to-detail is the approved CSS zoom/crossfade into a still image. Do not replace it with a new generated flight.

### Appearance

Only one mode is active at a time. On opening Paint or Wheels, stop requesting a hover pose and wait for the authored return to the neutral car. Show the selected appearance only when neutral and decoded. Do not place an appearance render over an open hood or X-ray frame.

Keep original hover/focus ownership, pointer corridor, pin-on-selection behaviour, leave timer, close timing and Escape. Disable unrelated points while the panel is active/closing. On close, restore the original car and unlock the other functions. Paint and wheel choices are independent render alternatives, not a combined configuration engine.

The menu must remain reachable from its point and must not cover the body or wheels. Preserve the desktop horizontal dock and phone-sized compact dock. Do not introduce an invisible full-page click blocker to keep it open.

## Verification

Treat the release source/media hashes as the reference test. If `pnpm verify:reference` fails during exact reproduction, identify why and restore the correct files. Do not regenerate the manifest just to pass.

Run existing unit checks and the production build. Inspect the actual browser, not just the source. At minimum check 1440x900, 1280x720 and 390x844; also check 1920x1080, 768x1024 and around 360px when the environment allows.

Exercise: default scene; every paint and wheel option; close and reopen; hood opening and return; battery reveal and return; rapid travel between system points; entry/return for both detail views; annotation toggles; Tab/Enter/Escape; pointer travel from hotspot to displaced menu; reduced motion. Verify no horizontal overflow, clipped primary controls, black endpoint, lost wheel, scale jump or video playing over an appearance selection.

Compare desktop and phone screenshots against the supplied references at matching viewport sizes. Allow normal browser/font rasterisation differences; do not claim pixel identity across every OS. Note any testing limits honestly, especially physical iOS/Safari and real touch devices.

Read known limitations before reporting a newly discovered regression. The reference contains an appearance-close focus race that can leave focus on the body; do not silently change behaviour in a reproduction task. Flag it and keep any future fix separately scoped.

## Optional LTX workflow

Do not use LTX to complete the reproduction. The files are already bundled. If I separately request new media, read `docs/LTX_API.md` and use https://console.ltx.io/api-keys for my own key. Never request that I paste the key into the conversation or expose it in a VITE_ variable.

Prepare a local dry run first. A paid submission needs my authorization for the specific cost and input upload. Keep outputs in `generated/`, preserve the saved job ID and resume interrupted polling instead of submitting twice. New generation cannot reproduce the approved image/video bytes deterministically.

## Finish

Return the working local preview URL, location of the project, release tag used, verification results and any real limitations. Keep the site running for review. Do not publish a website, push to my GitHub, create an account or incur generation charges unless I separately request that action. Preserve the repository license and attribution.

> .btn-primary {
>   position: relative;
>   overflow: hidden;
>   transition: transform 0.3s ease, box-shadow 0.3s ease;
> }
> .btn-primary::before {
>   content: '';
>   position: absolute;
>   inset: 0;
>   background: linear-gradient(120deg, transparent 0%, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05) 50%, transparent 100%);
>   transform: translateX(-100%);
>   transition: transform 0.5s ease;
> }
> .btn-primary:hover {
>   transform: translateY(-2px);
>   box-shadow: 0 6px 20px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.15);
> }
> .btn-primary:hover::before {
>   transform: translateX(100%);

> .btn-primary:active {
>   transform: translateY(0);
>   box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1);
> }
> ```
>
> **IntersectionObserver hook (`useInView`):**
> - Accepts a `threshold` parameter (default `0.15`), uses a ref.
> - Observes the element; once `isIntersecting` is true, sets `isVisible = true` and unobserves (one-shot animation).
> - Returns `{ ref, isVisible }`.
> - This section calls it with threshold `0.1`.

full_prompt:
# Kindred — Dot-Matrix Hands Hero (exact recreation prompt)

Build a single-file, full-viewport landing hero for **Kindred**, a community platform for creatives. The page is a calm off-white canvas with a centered headline, a black pill CTA with a rainbow underglow, and a row of partner logos at the bottom. Behind the copy, **two human hands reach toward each other (Creation-of-Adam style), drawn live in code as a black dot-matrix / LED halftone made of horizontal scanline rows of dots**. The hands slowly drift, roll and breathe, and each hand periodically **glitch-dissolves dot by dot into a second pose** and back. The background is rendered on a `<canvas>` every frame. It is not a video and not a GIF.

Plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JS in one file, with no frameworks. The only external resources are the Google Font and one Higgsfield image used as the luminance source for the halftone.

---

## 1. Assets (use exactly these URLs)

| Use | URL |
|---|---|
| Hand source sheet (2×2 black-and-white photo sheet of four isolated hands on pure white, 2688×1520 original, requested at w=1600 → 1600×905). Must be loaded with `crossOrigin="anonymous"` (the proxy sends `access-control-allow-origin: *`) so `getImageData` works. | `https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20261030_025250_100df7b8-31fd-4614-aa4a-c1b7d5b6b273.png&w=1600&q=85` |
| Font | `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500;600&display=swap` (with preconnect to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com crossorigin) |

Sheet layout (fractions of the sheet's width and height, `[x, y, w, h]`):
- `LA` = `[0, .06, .47, .40]`, top-left: left forearm entering from the left edge, palm down, index finger pointing right, other fingers loosely curled (Adam's hand).
- `RA` = `[.53, .06, .47, .40]`, top-right: right forearm entering from the right edge, index finger pointing left, fingers drooping (God's hand).
- `LB` = `[0, .55, .47, .40]`, bottom-left: the left hand open, fingers spread, palm down, reaching right.
- `RB` = `[.53, .55, .47, .40]`, bottom-right: the right hand open, palm turned up, fingers curved, reaching left.

Pose A = the pointing pair (LA + RA). Pose B = the open pair (LB + RB).

No other images. Logos are inline SVG.

---

## 2. Design tokens

```css
:root{--bg:#f7f7f5;--ink:#111111;--mute:#9a9a9a;--sub:#7b7b7b}
```
- Page background `#f7f7f5` (warm off-white). Dots are `#0d0d0d`.
- Font: **Inter** 400/500/600, `-webkit-font-smoothing:antialiased`, fallback `system-ui, sans-serif`.
- Global reset: `*{box-sizing:border-box;margin:0;padding:0}`. `html,body{height:100%}`.

---

## 3. Structure

```
section.hero (position:relative; height:100vh; min-height:660px; overflow:hidden)
  canvas#dots (absolute, inset:0, 100%×100%, display:block)
  nav
  div.copy
  div.logos
```
Everything except the canvas has `position:relative|absolute; z-index:3`.

### 3.1 Nav
- A flex row centered horizontally, `gap: clamp(18px, 2.6vw, 40px)`, `padding-top: 36px`, font-size 13.5px.
- **Brand:** an inline SVG mark (16×18, viewBox `0 0 16 18`, path `M2 0h4v18H2zM7 9c3-1 5-4 6-9h3c-1 5-3 8-6 9 3 1 5 4 6 9h-3c-1-5-3-8-6-9z`, a stylised "K" with a straight stem and two curved arms) plus "Kindred". Weight 600, 15px, letter-spacing −.01em, gap 8px, margin-right 10px.
- **Links:** Platform · Marketplace · Creators · Resources · Company. Colour `#3a3a3a`, no underline; hover `#000` (transition .2s).
- **Sign In pill:** background `#111`, white text, padding 10px 21px, radius 999px, weight 500, margin-left 10px. On hover it rises 1px (`translateY(-1px)`, .25s).

### 3.2 Copy block
- Absolute: `left:50%; top:24.5%; transform:translateX(-50%)`, centered text, `width:min(92vw,720px)`.
- `h1`: weight 500, letter-spacing −.035em, line-height 1.04, `font-size: clamp(38px, 3.75vw, 68px)`.
  - Line 1, "Reconnecting", is a block span in grey `#9a9a9a`.
  - Line 2, "Human Creativity.", is ink `#111`.
- Subline `p`: "We’re not building another platform. We’re building a place where people belong." Margin-top 20px, auto sides, `max-width:340px`, colour `#7b7b7b`, `font-size:clamp(13px,1.02vw,15.5px)`, line-height 1.4. It wraps to two centered lines.
- CTA wrapper `.cta`: inline-block, relative, `margin-top: clamp(34px, 3.6vw, 52px)`.
  - The anchor "Join the circle" is a black `#111` pill with white 13.5px weight-500 text, padding 11px 20px, radius 999px.
  - **Rainbow underglow:** a `::before` element, absolute, `left:10%; right:10%; bottom:-6px; height:16px; border-radius:50%`, with background `linear-gradient(90deg,#ffcf5a,#7dffa8,#5ad7ff,#9b7bff,#ff6fd8,#ffb36b)`, `filter: blur(9px)`, opacity .85. It sits behind the pill and peeks out below it as a soft spectrum glow.
  - Hover: the glow goes to opacity 1, `blur(12px)` and `bottom:-9px`. The pill rises 1px. All transitions .3s.

### 3.3 Partner logos
- Absolute, `bottom: clamp(28px, 6vh, 64px)`, full width, flex centered, `gap: clamp(26px, 4.6vw, 66px)`, wraps, padding 0 16px.

- The six logos, all fictional:
  1. **Lumenix**, leaf: `M3 15c0-7 5-12 14-12-1 9-6 14-13 13l-1 2-2-1z`
  2. **Velora**, hexagon ring: `M10 1l8 4.5v9L10 19l-8-4.5v-9zM10 6l-4 2.3v4.4L10 15l4-2.3V8.3z`
  3. **Nimbus**, double wave: `M1 5q4.5-3 9 0t9 0v3q-4.5 3-9 0t-9 0zm0 7q4.5-3 9 0t9 0v3q-4.5 3-9 0t-9 0z`
  4. **Quanta**, concentric rings: `M10 1a9 9 0 110 18 9 9 0 010-18zm0 3a6 6 0 100 12 6 6 0 000-12zm0 3a3 3 0 110 6 3 3 0 010-6z`
  5. **Solstice**, two peaks: `M1 17L7 6l3 5 3-7 6 13z`
  6. **Parallax**, stacked layers: `M10 1l9 4-9 4-9-4zm-9 8l9 4 9-4v3l-9 4-9-4zm0 5l9 4 9-4v2l-9 4-9-4z`
- All SVG viewBoxes are `0 0 20 20`.

---

## 4. The dot-matrix hands (canvas, the core of the design)

### 4.1 Pipeline per frame
1. Load the sheet once. Slice it into **four pre-downscaled tiles**, one 420px-wide canvas per `SRC` rect (height from aspect), drawn with `imageSmoothingQuality='high'`.
2. Keep two tiny offscreen "field" canvases, `fA` and `fB` (`willReadFrequently:true`). Each is sized **cols × rows**, so each pixel equals one dot.
3. Every frame, fill both fields white. Draw pose-A tiles (LA, RA) into `fA` and pose-B tiles (LB, RB) into `fB`, each with its hand's current transform (4.3). Read both with `getImageData`.
4. Clear the visible canvas. For each grid cell, pick a field (4.4), turn its luminance into a quantised dot size, and draw a filled circle in `#0d0d0d`.

### 4.2 Grid
- `DPR = min(2, devicePixelRatio)`. The canvas backing size is W·DPR × H·DPR. Draw with `setTransform(DPR,0,0,DPR,0,0)`.
- Horizontal pitch `step = max(5, W/205)` (≈7px at 1440 wide).
- Row pitch `rowStep = step × 2.05`. The rows read as LED scanlines, with dots nearly touching along a row and clear gaps between rows.
- `cols = ceil(W/step)`, `rows = ceil(H/rowStep)`. The dot centre is `((i+.5)·step, (j+.5)·rowStep)`.
- Base radius `R = step × .46`.
- Per-cell dissolve seed: `seed = .55·hash(i,j) + .45·hash(j·3.1, 7.7)`. It is mostly random per dot, with a per-row bias so dissolves streak along rows. Here `hash(a,b) = fract(sin(a·127.1 + b·311.7)·43758.5453)`.
- Recompute everything on resize.

### 4.3 Hand placement and drift
- `LOOP = 20` seconds. `a = 2π·t/LOOP`. Phase `ph = 0` for the left hand and `π` for the right, so they move in counter-phase.
- Block size: `hw = W·.53` (portrait `W·.66`). `hh = hw · (.40·1520)/(.47·2688)`, which keeps the sheet aspect.
- Vertical centre: `cy = H·.54` (portrait `H·.66`).
- Base x position:
  - Left: `x = reach − W·.045`.
  - Right: `x = W − hw + W·.045 − reach`.
  - The forearms run past the screen edges.
- Motion:
  - `reach = (.035·sin(a+ph) + .012·sin(2a+1.3+ph))·W`: the hands slowly reach in and pull back.
  - `scale = 1 + .07·sin(a+.9+ph)`: they breathe toward and away from the viewer.
  - `rot = (left ? 1 : −1) · .045·sin(a+2.1+ph)` radians: a gentle roll.
- Transform order when drawing into the field: scale to field space `(cols/W, rows/H)`; translate to the pivot (left edge or right edge, `cy`); rotate; scale; translate back. Then `drawImage(tile, x, cy−hh/2, hw, hh)`.

### 4.4 Pose switches (glitch dissolve)
- `smooth(a,b,x)` is a clamped smoothstep. `mixAt(t,on,off,dur) = smooth(on,on+dur,t) · (1 − smooth(off,off+dur,t))`.
- Left half (`i < cols/2`): `mL = mixAt(t, 6.2, 14.6, 1.6)`. Right half: `mR = mixAt(t, 2.4, 10.4, 1.6)`.
  - The right hand opens at 2.4s and returns at 10.4s. The left opens at 6.2s and returns at 14.6s.
  - Both are back in pose A before the 20s loop restarts, so the loop is seamless.
- Per dot: `useB = seed < m`, and sample `fB` if true, otherwise `fA`. Dots switch in a scattered, row-streaked order.
- While a switch is in progress (`0.001 < m < 0.999`), any dot with `|seed − m| < .12` sits on the "front". Its value is multiplied by `|seed−m|/.12`, and also by `.3` when `hash(i+tick, j) ≤ .4`. The front flickers, thins and sparkles as it sweeps.

### 4.5 Luminance → dot
- `lum = red/255` of the chosen field pixel.
- `v = clamp((1 − lum − .16)/.42, 0, 1)`. White background gives no dot. Mid-grey skin gives big dots. Highlights give small dots, which produces visible shading inside the hands.
- Shimmer: `v *= .86 + .14·sin(t·3.2 + seed·40)`.
- Centre fade: with `cx = |(i+.5)/cols − .5|`, apply `v *= smooth(.035, .11, cx)`. The fingertips dissolve just before the CTA and never touch.
- Copy quiet zone: with `ex = cx/.2` (portrait `.44`) and `ey = ((j+.5)·rowStep/H − .385)/.085` (portrait centre `.33`), apply `v *= smooth(.85, 1.25, hypot(ex,ey))`. No dots cross the headline subline.
- **Quantise** to `LEVELS = [0, .26, .52, .78, 1]`: take the highest level with `v ≥ level − .13`. Level 0 draws nothing.
- Radius = `R × level`, except the lowest level, which uses `R × .38`. That gives the tiny "····" pinpoints in light areas. The result reads as a crisp LED halftone with five sizes, not a smooth gradient.

### 4.6 Row glitch
- `tick = floor(t·7)`, so the pattern changes 7 times a second.
- For each row, if `hash(j, tick) > .965`, the whole row slides by `round((hash(tick, j) − .5)·8)` columns. The sample index is `clamp(i − shift)`.
- A few random rows jump sideways for a beat, like a misaligned LED display.

### 4.7 Loop
- `requestAnimationFrame` calls `render((now − t0)/1000)`. `render` wraps `t` into `[0, LOOP)`.
- Expose `window.__render = render` so a deterministic recorder can drive time.

---

## 5. Responsive (≤760px)
- Nav: hide every link except Sign In. Use `justify-content:space-between` with padding `22px 18px 0`.
- Copy `top:20%`.
- Logos wrap onto two rows with `gap:14px 24px` and font-size 13px.
- On a portrait viewport (H > W), the hand band sits lower at `cy = .66H`, the hands are wider (`.66W`), and the quiet zone moves to `.33H` with width `.44`. The hands sit under the CTA.

## 6. Feel
Quiet, editorial and human. The hero should look like a monochrome LED wall showing two reaching hands. Motion is slow and continuous: drift, breathe, roll, shimmer. Every few seconds one hand crackles apart dot by dot and re-forms in a new pose. Keep everything black on warm off-white. The only colour is the soft rainbow glow under the CTA.

full_prompt:
# Prompt: Verra Events hero

Build a single-file **community-platform hero** for a fictional creator platform, **Verra**, in plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JS with no framework, no build step and no media files. A black page holds a rounded dark frame. Inside it, a huge glowing vortex ring of fine red, pink and orange fins is drawn live on a canvas, cropped by the top of the frame. Below it sit a giant gradient word with a typing caret, a two-line subline and a white button. The ring turns slowly and the word types itself through a short list.

## Frame and scale

- **Page:** `#000`. The frame is inset 5vw left and right and 7.2vh top and bottom, with radius 14u, a 1px border at white 9%, and overflow hidden.
- **Unit:** `u = min(frameWidth / 1052, frameHeight / 754)`, written to `--u`. On phones (under 768px) `u = frameWidth / 600` and the frame is inset 10px.
- **Font:** Inter (variable, 400 to 600), self-hosted latin woff2.

## Nav (24u from the top, 26u and 24u side insets)

- **Left:** a small two-chevron logo (an outlined diamond over an open V, 1.7px white stroke) and "Verra" at 17.5u, weight 500.
- **Right:**
  - a frosted pill (29u tall, radius 8u, background `rgba(150,150,150,.38)`, 14px blur) holding "Explore", "Circles" and "People" at 14u;
  - a 4u gap;
  - a white "Connect" button (29u, radius 8u, dark text, weight 500) that lifts 1px on hover.
- **Phones:** the pill hides.

## The ring (canvas, redrawn every frame)

- **Geometry:**
  - centre (frameWidth/2 + 34u, −212u), so it sits above the frame and only the lower arc shows;
  - inner radius 435u, outer radius 652u;
  - vertical scale 1.03 (plus up to ±3.5% from pointer tilt).
- **Strands:** 196 of them, each sampled at 41 points from the inner rim to the outer rim, with q = 0 → 1 and r = ri + (ro − ri)·q.
  - **Angle:** θ = uᵢ + k·(1 − q)^4.2 + 0.05·k·q² + 0.02·sin(πq)·sin(3uᵢ + 0.4t), where uᵢ = 2πi/196 + spin.
  - **Result:** each strand curls tangentially along the inner rim and then runs almost radially to the outer rim, like a turbine fin.
  - **Motion:** spin = 0.06·t rad/s (a seamless rotation), and k = 0.42·(1 + 0.12·sin 0.55t) gently breathes the curl.
- **Fins:**
  - Each strand is a filled ribbon around its centreline. Its half-width is (0.15 + 3.3·s·(1 − 0.25q))·u, where s is a smoothstep of q over 0 to 0.28, so it tapers to nothing at the inner rim.
  - Draw them in angular order starting at the top of the ring (which is off-screen), so the overlap never shows a seam. Each body is opaque (`source-over`), then its leading edge, offset by the half-width, is stroked 1.45u wide in `lighter` mode. The next body covers part of that edge, which gives the layered-fin depth.
- **Colour (radial gradients from ri to ro, so colour follows radius):**
  - body: `#b01e50` → `#9c1236` (12%) → `#860c18` (40%) → `#9c1a0a` (70%) → `#c63c0e` (90%) → `#e85a18`.
  - edge: pink `rgba(255,130,185,.85)` → `rgba(255,84,138,.95)` (8%) → `rgba(255,56,80,.95)` (28%) → `rgba(255,58,44,.95)` (55%) → `rgba(255,92,36)` (80%) → `rgba(255,122,44)` (94%) → `rgba(255,150,70)`.
- **Light:**
  - a deep-red ambient fill in the annulus (`rgba(170,14,50,.35)` → `rgba(120,8,14,.45)` → `rgba(170,40,6,.4)`);
  - an orange halo from ro − 16u to ro + 70u (peak 0.42);
  - a faint pink inner halo (0.09);
  - a thin orange outer-rim line (1.6u).
- **Bloom:** draw every edge again on an offscreen canvas at 0.32× size (5.3u wide, alpha 0.7), plus a 9u orange outer-rim ring and a 5u pink inner-rim ring. Composite it onto the main canvas in `lighter` mode with an 8u blur.
- **Performance:** device pixel ratio is capped at 2. The loop pauses while the tab is hidden. Reduced motion draws one still frame.
- **Pointer:** the ring centre eases up to 14u × 10u toward the pointer (lerp 0.05).

## Headline group (cap top about 447u from the frame top, centred)

- **Word:** at 176u, weight 600, tracking −0.03em, filled with `linear-gradient(12deg, #fffaf6 28%, #ffe6d6 46%, #ffbc98 66%, #ff8f62 88%, #ff7a4c)`. The result is white at the lower left and peach-orange at the top right.
- **Caret:** a 1.6u × 124u bar in `#ffb48c`, 7u to the right of the word.
- **Typewriter:**
  - The words are Events, then Circles, then Creators, looping.
  - Each word holds for 2.6s with the caret blinking every 0.55s. It deletes at 70ms per letter, pauses 0.25s empty, types the next word at 100ms per letter, then pauses 0.15s.
  - Everything is a pure function of time.
- **Subline:** "Verra provides a space for creators to build / communities from zero to millions.", 26u below the word, 18u on a 24u line, white at 92%.
- **Button:** "Get started now", 19u below the subline. It's white, 41u tall with 17u side padding, radius 10u, 15u text at weight 500. On hover it lifts 2px and gains a soft orange glow.
- **Phones:**
  - the word is min(176u, 22vw);
  - the subline is 15px on a 21px line;
  - the whole ring and text block is centred vertically by shifting both the ring centre and the text down by half the leftover height.

## Timing and recording

- **Clock:** the ring and the typewriter read one clock, `performance.now()`.
- **`?rec=1`:** time comes instead from a paused Web Animation, a 100s linear `translateX(0 → 100000px)` on a hidden 1px element. A frame-by-frame recorder can seek it to get exact frames.

## Acceptance check (1440×960)

- **Look:** a crisp, glowing red-pink-orange fin vortex arcs across the top with a pure-black hole.
- **Text:** "Events" sits under the arc in a cream-to-orange gradient with a blinking caret.
- **Motion:** the ring turns slowly and seamlessly. After about 2.6s the word deletes and types "Circles".
- **Performance:** 60fps on a laptop.
- **Content:** no real brands or logos.

# Prompt: Reelmark hero

Build a single-file, one-screen **landing hero for a short-form video creator marketplace**, **Reelmark** ("Captivate Crowds with Snackable Reels"). Use plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JS, with no framework and no build step. The look is soft mint studio: a warm off-white page `#F5F8EF`, deep forest-green accents `#08482D`, a mint badge `#DAE7C7`, a big bold black headline, and an arched row of seven tall video cards playing bright sage-green product clips, with hand-drawn green notes and arrows.

## Frame

- **Frame:** one **1440×1080** frame, contained and centred: `--u = min(100vw/1440, 100vh/1080)`. Every element is placed in frame units.

## Type

- **Headline:** **Inter Tight 700**, 88u on a 92u line, tracking −0.035em (−0.022em on line 2), ink `#101410`.
- **UI:** **Inter** 400/500. The subline is `#5E5E61`.
- **Notes:** **Caveat 600** for the hand-drawn notes, in forest green.

## Layout (1440×1080)

- **Top bar:**
  - **Logo:** a green leaf mark with "Reelmark", at (37, 36).
  - **Nav:** Brands · Creators · Pricing · Use Cases · Contact, Inter 16.4u, starting at x = 505 with a 31u gap.
  - **Buttons:** a white "Log in" pill, 92×40 at (1211, 29), and a forest-green "Sign up" pill, 97×40 at (1304, 29).
- **Badge:** a mint pill, 292×37 at (575, 115): "Trusted by 120,000+ indie makers", Inter 500 16.6u in green.
- **Headline:** centred, top 176: **"Captivate Crowds / with Snackable Reels"**.
- **Subline:** centred, top 394, 20.8u / 32u, three lines: "Grow your brand with short, snappy product clips by / our handpicked video makers. Our crew is ready to / lift your next launch higher."
- **Notes:**
  - a "//" doodle at (263, 377)
  - a handwritten "Be seen / with clips" rotated 16° at (1212, 310), with a long curving arrow down to the cards
  - "Zero cost" rotated 24° at (521, 937), with a small arrow pointing to the button
  - the doodle strokes draw themselves in
  - the "Be seen" arrow starts **below** the note (it never crosses the words) and curls down to the cards
- **Card row: a curved video carousel.** Ten tall cards scroll continuously **right → left** (about 50u per second, looping seamlessly). The row is draggable with the pointer or touch: it follows the drag 1:1, coasts with momentum after release (velocity decays about 95% per second), then the slow auto-scroll carries on. The cursor is grab / grabbing.
  - **Curve:** each card's geometry comes from its x position relative to the centre, like the inside of a cylinder.
    - Normalised distance d = |x − 720| / 706.
    - Width = (170 + 48·d²)u. Cards sit on an even 196u pitch, then each centre is pushed outward: x = 720 + t·(1 + 0.083·(t/706)²), where t is the unpushed offset from the centre. This keeps about a 26u gap even at the edges.
    - Each vertical edge's height = (280 + 92·q^2.6)u, where q is that edge's own normalised distance.
    - The vertical centre sits at (687 − 12·d²)u.
  - **Result:** centre cards are upright 170×280 rectangles, and cards near the screen edges grow to about 370u tall with their outer edge taller than the inner edge.
  - **Drawing:** each card is a rounded quad (`clip-path: path()`, 15u corners) recomputed every frame.
  - **Details:** no drop shadow, a small frosted round play icon at each card's bottom-left, and cards clipped by the frame edges.
- **Button:** a forest-green "Make a Reel" pill (172×58) inside a dashed green outline ring (190×74) at (626, 901).

## Card media (one video for all ten)

- **Grid:** all card clips live in ONE 16:9 **5×2 grid** (10 tiles of 384×540, edge to edge):
  - **Still poster:** `https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/b7ebb74a-8c8a-4f7e-8f80-55e2d74ecd05.webp`
  - **Loop:** `https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/04fd3d5f-99d7-476e-98a4-46c08518ffb3.mp4` (1280×720, 5s, muted, loops)
- **Tiles** (row-major) are the sneaker, skincare splash, latte pour, headphones, plant shop, florist bouquet, pottery wheel, serum splash, latte top-down and headphones on a stand. Each tile animates on its own.
- **Each card:** shows its own tile, cover-fitted. Inside the clipped card, place a `<video>` and a poster layer sized 5 × tile width by 2 × tile height, offset to that tile, where the tile height is max(card height, card width / 0.7111).
- **Sync:** every card uses the same src, so it downloads once. Keep all ten on the same timestamp, and fade each in when its first frame is ready.
- **Clock:** drive the carousel from a long-running Web Animations clock (`document.documentElement.animate(…, {duration: 1e9})`) so the scroll is time-based.

## Motion (UI)

- **Entrance:** a one-time Web Animations sequence.
  - The nav drops in, the badge pops, each headline line rises out of a blur, then the subline.
  - The card row rises in, the button scales in, the doodle strokes draw, and the notes fade in.
- **Reduced motion:** no entrance and no video.

## Phones (≤ 820px)

- **Top:** the logo and a Sign up pill.
- **Copy:** stacked and centred: the badge, the headline (clamp 38–56px) and the subline.
- **Cards:** the same auto-scrolling, draggable curved carousel, scaled to the screen width (640-unit scale), in a 250px-tall band.
- **Bottom:** the button and the "Zero cost" note.

## Acceptance check (1440×1080)

- The headline sits centred above the arched card row, matching the coordinates above.
- The card row keeps drifting left and can be flung by dragging.
- Each card plays a different clip in motion, and the edge cards are taller and lean like the inside of a cylinder.
- **Content:** no real brand logos.

# HERO PROMPT — "olla" Stack-smart Kitchenware Landing Page (Balloon-Drop Grill)

> Exact recreation brief. Build a **single self-contained HTML file** (inline `<style>` and inline `<script>`, no frameworks, no build step, no libraries) that reproduces the page described below pixel-for-pixel and frame-for-frame. Every number in this document is load-bearing. Where a value is given in `vw`, `vh`, `%` or `px`, use exactly that unit. Where an easing curve, duration or delay is given, use exactly that. Every copy string is quoted verbatim — do not rephrase, re-capitalise or add punctuation.

---

## 0. Concept in one paragraph

A minimal, warm-beige kitchenware landing page for a brand called **olla**. At the top: a fixed white rounded navigation bar with a "Shop" mega-menu that wipes open downward into a strip of five line-icons. Below it, a hero made of two rounded panels side by side: a wide **night-sky panel** (deep navy sky, lilac clouds) on the left, and a narrow **yellow product card** on the right that plays a looping video of cookware nesting into itself. In the sky panel, a **folding grill pan hangs from a bunch of seven yellow balloons**, gently bobbing. A giant white word "olla" sits at the bottom-left of the sky panel. When the user scrolls, the balloons let go and float up out of the panel, and the grill **falls under gravity** — opening into a V shape and folding shut again as it falls — drifts sideways, shrinks, **passes behind the beige gutter between the sky panel and the kitchen panel below**, and **lands exactly in an empty gap on a kitchen counter** in a photographic kitchen section. When it lands, a centred headline fades up over the kitchen photo.

---

## 1. Document setup

- Fonts: preconnect to `https://fonts.googleapis.com` and `https://fonts.gstatic.com` (the latter with `crossorigin`), then load **Jost** from Google Fonts with weights **400, 500, 600** and `display=swap` (stylesheet URL: `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Jost:wght@400;500;600&display=swap`).
- Font stack for `body`: `"Jost", "Futura", "Century Gothic", Arial, sans-serif`. Enable `-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased`.
- Global reset: every element `box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0; padding: 0`.
- `html` background = page beige **#e9e7df**. `body` has `overflow-x: hidden`.
- Links and buttons: inherit font and colour, no background, no border, pointer cursor, no text-decoration.

**Colour sampling (makes the card seamless with the video):** once the pots video fires `loadeddata` (listen once), draw the video's **top-left region of 12 % width × 12 % height** (source rect x 0, y 0, w = videoWidth·0.12, h = videoHeight·0.12) into an **8 × 8** offscreen canvas, read all 64 pixels, average R, G and B separately (integer-truncate each), and set the card's inline `background` to `rgb(R, G, B)`. Wrap in try/catch so a CORS failure silently keeps #f7d23a. The intent: the clip's flat yellow backdrop and the card colour become identical, so the feathered video edge is invisible.

**Contents (top → bottom):**

1. **"NEW" pill** `span.new`: `display: inline-grid; place-items: center`, `height: 3vh`, `min-height: 22px`, horizontal padding **1.25vw**, `border-radius: 30px`, white background, `font-size: clamp(9px, 0.66vw, 12px)`, weight **600**, `letter-spacing: .02em`. Text: **NEW**.
2. **Paragraph** `p`: `margin-top: 2.1vh`, `font-size: clamp(12px, 0.92vw, 16px)`, `line-height: 1.55`, weight **500**. Text with two hard line breaks: **Say hello to simplicity.** / **Introducing Stack-smart™** / **kitchenware.** — the ™ is a `<sup>` at `.6em` with `vertical-align: top`.
3. **Pots video** `video#pots`: attributes `muted loop playsinline autoplay crossorigin="anonymous"`; `src` set from JS to `POTS_CLIP`, then `.play()` called (swallow the rejection).
   - Absolute, `left: 50%`, `top: 52%`, `width: 118%` of the card, `aspect-ratio: 1`, `transform: translate(-50%, -50%)`, `object-fit: cover`, `pointer-events: none`. It is wider than the card, so it bleeds off both sides and is cropped by the card's overflow.
   - **Radial feather mask** (both `-webkit-mask` and `mask`): `radial-gradient(closest-side, #000 72%, transparent 99%)` — fully opaque inside 72 % of the closest-side radius, fading to transparent by 99 %. Combined with the sampled background colour, the video has no visible edge.
   - The video sits in normal stacking order (no z-index), painted above the pill/paragraph only where they overlap — in practice it sits in the middle of the card under the text block.
4. **Shop button** `a.shop`: absolute, `left: 1.4vw; right: 1.4vw; bottom: 2.4vh`, `height: 4.3vh`, `min-height: 32px`, `border-radius: 40px` (full pill), white background, `display: grid; place-items: center`, `font-size: clamp(11px, 0.84vw, 15px)`, weight **600**. Text: **Shop Stack-smart™** (literal ™ glyph). Hover: background `--navy` (#141a4a), text white; transition `background .3s, color .3s`.

---

## 7. Kitchen panel (`#kitchen`)

- `position: relative`, `width: 87vw`, `height: 89.3vh`, `margin: 1.19vw auto 0` (the same gutter as between the hero panels), `border-radius: 14px`, **`overflow: hidden`**.
- Background colour `#efe9de` fallback + `KITCHEN` image, `center / cover`, no-repeat.
- Contains `canvas.grill#gK` (grill copy #2) and the headline block.

### 7.1 Headline block `#ktext`

- Absolute; its `left`/`top` are **set by JS in pixels** to the cover-fitted image point (0.496, 0.125) (see §10), with initial CSS fallback `left: 50%; top: 13%`.
- `transform: translate(-50%, -50%)` (centred on that point), `text-align: center`, colour **#1b1b1b**, `z-index: 4`, `white-space: nowrap`.
- **h2**: text **Cooks for your family. Fits your space.** — `font-size: var(--kh, 22px)`, weight **600**, `letter-spacing: -0.01em`, `line-height: 1.2`.
- **p**: text with one hard line break **A stack-smart kitchenware system designed** / **to save up to 50% more cupboard space.** — `margin-top: .45em`, `font-size: var(--kp, 15px)`, `line-height: 1.38`, weight **450** (requested even though only 400/500/600 load; the browser will synthesise/round it).
- `--kh` and `--kp` are set by JS on `#kitchen` to **2.85 %** and **2.05 %** of the **displayed image height** (KITCHEN intrinsic height 1520 × cover scale), formatted to 1 decimal place + "px". This keeps the type locked to the photo's scale at every viewport.

### 7.2 Landing fade

- Both children (`h2` and `p`) start at `opacity: 0; transform: translateY(14px)`, with `transition: opacity .7s var(--ease), transform .7s var(--ease)`. The `p` has `transition-delay: .12s`.
- When `<body>` has class `landed`, both go to `opacity: 1; transform: none`. Removing the class reverses the fade (it is toggled continuously; see §11).

### 7.3 Footer spacer

`div#foot` with `height: 9.3vh` after the kitchen panel — this is what allows the page to scroll far enough for the kitchen panel's top to reach 9.3vh from the viewport top (directly under the nav).

---

## 8. The grill technique (green-screen clip → keyed frame cache → scroll scrub)

The grill is **not** a playing video. It is a set of pre-keyed frames scrubbed by scroll.

### 8.1 Two canvases

- Both canvases have class `.grill`: `position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; z-index: 2; pointer-events: none; will-change: transform`.
- `#gS` lives inside `#sky`; `#gK` lives inside `#kitchen`. Both always show the same frame at the same document-space position, size and rotation (§12 explains why).

### 8.2 Frame caching

- Constants: **NF = 48** frames, **FS = 560** px square cache canvases.
- Create an offscreen `<video>`: `crossOrigin = "anonymous"`, `muted = true`, `playsInline = true`, `preload = "auto"`, `src = GRILL_CLIP`. Wait for `loadeddata` (reject on `error`; the whole cache routine's failure is silently caught).
- Let `dur = video.duration − 0.05` (avoid seeking past the last decodable frame).
- For i = 0 … 47 sequentially: set `currentTime = dur · i / 47`, await the `seeked` event, then create a 560 × 560 canvas (2D context with `willReadFrequently: true`), draw the video scaled into the full 560 × 560, apply the chroma key (§8.3) in place, and push the canvas into the frames array.
- As soon as frame 0 is cached, set a `ready` flag and force a redraw, so the grill appears immediately while the remaining frames continue to cache.

### 8.3 Chroma key (per pixel, on the 560 × 560 canvas)

For each pixel with channels r, g, b:

1. m = max(r, b)
2. k = g − m (how much "greener than anything else" the pixel is)
3. If **k > 18**:
   - alpha = max(0, 1 − (k − 18) / 52) → written as alpha·255 (integer-truncated). So k = 18 is fully opaque, k ≥ 70 is fully transparent, linear in between (threshold **18**, soft range **52**).
   - **Despill**: g = min(g, m + 6) — clamps green to at most 6 above the larger of red/blue, removing the green fringe on edges.
4. Otherwise leave the pixel untouched (alpha stays 255).

Write the image data back with `putImageData`.

### 8.4 Drawing a frame

- Frame index f (see §11.4) is computed each animation frame; only when f changes (or on a forced redraw) do both canvases get cleared and redrawn: `clearRect` the full backing store, then `drawImage(frames[f], 0, 0, canvasWidth, canvasHeight)` (scale the 560 cache to the canvas backing size). If f exceeds the number of frames cached so far, use the last cached one.
- Before `ready`, f = 0 and nothing is drawn (empty canvas).

### 8.5 Canvas sizing

- m = ceil( max(c0, c1) · 1.05 ) CSS px, where c0 and c1 are the start and end grill sizes (§9, §10). Both canvases: CSS width/height = m px; backing store = m · dpr square, with **dpr = min(devicePixelRatio, 2)**.
- The visible size is then controlled purely by a CSS `scale(size / m)` in the transform (§11.5), so the canvas never needs to be resized during scroll.

---

## 9. Geometry: sky panel start state and balloons

All geometry is computed in **document coordinates** (bounding client rect + `scrollY`) in a `measure()` function, run on load, after `document.fonts.ready`, and on every `resize`.

- S = sky panel rect: S.x = left, S.y = top + scrollY, S.w, S.h.
- K = kitchen panel rect, same way.

**Grill start (hanging in the sky):**
- Centre x0 = S.x + **0.81 · S.w**; centre y0 = S.y + **0.525 · S.h** (81 % across, 52.5 % down the sky panel — right of centre, in the lower half, clear of the tagline).
- Frame size c0 = **0.425 · S.h** (the square frame is 42.5 % of the panel height).

**Balloons (strings meet the grill handle):**
- Width bw = **0.30 · S.w**; height bh = bw · 2048 / 1360.
- Handle point in the panel's local coordinates: x = 0.81 · S.w, y = 0.525 · S.h − c0/2 + **0.075 · c0** (top of the frame plus 7.5 % of the frame).
- Balloon element `left` = 0.81 · S.w − bw · **0.494**; `top` = (0.525 · S.h − c0/2 + c0 · 0.075) − bh · **0.946**. That places the image's string-meeting point (49.4 %, 94.6 %) exactly on the handle.

---

## 10. Geometry: kitchen cover-fit mapping and landing target

The kitchen photo is `background-size: cover` and centred, so image-relative coordinates must be mapped through the fit:

- Intrinsic KI = 2688 × 1520.
- sc = max(K.w / 2688, K.h / 1520) (cover scale).
- ox = (K.w − 2688 · sc) / 2; oy = (K.h − 1520 · sc) / 2 (negative overflow offsets, centred).
- Image point (nx, ny) in 0…1 → document px: ( K.x + ox + nx · 2688 · sc , K.y + oy + ny · 1520 · sc ).
- Displayed image height H = 1520 · sc.

**Landing gap** (empty spot on the counter) = image point **(0.489, 0.641)** → (gx, gy).

**End size**: c1 = H · **0.2 / 0.83** — the grill body (≈ 83 % of its square frame) ends up 20 % of the displayed image height, matching the scale of the neighbouring air fryer.

**End centre**: x1 = gx; y1 = gy − c1 · **0.91** + c1 / 2 — i.e. the frame is positioned so that the point at **91 % down the frame** (the bottom of the grill body / its feet) rests exactly on the gap point on the counter.

**Headline**: image point **(0.496, 0.125)** → set `#ktext` left/top to that point minus K.x / K.y (panel-local px). Set `--kh` = H · 0.0285 px and `--kp` = H · 0.0205 px on `#kitchen` (1 decimal).

**Scroll end** (progress = 1): end = max(200, K.y − 0.093 · innerHeight) — the scroll position at which the kitchen panel's top sits 9.3 % of the viewport height from the top, directly under the nav, mirroring the hero panel's offset.

After measuring, resize both canvases (§8.5) and force a redraw.

---

## 11. Scroll choreography (runs every requestAnimationFrame)

### 11.1 Progress and smoothing

- Every frame: target = scrollY / end. Smoothed progress sp += (target − sp) · **0.18**. If |target − sp| < 0.0005, snap sp = target.
- p = clamp(sp, 0, 1) (clamp = min/max to [0, 1]).
- The loop starts after `document.fonts.ready` resolves (measure first, then begin rAF). Also call measure once immediately at script end.

### 11.2 Fall parameter and curves

- q = clamp( (p − 0.02) / 0.9 ) — nothing moves for the first 2 % of progress; the fall completes at p = 0.92.
- **Vertical** uses gravity-like acceleration: fall = q^**1.75**.
- **Horizontal drift** and **size** use smoothstep: s(q) = q² · (3 − 2q).

### 11.3 Idle motion (while hanging)

Let t = performance.now() / 1000 (seconds), idle = 1 − clamp(p · 12) — full at p = 0, faded to 0 by p = 1/12.
- **Bob** = idle · sin(1.9 · t) · **6 px** (±6 px vertical, 1.9 rad/s).
- **Sway** = idle · sin(1.3 · t) · **1.4°** (±1.4°, 1.3 rad/s).

### 11.4 Grill position, size, tilt, frame

- x = x0 + (x1 − x0) · s(q)
- y = y0 + (y1 − y0) · q^1.75 + bob
- size = c0 + (c1 − c0) · s(q)
- tilt (degrees) = sin(q · π) · **−9** + sway — tilts up to 9° counter-clockwise mid-fall and returns to level on landing.
- Frame index f = round( clamp( (q − 0.12) / 0.72 ) · 47 ), also clamped to [0, cachedFrames − 1]; 0 when not ready. The grill stays closed for the first 12 % of the fall, opens into its V around the middle, and is fully closed again by q = 0.84 — it lands closed.

### 11.5 Applying to the two canvases

With scl = size / m:
- `#gS` transform: translate( x − S.x − m/2 px, y − S.y − m/2 px ) rotate( tilt deg ) scale( scl )
- `#gK` transform: translate( x − K.x − m/2 px, y − K.y − m/2 px ) rotate( tilt deg ) scale( scl )
- Order matters: translate first, then rotate, then scale; transform-origin is the default centre of the canvas, so rotation and scaling happen around the grill's centre.

### 11.6 Balloons release

- r = clamp( p · 1.25 ) (the balloons finish leaving by p = 0.8).
- Balloon transform: translate( r · −0.06 · S.w px, bob − r · 1.25 · S.h px ) rotate( sway · 1.6 − r · 6 deg ).
- So they bob in sync with the grill while idle (same bob, sway amplified ×1.6), and on scroll they rise by 1.25 panel heights (well out of the top of the sky panel, clipped by its rounded overflow), drift left by 6 % of the panel width, and rotate to −6°, pivoting on the string knot.
- Note there is no tether: the balloons rise and the grill falls simultaneously — the release reads as "let go".

### 11.7 Landed state

Toggle class `landed` on `<body>` whenever **p > 0.9** (on every frame — scrolling back up removes it and the headline fades out).

### 11.8 Debug hook (optional, but included in the original)

Expose `window.__olla` with getter `p` (current smoothed progress), getter `ready` (number of cached frames) and the `measure` function.

---

## 12. Layering — why two canvases (the key illusion)

- The sky panel and the kitchen panel are **separate rounded boxes with `overflow: hidden`**, separated by a **1.19vw strip of page beige** (#e9e7df).
- The grill is drawn **twice**: once in a canvas inside the sky panel, once in a canvas inside the kitchen panel. Both are positioned from the **same document-space centre (x, y)** by subtracting each panel's own document origin. Same frame, same size, same rotation.
- Each panel clips its own copy to its own rounded window. So while the grill crosses the boundary, its upper part is visible inside the sky panel, its lower part inside the kitchen panel, and **the slice that overlaps the beige gutter is invisible** — the grill appears to pass *behind* the page, as if the panels were windows onto one continuous space. The rounded corners clip it too.
- Do NOT use a single fixed/overlay canvas — that would paint over the beige gutter and break the illusion.
- In the sky panel the giant "olla" word (z 3) and tagline (z 3) are above the grill (z 2), and the grill (later in DOM, same z 2) is above the balloons. In the kitchen panel the headline (z 4) is above the grill.

---

## 13. Responsive / phone layout (max-width: 760px)

- `--w` becomes `calc(100vw − 32px)` (16 px side gutters); `--gap` becomes **12px**.
- Hide `#links` and `#drop` entirely (`display: none`). Nav horizontal padding becomes **18px** (logo left, search icon right).
- `#hero`: `flex-direction: column`, `height: auto`, `padding-top: 76px`.
- `#sky`: `flex: none`, `height: 72vh`; `.word` font size **34vw**.
- `#card`: `flex: none`, `height: 78vh`, padding **18px**; the shop button `left: 18px; right: 18px`.
- `#kitchen`: `height: 70vh`.
- `#ktext`: `white-space: normal`, `width: 86%`.
- The JS geometry is unchanged — because everything is measured from live bounding rects in document space, the grill automatically falls from the sky panel, past the card (which is now stacked between sky and kitchen — the grill simply passes behind it since neither panel copy paints over the card), and lands in the kitchen gap. The scroll end formula is the same.

---

## 14. Copy deck (all text, verbatim)

| Location | Text |
|---|---|
| `<title>` | olla — Stack-smart kitchenware |
| Nav logo | olla |
| Nav links | Shop · olla · olla PRO · Simply Good · Recipes · Journal |
| Search button aria-label | Search |
| Drop items | Shop All · Stack-smart™ · EverCoat™ · Family Sized · Pro Performance |
| Sky tagline | Stack-smart<sup>™</sup> ⏎ kitchenware |
| Sky giant word | olla |
| Card pill | NEW |
| Card paragraph | Say hello to simplicity. ⏎ Introducing Stack-smart<sup>™</sup> ⏎ kitchenware. |
| Card button | Shop Stack-smart™ |
| Kitchen h2 | Cooks for your family. Fits your space. |
| Kitchen p | A stack-smart kitchenware system designed ⏎ to save up to 50% more cupboard space. |

(⏎ = `<br>`.)

---

## 15. Timeline walkthrough (what the user should experience)

1. **Load (scroll 0)**: Nav, sky panel, yellow card. Pots clip loops in the card with no visible edges (card colour sampled from the clip). Grill appears (as soon as frame 0 is keyed) hanging at 81 %/52.5 % of the sky panel, 42.5 % of the panel height, closed, gently bobbing ±6 px and swaying ±1.4°, with the balloon bunch above it, strings tied to the handle, bobbing with it.
2. **First few percent of scroll**: idle bob/sway fade out by p ≈ 0.083. Balloons start rising and drifting left, rotating toward −6°; they leave the top of the sky panel by p = 0.8.
3. **p 0.02 → 0.92**: the grill falls — slow at first, accelerating (q^1.75) — drifts horizontally toward the counter gap and shrinks (smoothstep), tilting up to −9° at mid-fall. From q 0.12 it opens into a V, then folds shut by q 0.84. It slides behind the giant "olla" word, exits the bottom of the sky panel, is hidden while crossing the beige gutter (and behind nothing else), re-emerges from the top edge of the kitchen panel and settles, level and closed, with its feet on the counter gap at image point (0.489, 0.641).
4. **p > 0.9**: headline "Cooks for your family. Fits your space." fades up 14 px over 0.7 s, the paragraph follows 0.12 s later. Kitchen panel top is now just under the nav.
5. **Scrolling back up** reverses everything exactly (all state is a pure function of smoothed scroll progress plus time for the idle motion).

---

## 16. Implementation notes and pitfalls

- Everything must be computed from live layout; never hard-code pixel positions. Re-run measure on resize.
- Use one rAF loop for everything; do not use scroll event listeners for animation (the loop reads scrollY directly).
- The grill canvases are never resized during scroll — only transformed. Redraw canvas pixels only when the frame index changes.
- Draw the cached 560 px frames with the default image smoothing.
- Do not add any opacity fades, blurs or crossfades to the grill, balloons or videos. The only opacity transitions on the page are the menu items and the landed headline.
- The card video must stay a real `<video>` element (not canvas), muted, looping, inline.
- Don't add shadows to any panel, nav or pill. Flat design: white, beige, navy, yellow.
- Panels' corner radius is **14px**; nav and drop strip **10px**; pill and button fully rounded (30px / 40px).
- If the grill clip fails to load (CORS/network), the page must still work: nothing is drawn for the grill and the rest animates normally.

---

## 17. Acceptance checklist

- [ ] Single HTML file; Jost 400/500/600 from Google Fonts; title "olla — Stack-smart kitchenware".
- [ ] Page background #e9e7df; ink #16193a; navy #141a4a; card fallback #f7d23a; easing cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1) everywhere an ease is used.
- [ ] All five asset URLs present verbatim (SKY, BALLOONS, KITCHEN via images.higgs.ai; GRILL_CLIP, POTS_CLIP via cloudfront), none substituted or re-hosted.
- [ ] Nav: fixed, 87vw, 5vh (min 40px) tall at top 1.9vh, white, radius 10px, 3.9vw side padding; logo "olla" clamp(17px,1.35vw,24px)/600/−0.03em; links centred with translateX(−52%), gap 2.4vw, clamp(12px,.95vw,16px)/500; left-to-right underline on hover (1.5px, bottom −3px, .35s); 18px search glyph at right.
- [ ] Shop hover/click opens the drop strip: 0.9vh below nav, 9.5vh (min 70px), clip-path wipe down .45s, items fade/slide from −6px with 0/40/80/120/160 ms stagger; chevron rotates 180°, Shop dims to .55; 160 ms close delay bridges the gap; five line icons (storefront, stacked cubes, leaf, family, bolt-in-circle) stroke 1.3, hover #3a49c9.
- [ ] Hero row: 87vw, padding-top 9.3vh, 100vh tall, gap 1.19vw; sky panel 71.1% × 89.3vh, radius 14, overflow hidden; card fills the rest, 89.3vh, radius 14.
- [ ] Sky tagline at 6.45%/8.8%, clamp(20px,2.05vw,36px)/500/1.08/−0.01em with small top-aligned ™; giant "olla" at left 6.1% bottom 5.4%, 27vh/500, line-height .74, −0.035em, above the grill.
- [ ] Card: NEW pill (3vh, min 22px, 1.25vw padding, radius 30), paragraph 2.1vh below at clamp(12px,.92vw,16px)/1.55/500, pots video at 50%/52%, 118% wide square, object-fit cover, radial mask closest-side #000 72% → transparent 99%; card background equals the average of the clip's top-left 12% region; "Shop Stack-smart™" pill button at bottom 2.4vh, 4.3vh tall (min 32px), hover navy/white.
- [ ] Kitchen panel: 87vw × 89.3vh, 1.19vw below hero, radius 14, overflow hidden, cover-fitted photo; 9.3vh spacer after it.
- [ ] Headline centred on cover-mapped image point (0.496, 0.125); h2 size = 2.85% and p size = 2.05% of displayed image height; hidden until p > 0.9, then .7s fade/rise with .12s stagger; reverses on scroll up.
- [ ] Grill clip cached as 48 seeked frames into 560px canvases; chroma key k = g − max(r,b), threshold 18, soft range 52, despill g → min(g, max(r,b)+6); grill appears as soon as frame 0 is ready.
- [ ] Grill hangs at 81%/52.5% of sky panel, frame = 42.5% of panel height, bobbing ±6px @1.9 rad/s and swaying ±1.4° @1.3 rad/s, fading out over the first 1/12 of progress.
- [ ] Balloons 30% of sky width, aspect 1360:2048, transform-origin 49.4% 94.6%, strings meet the handle at 7.5% of the grill frame; release: up 1.25 × panel height, left 6% width, rotate −6°, complete at p = 0.8.
- [ ] Progress = scrollY / max(200, kitchenTopDoc − 0.093·innerHeight), smoothed by 0.18/frame with 0.0005 snap; q = clamp((p − 0.02)/0.9); vertical q^1.75; drift and size smoothstep; tilt sin(qπ)·−9° + sway; frame = round(clamp((q − 0.12)/0.72)·47).
- [ ] Landing: centre x at gap x, frame bottom (91% of frame) on the counter gap at image point (0.489, 0.641); size = displayed image height × 0.2 / 0.83; lands closed and level.
- [ ] Two grill canvases (one per panel) driven by the same document coordinates; the grill visibly disappears in the beige gutter between sky and kitchen and is clipped by the rounded corners — never drawn on top of the gutter.
- [ ] Canvases sized ceil(max(c0,c1)·1.05) CSS px at dpr ≤ 2, animated only via transform translate→rotate→scale(size/m).
- [ ] Phone (≤760px): width 100vw − 32px, gap 12px, no links/drop, nav padding 18px, stacked hero (padding-top 76px), sky 72vh with 34vw word, card 78vh with 18px padding, kitchen 70vh, headline wraps at 86% width; the fall still lands in the gap.
- [ ] No opacity crossfades on grill/balloons/videos, no shadows, no external JS libraries; page works (minus the grill) if the clip fails.

title: Clothes Rail
description: Single-page, full-screen hero for a fictional children's clothing label called HINA. The page is one quiet studio wall with a steep diagonal clothes rail running from the top-left corner down towards the centre-right. Features interactive cursor/mouse tracking and scrub-driven interaction with precision layout polish.
full_prompt:
# HINA — Little Wardrobe: interactive garment-rail hero

Build a single-page, full-screen hero for a fictional children's clothing label called **HINA**. The page is one quiet studio wall with a steep diagonal clothes rail running from the top-left corner down towards the centre-right. Twelve small garments hang on it; the first one hangs large at the front-left, the other eleven hang behind it on the rail at full width, each one tucked behind the piece in front so that only its right-hand side shows, and they get smaller as they recede. A thin, very airy info column sits on the right. Visitors browse the rail (wheel, arrow keys, arrow buttons, swipe), hover a piece on the rail to see it pulled out like someone lifting a hanger to look at it, click a rail piece to bring it to the front, and click the front piece to open a detail view in which the rest of the rail closes up into a soft blurred stack behind it while a detail panel with three photo tabs slides in. Everything must feel calm, soft and premium — pastel, thin type, very wide letter-spacing, slow eased motion. Use a single HTML file with inline CSS and inline JavaScript, no frameworks, no build step.

## 1. Assets (use these exact URLs)

All images are loaded straight from their Higgsfield result links through the images.higgs.ai proxy, which converts them to WebP. Build each proxied URL as: `https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=` + the URL-encoded result link + `&w=<width>&q=85`. Do not download, crop or re-host any of them; every piece is shown with CSS background-size and background-position crops of the sheets below.

| Asset | Result link (encode it into the proxy URL) | Proxy width | Native size | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Garment sprite sheet (transparent) | https://d8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/hf_20261113_121624_09fa35c4-680e-46a5-b6a9-8acd429bce67.png | 3312 | 3312 × 2480 | A 4 × 3 grid of twelve children's garments, each on a small natural-wood hanger with a silver hook, background removed (true alpha).
