full_prompt:
# HERO PROMPT — "Dune Play" by Grovekit (interactive pixel-art plant playground)

Build a single self-contained `index.html` (inline CSS + inline vanilla JS, no frameworks, no build step) that recreates the page described below **exactly**. The page is a full-viewport, non-scrolling toy: three pixel-art desert plants (a coconut palm, a barrel cactus with a pink flower, and a jacaranda tree) stand on small sand mounds over a flat warm-sand background. You can click or brush them to shake their leaves and petals loose, turn on weather so the wind bends them and strips foliage off, watch leaves fall and pile up as litter, have everything "grow back", flip to an x-ray "skeleton" view, toggle sound, switch to a single-plant carousel and toggle dark mode.

Everything visual on the plants is made of square "cells" (fat pixels) drawn on one full-screen `<canvas>`. All UI chrome is HTML floating above the canvas.

Document title: **`Dune Play · Grovekit`** (with a middle dot). `lang="en"`, UTF-8, `width=device-width,initial-scale=1` viewport.

---

## 1. Assets

Exactly three sprites are used. Each is a **transparent-background pixel-art PNG** rendered by Higgsfield and served through the images.higgs.ai proxy. Load them with `crossOrigin = "anonymous"` (pixel data is read back from a canvas, so CORS must be honoured). Use these URLs verbatim:

| key | plant | URL |
|---|---|---|
| `palm` | coconut palm | `https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=png&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20261109_023150_cc5c0d10-d6fc-429d-9245-a05e69771f45.png&w=1024` |
| `cactus` | barrel cactus with pink flower | `https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=png&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20261109_023155_2d3af7db-5e50-423f-822f-fbbb8b599e76.png&w=1024` |
| `jac` | jacaranda tree (purple blossom) | `https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=png&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20261109_023200_f11ab77e-4a73-43f2-971c-d77090c352ff.png&w=1024` |

Font: **Inter** from Google Fonts, weights **400, 500, 600** only, `display=swap`, with `preconnect` hints to `fonts.googleapis.com` and `fonts.gstatic.com` (crossorigin). Fallback stack: `"Inter", system-ui, sans-serif`. Antialiased font smoothing (`-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased`).

No other images, icon fonts or libraries. All icons are tiny inline SVGs or text glyphs, described below.

The three sprites are loaded in parallel; only when all three are decoded and converted does the app run layout and start the animation loop. Until then the page shows the UI over the plain background.

---

## 2. Theme tokens

Define CSS custom properties on `:root` (light) and override them on `body.dark` (dark). The theme switches by toggling the class `dark` on `<body>`.

| token | light | dark | use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--bg` | `#f2ebdf` | `#14110d` | page + canvas background (warm sand / near-black brown) |
| `--panel` | `#fff` | `#1f1b15` | pill / panel fill |
| `--ink` | `#17140f` | `#f3ede2` | primary text, slider fill |
| `--mute` | `#8b8378` | `#8f877a` | secondary text, inactive segments, dots, ticks |
| `--line` | `rgba(23,20,15,.09)` | `rgba(243,237,226,.09)` | 1 px borders, dividers |
| `--seg` | `#ece5d9` | `#2b261e` | segmented-control trough, BETA chip |
| `--knob` | `#fff` | `#f3ede2` | switch & slider knobs (but see dark overrides below: both become pure `#fff` in dark) |

## 4. The canvas

- `<canvas id="scene">` fixed, `inset:0`, 100%×100%, `image-rendering: pixelated`, `touch-action:none`. It sits below all UI.
- Backing size = `round(innerWidth·DPR) × round(innerHeight·DPR)` where **DPR = min(devicePixelRatio || 1, 2)**.
- All drawing is axis-aligned filled squares of side **C** device pixels (one "cell"). No antialiasing, no images drawn to the main canvas — every sprite pixel is its own `fillRect`.

---

## 5. Sprite-to-grid pipeline (run once per plant at load)

Each plant definition:

| key | target rows | flex (bendiness) | default foliage kind | wood rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| palm | **96** | **1.15** | `frond` | hue 12–48° (inclusive), saturation > .30, value < .82 |
| cactus | **58** | **0.12** | `flesh` | special (below) |
| jac | **86** | **0.60** | `petal` | hue 8–50° (inclusive), saturation > .22, value < .72 |

Steps:
1. **Decode** the PNG, draw it to an offscreen canvas at native size, read pixels.
2. **Crop to alpha bounding box**: the bbox of all pixels with alpha **> 60**.
3. **Downsample**: target rows = per plant (above); cols = `round(rows · bboxWidth / bboxHeight)`. Draw the cropped region into a `cols × rows` canvas with `imageSmoothingEnabled = true` and `imageSmoothingQuality = 'high'` and read it back.
4. **Alpha threshold**: skip any cell with alpha **< 120** (everything kept is drawn fully opaque).
5. **Posterise**: each R, G, B channel → `round(c/8)·8` (multiples of 8), clamped to ≤ 255 when building the colour string `rgb(r,g,b)`.
6. **Classify** using HSV of the posterised colour (h in degrees 0–360, s = (max−min)/max, v = max, all from 0–1 channels; standard hue formula, negative hue + 360):
   - **Palm / Jacaranda**: `wood = rule(h,s,v)` from the table — brown trunks/branches are wood; everything else is foliage of the plant's default kind (`frond` for palm, `petal` for jacaranda — the whole jacaranda canopy behaves like petals).
   - **Cactus** (evaluated in this order):
     - `green` = 60 < h < 170.
     - If green **and v < .36** → **wood** (the dark rib lines) with a **bare colour `#b2875a`** (see §9).
     - else if **flower** → kind `petal`. Flower = (h > 300 or h < 18) with s > .35 (pink petals), **or** (38 ≤ h ≤ 62 with s > .6 and the cell is in the top 30 % of rows, y < rows·0.3) (the yellow flower centre).
     - else if **spine** = s < .38 and v > .55 (pale, low-saturation light pixels) → kind `spine`.
     - else → kind `flesh` (the green body).
7. **Looseness**: build an occupancy grid of kept cells. For each cell count occupied cells `n` in its **7×7 neighbourhood** (offsets −3…+3 both axes, the cell itself included, out-of-bounds ignored). `loose = clamp((1 − n/49)·1.8 + random·0.25, 0, 1)`. Edge/outer cells are loose (≈1), interior cells are tight (≈0).
8. **Seed**: each cell gets `seed = random · 6.28`.

Each cell record stores: home column `hx`, home row `hy`, colour, `wood` flag, optional `bare` colour, `kind` (`frond` | `petal` | `flesh` | `spine`), `loose`, `seed`, and runtime state. Each plant record also stores `cols`, a spring position `k = 0` and velocity `kv = 0`.

## 6. World layout (on load and on every window resize / view change)

- **Cell size**: `C = max(2, round(innerHeight · DPR · 0.0054))` device pixels in the three-plant view; factor **0.0068** in single view (plants appear ~26 % larger).
- Grid width `cols = ceil(canvasWidth / C) + 2`.
- **Ground row** `GY = round(canvasHeight · 0.68 / C)` — the ground line is at 68 % of the viewport height.
- Allocate a **litter height map** `hm` (one int per column, all 0) and a **floor mask** `floor` (one flag per column, all 0).
- Plant centre fractions of width: palm **0.20**, cactus **0.48**, jacaranda **0.77**. In single view all are at **0.50** and only the selected plant is visible (`one` index; default **1 = cactus**).
- Per plant: centre column `cx = round(canvasWidth · fx / C)`; origin `ox = cx − round(cols/2)`; `oy = GY − rows` (the sprite's bottom row sits on row GY−1).
- **Sand mound** per plant: width `w = round(max(plantCols · 1.05, 40))` cells, starting at column `cx − round(w/2)`. For each x = 0…w−1 with `t = x/(w−1)`, mound height `hgt = round( sin(t·π)^0.6 · 3 )` (0–3 cells, a flat-topped dome). Fill cells from row `GY+1` up to row `GY+1−hgt` (y = 0…hgt, row = GY − y + 1). Each cell's tone = `tones[(x·7 + y·3) mod 4]` with tones `['#e4cfa6', '#d9c094', '#cdb282', '#efdcb8']` — a dithered sandy texture. The mound is drawn before the plant every frame (the plant base overlaps its top).
- **Litter floor**: only under visible plants, columns `cx − (W>>1)` to `cx + (W>>1)` (exclusive) where `W = round(max(plantCols·1.05, 40) · 1.25)` — i.e. **1.25× the mound width**. Falling foliage can only land where `floor` is set; elsewhere it falls through and off the bottom of the screen.
- Update the single-view dots (active = selected index).
- **Reset**: every cell of every plant goes back to attached (state 0); body class `bare` is removed.

## 7. Interaction: shaking

### Hit test
Convert the pointer to grid coords: `gx = clientX · DPR / C`, `gy = clientY · DPR / C`. For each visible plant, quick-reject unless `ox−3 ≤ gx ≤ ox+cols+3` and `oy−3 ≤ gy ≤ GY+2`. Then the plant is hit if **any attached cell** (state 0, wood or foliage) has `|ox + hx + sx − gx| < 3` and `|oy + hy − gy| < 3` (sx = that cell's current sway offset). First hit plant wins.

### Hover cursor
On pointermove (when not dragging) set the canvas cursor to `pointer` over a plant, otherwise `default`.

### Click (pointerdown)
If a plant is hit: capture the pointer, start a drag record `{plant, lastX = clientX}`, and **shake(plant, dir = random ±1, power = 1)**.

### Drag shake
While dragging, on pointermove compute `dx = clientX − lastX`; whenever `|dx| > 28` px, **shake(plant, sign(dx), power = 0.7)** and set `lastX = clientX`. (So brushing back and forth keeps shaking the same plant.) pointerup / pointercancel end the drag.

### shake(plant, dir, power)
1. `leaves` = all foliage (non-wood) cells currently attached.
2. Spring impulse: `kv += dir · (5 + 4·power)`.
3. Count to detach: `n = max( min(leaves, 30), min( round(leaves · 0.13 · power), 170 ) )` — at least 30 (or all if fewer), ~13 % of what's left, capped at 170.
4. Sort leaves descending by `loose + random·0.9` (looser, outer leaves preferred, with randomness) and detach the first `n` with initial velocity:
   - `vx = dir·(6 + random·16) + windDir·windSpeed·12`
   - `vy = −(6 + random·16)` (upward toss; units = cells/second, +y is down)
5. Increment the Shaken counter by 1 (always, even if nothing was left to drop) and re-render it as en-US formatted.

### Spring
Each plant has a 1-D damped spring `k` (position) / `kv` (velocity), integrated every frame: `kv += (−k·42 − kv·3.4)·dt; k += kv·dt` (stiffness **42**, damping **3.4**, semi-implicit Euler). Its contribution is added to the sway (§8), so a shake makes the whole plant whip side to side and settle over ~1–2 s.

---

## 8. Wind model and per-frame simulation

### Time
`t` = seconds since page start; `dt = min(0.05, frame delta seconds)`.

### Gust noise
`gustN(t) = ( sin(1.31t) + sin(2.17t + 1.3) + 0.8·sin(0.63t + 2.1) + 2.8 ) / 5.6` → a smooth 0…~1 signal.

### Wind value
`g = gustN(t)`; `w = dir · ( speed·0.75 + speed·g·gust·0.9 + gust·g·0.12 )`, `aw = |w|`. `dir` is −1 (Left) or +1 (Right). Note that even at speed 0 the gust term gives a faint idle breath.

### Automatic shedding rate
`rate = speed > 0.15 ? speed^2.4 · 0.045 · (0.35 + gustN(1.7t) · gust · 1.7) : 0`.

### Per plant, per frame
1. Draw its sand mound cells.
2. Integrate the spring (§7).
3. **Sway**: `sway = ( w·0.55 + sin(0.9t + cx)·0.05 + (aw > 0.05 ? sin(3.1t + cx)·aw·0.12 : 0) ) · flex + k·0.55·max(0.25, flex)` (cx = plant centre column, de-syncing plants).
4. For each cell with `hg = 1 − hy/rows` (0 at base, 1 at top):

**Attached (state 0)**
- Foliage only: counts toward `total` and `attached`. Auto-detach with probability per frame `rate · dt · (spine ? 0.25 : 1) · (0.2 + loose·1.6) · (0.4 + hg)`, initial velocity `vx = w·30 + (random−0.5)·8`, `vy = −random·6`. If detached, skip drawing as attached.
- **Bend offset** (all attached cells): `ox = sway · hg^1.7 · rows · 0.14`, `oy = 0` — the base is anchored, the top bends most.
- **Streaming tails** (foliage only): `arm = loose^1.6 · (flex > 0.3 ? 1 : 0.35)` (stiff plant — cactus — gets 0.35×); `g = 0.65 + 0.35·sin(2.6t − hx·0.18 + seed·0.3)` (a travelling ripple across the canopy); then `ox += w·aw·arm·rows·0.42·g + sin(7t + seed)·arm·aw·1.4` (pull downwind plus fast flutter) and `oy = −arm·aw²·3·g` (outer leaves lift slightly in strong wind).
- Store `sx = round(ox)`, `sy = round(oy)` (whole cells, keeping it crunchy pixel art). Draw at cell `(ox_plant + hx + sx, oy_plant + hy + sy)`.
- Colour: the cell colour, except cactus rib wood cells which are mixed toward their bare colour (§9).

**Not attached** — foliage counts toward `total` only.

**Flying (state 1)** — lifetime factor `lt` by kind: **petal 1.5, frond 1.25, flesh 0.95, spine 0.6** (set at detach; each flying cell also gets a random phase `ph ∈ [0, 6.28)`).
- Accelerations: `ax = w·48·lt + sin(4.2t + ph)·16·lt` (wind push + side-to-side flutter); `ay = (spine ? 50 : 18) / lt` (gravity: spines drop fast, petals float).
- Drag-toward-target integration: `vx += (ax − vx·1.6)·dt`; `vy += (ay − vy·1.1)·dt`.
- Position: `x += vx·dt + sin(6t + ph)·0.05·lt`; `y += vy·dt`.
- **Leaving the screen**: if `x < −4` or `x > cols + 4` or `y > canvasHeight/C + 4` → state 3 (gone, not drawn).
- **Landing**: with `c = round(x)`, if `c` is in range, `floor[c]` is set, `y ≥ GY − hm[c]` and `vy > 0` → state 2, snap `y = GY − hm[c]`, `x = c`, then `hm[c] = min(5, hm[c] + 1)`. Litter piles up on the ground row and stacks at most **5** cells high per column.

**Landed (state 2)** — if `aw > 0.55` (storm-strength), each frame with probability `(aw − 0.5)·dt·1.4` the litter is **re-lifted**: detach again with `vx = w·40`, `vy = −8 − random·10` (and its column's `hm` decrements by 1).

**Returning (state 4)** — see §9.

States 1, 2, 4 are drawn at `(round(x), round(y))` in the cell's own colour.

General detach rules: wood never detaches; a cell already flying is ignored; detaching an attached cell starts it at its current displayed position (home + sx, sy); detaching a landed cell decrements `hm` at its column; gone (3) and returning (4) cells cannot be detached. Every detach increments a per-frame counter used for sound.

5. **Skeleton overlay** (when Skeleton is on): after all the plant's cells, draw every attached wood cell again on top in `#c8382a` (light) / `#ff6a4d` (dark) at `(ox + hx + sx, oy + hy)` (horizontal sway applied, no vertical tail offset). Result: palm trunk and frond ribs, jacaranda trunk/branches and cactus rib lines show as a red x-ray rig while foliage still moves around them.
6. Plant bareness `bareK = total ? 1 − attached/total : 0`; the scene is "bare" if any visible plant has `attached < total`.

After all plants: unless a grow-back is in progress, toggle `body.bare` to the bare flag (shows/hides Grow back). Fire one rustle burst for the frame's detach count (§11). Update wind sound gain. Draw the windsock with the current `t` and `w`. Request the next frame.

## 9. Bare colour mixing & Grow back

### Cactus ribs
Cactus rib cells (wood with bare colour `#b2875a`) are drawn as `mix(original, #b2875a, bareK)` — linear RGB interpolation, rounded. As the cactus loses its green flesh/spines/flower, the dark rib lines warm up into a tan woody skeleton; when fully stripped they are pure `#b2875a`. (Uses the previous frame's bareK.)

### Grow back (button click)
1. Set a `growing` flag (suppresses toggling `body.bare` for **1800 ms**), clear `hm` to all zeros.
2. For every visible foliage cell not attached: if it is gone (state 3) or has never had a position, respawn it at `x = homeX + (random − 0.5)·30`, `y = GY + 6` (just below ground, spread around the plant). Set state 4, remember start `fx, fy`.
3. **Staggered, bottom-first** start time: with `r = hy/rows`, `t0 = now + (r > 0 ? (1 − r)·0.25 : 0) + (1 − r)·0.45 + random·0.35` seconds — cells near the base start first, the crown last (up to ~1.05 s later). Duration `du = 0.55 + random·0.35` s.
4. Remove `body.bare` immediately (button fades out).
5. Each frame for state 4: `e = clamp((now − t0)/du, 0, 1)`, `ez = 1 − (1 − e)^3` (**ease-out cubic**); `x = fx + (homeX − fx)·ez`, `y = fy + (homeY − fy)·ez − sin(e·π)·8` — every pixel flies home along an **8-cell upward arc**. Home = `(ox + hx, oy + hy)` (no sway). Before its start time a cell waits at its start position. When `e ≥ 1` it becomes attached (state 0) with `sx = 0`.

### Grow back visibility rules
- Visible (`body.bare`) whenever any visible plant has any detached foliage (flying, landed, gone or returning), recomputed every frame — except during the 1.8 s grow window, where it stays hidden.
- Removed on layout changes (resize, view switch, carousel step), which also reattach everything.
- In single view it sits right of the carousel nav (§3.9).

---

## 10. Windsock (pixel art, in the control bar)

Drawn every frame on the 28×30 canvas (displayed at 2×, pixelated). Clear it, then:
- **Pole**: colour `#6b6258` (light) / `#9a8f80` (dark). A 2-px-wide rectangle at x = 13, y = 1, height 29; plus a 4×2 base foot at x = 12, y = 28.
- **Sock**: `a = min(1, |w|)`, `d = sign(w)` (or +1 if 0), droop angle `ang = (1 − a)·1.25` rad (calm: hangs ~72° down beside the pole; gale: straight out horizontally). Five segments `i = 0…4`:
  - distance from pole `r = 2 + 2.4·i`
  - flap `fl = sin(10t − 1.2i) · a · 0.9` (a wave travelling down the sock, stronger in stronger wind)
  - `dx = cos(ang)·r`, `y = 3 + sin(ang)·r + fl`
  - segment height `h = max(2, 4 − floor(i/2))` → 4, 4, 3, 3, 2 (tapering)
  - colour: even i `#e8573b`, odd i `#f4efe6` (orange/white stripes)
  - x: if d > 0, `15 + dx`; else `9 − dx` (mirrored to the left side of the pole)
  - fill a rect `3 × h` at `(round(x), round(y − h/2 + 1))`.

---

## 11. Sound (Web Audio, created lazily on first Sound ON)

- Turning Sound ON the first time creates an `AudioContext` (with `webkitAudioContext` fallback); later ON clicks just `resume()` it.
- **Noise buffer**: mono, 2 s at the context sample rate, brown-ish noise: `l = (l + 0.02·white)/1.02`, sample = `l · 3.5`, where white ∈ [−1, 1).
- **Wind bed**: looping buffer source → **bandpass 420 Hz, Q 0.6** → gain (starts 0) → destination, started immediately. Every frame the gain is smoothed with `setTargetAtTime(target, now, 0.25)` where target = Sound on ? `min(0.5, aw·0.45 + 0.01)` : 0 (so turning Sound off fades it out but keeps the graph alive).
- **Rustle bursts**: once per frame when ≥ 1 cell detached that frame (and Sound is on): a new one-shot source on the same noise buffer → **highpass 1800 Hz** → gain envelope → destination. Peak `a = min(0.22, 0.02 + n/180)` (n = cells detached this frame); gain 0 at now, linear ramp to `a` in 20 ms, exponential ramp to 0.0005 by +0.35 s; start at a random offset 0–1 s into the buffer; stop at +0.4 s.

---

## 12. Controls state & behaviour

Initial state: weather off, mode `breezy`, direction +1 (Right), wind speed **0**, gust **0.45**, skeleton off, sound off, light theme, three-plant view, single index 1.

- **Weather switch**: toggles weather. Turning it **ON** applies the current mode's preset with animated sliders. Turning it **OFF** animates speed back to **0** and gust to **0.45**. The Breezy/Storm segment is dimmed (.55) while weather is off.
- **Presets** (speed, gust): **Breezy = 0.40 / 0.45** (labels "Breeze" / "Gusty"), **Storm = 0.95 / 0.95** (labels "Gale" / "Wild gusts").
- **Breezy/Storm buttons**: select the mode **and** force weather ON, then apply the preset (animated .7s).
- **Direction Left/Right**: sets dir −1/+1 and moves the `.on` highlight. Affects wind sign, leaf flight, toss velocity, sway direction and windsock side.
- **Sliders**: manual edit; touching one turns weather OFF (no preset reset).
- **Skeleton switch**: toggles the red wood overlay.
- **Sound switch**: toggles audio (initialises on first enable — requires that user gesture).
- **Moon**: toggles dark theme (all tokens + canvas background + skeleton/pole colours).
- **View toggle**: "All plants" / "One plant" sets single mode, swaps `.on`, toggles `body.single`, re-layouts (bigger cells, one centred plant, reset).
- **‹ / ›**: previous `(one + 2) mod 3` / next `(one + 1) mod 3`, re-layout. Dots reflect palm, cactus, jacaranda order.
- **Resize**: re-layout (resets all foliage).

Optional debug hook: expose `window.__pp` with the plants array, state object, grow, slider setters, weather sync, shake, setSingle and a `detachAll` that throws every foliage cell with random velocity (x ±10, y up to −20) — handy for testing, not visible.

---

## 13. Look & feel summary

- Light: warm cream sand `#f2ebdf` everywhere, white rounded pills with hairline borders, near-black ink. Dark: deep brown-black `#14110d` with `#1f1b15` pills and cream ink; transitions are .5 s.
- The plants are chunky (cells ≈ 0.54 % of viewport height, e.g. 5 device px on a 900 px tall 1× screen, 10 on retina), sitting on the 68 % ground line with small dithered sand mounds. Palm left (tall, very bendy), cactus slightly left of centre (short, nearly rigid, pink flower on top), jacaranda right (purple canopy, medium flex).
- At rest there is a subtle idle sway. In Storm the palm whips hard downwind, fronds stream out into tails, petals and leaves rip away, flutter across the screen, pile up in little drifts under the plants (max 5 high) and get swept off again; the windsock stands straight out and flaps.
- Pixel crispness everywhere: integer cell offsets, `image-rendering: pixelated`, crisp-edged icon SVG.

---

## 14. Acceptance checklist

- [ ] Title is `Dune Play · Grovekit`; Inter 400/500/600 loaded from Google Fonts.
- [ ] All light and dark tokens match §2 exactly; theme toggles via `body.dark` with .5 s background transition and the canvas background follows the computed body colour.
- [ ] Brand pill "Grovekit" at 24/16, 44 px high, 14px/600.
- [ ] Title "Dune Play" 17px/500 + raised 8px BETA chip + 20 px circled "i" 14 px further right; tooltip text verbatim, 290 px, slides 6 px + fades; outside click closes it.
- [ ] Counter pill at top 88, 7×7 pink flower with yellow centre, "Shaken **4,812** times", increments per shake with en-US commas.
- [ ] View toggle (two buttons 44×36, three-bar / one-bar icons) at right 88, moon pill 46×46 at right 24; view toggle hidden ≤ 900 px.
- [ ] Control bar: min(1240px, 100vw−32px) × max(13vh, 96px), bottom 16, radius 28, gap 28, padding 28, big soft shadow; order windsock · Weather · divider · Direction · Wind speed · Gusts · divider · Show.
- [ ] Switches 50×30, springy knob, green `#2fb35a` when on; segments with white raised selected chip; custom 168 px sliders with 3 tick dots and 20 px knob.
- [ ] On load labels read "Calm" and "Gusty"; Breezy → 0.40/0.45 ("Breeze"/"Gusty"), Storm → 0.95/0.95 ("Gale"/"Wild gusts"), animated .7s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1); weather off → 0/0.45; touching a slider turns weather off.
- [ ] Three sprite URLs used verbatim, loaded with CORS; converted via alpha bbox (>60), high-quality downsample to 96/58/86 rows, alpha ≥ 120 kept, channels posterised to multiples of 8.
- [ ] Wood classification per §5 (palm h12–48 s>.3 v<.82; jac h8–50 s>.22 v<.72; cactus dark green v<.36 ribs → wood with bare `#b2875a`; pink/yellow-top → petal; pale low-sat → spine; rest flesh).
- [ ] Looseness from 7×7 neighbourhood `(1−n/49)·1.8 + rand·0.25`, clamped; per-cell random seed.
- [ ] C = round(H·DPR·0.0054) (single 0.0068), min 2, DPR ≤ 2; ground at 68 %; plants at 20/48/77 % (single: centred, default cactus).
- [ ] Sand mounds: width max(cols·1.05, 40), height round(sin(tπ)^0.6·3), four tones by (7x+3y) mod 4; litter floor only under mounds at 1.25× width; litter stacks ≤ 5.

# Found — The Curiosity Cabinet with a Web-Spinning Spider (exact recreation prompt) Give me a single-file, full-screen home page for **found**, a personal archive of curious objects called "the curiosity cabinet". The page is flat electric blue with a giant white wordmark `found` in the middle. Collectible cut-out objects float around it: a "Main Character" mug, a frosted glass radio player, a retro laptop in a glass sleeve, a pink book with an iPod, and a "CALL MY LAWYER" t-shirt at the bottom edge. A photo-real jumping spider lives on the page. It drops in on a silk thread, chases a fly that replaces the mouse cursor, and walks on inverse-kinematics legs cut from one photo. As it moves, it spins real-looking silk threads between the letters and objects: sagging verlet ropes with dew drops, fuzz, iridescence and shadows that fall only on the objects. Click to make it pounce on the fly and wrap it in silk. Press Delete to shake the web off. When it rests, its head crossfades to a cute face that blinks, and later it falls asleep. All of it runs in one HTML file with a single 2D canvas and no libraries. The live original was a small Preact app, and plain DOM plus vanilla JS is fine. The only external resources are the Inter font, which the supplied file embeds, and three radio streams. **Source of truth:** the supplied **HTML Code** section is the complete working page. Images (all embedded as data URIs in the supplied file) | Image | Format, size | Used for | |---|---|---| | Spider photo | WebP 560 × 560 | Top view of a brown and cream banded jumping spider. Sprite space 308. | | Fly | WebP 240 × 246 | Top view of a house fly. Sprite space 920 × 945. | | Objects | PNG | Book 293 × 322, iBook 312 × 377, mug 241 × 220, t-shirt 250 × 226, all with transparency. | | UI icons | PNG | Player art 40, logo back 53 × 41, logo front 53 × 34, search 26, menu 26, heart 20, shuffle 16, previous 24, play 48, next 24, repeat 16. | ## 5. Spider rig (sprite units, 1254 base) - **Body points:** - pivot `(627,600)`, waist `(627,548)`, spinneret `(627,150)`. - Abdomen ellipse `(628,345) r 220×205`. - Head ellipses `(630,680) r 172×148`, `(545,880) r 74×70`, `(712,880) r 74×70`. - **Masks:** the abdomen and head layers are cut from the photo with these ellipses, drawn black with `blur(2·scale px)` and applied `destination-in`. - **Legs:** four legs per side, each as hip, knee and foot in the image. The left side mirrors the right with `x → 1254 − x`. - `[(470,760),(370,830),(400,1160)]` - `[(460,665),(300,690),(100,955)]` - `[(480,605),(370,580),(55,475)]` - `[(490,560),(360,420),(410,52)]` - **Leg strips:** each leg is resampled from the photo into a straight strip: - Length = femur + tibia. Width `legWidth 92`. - Bilinear sampling along the hip→knee→foot polyline. - Alpha fades out over the outer 28% of the half-width. - `split` = femur share of the strip, used to draw the femur and tibia halves separately. - **Body space:** image point → body point `(y − 600, −(x − 627))`, so the head points along +x of the heading. Each leg stores `hip` and `rest` (its foot) in body space, and `a` / `b` are the femur and tibia lengths. - If `a+b < 1.15·|rest−hip|`, scale a and b up to that. - Gait group = `(legIndex + (rightSide?0:1)) % 2`, an alternating tetrapod gait. ## 6. Spider motion (per frame, `dt = min(0.033 s, real delta)`) - **Target:** the fly's position, or the raw pointer when there is no fly image. The fly cursor - **Drawing:** the fly is drawn at `79·flySize` px wide. The wings are cut from the photo with an 11-point polygon, `(398,380) (330,415) (250,515) (180,615) (132,720) (148,795) (212,805) (305,742) (385,652) (410,560) (414,455)`, mirrored for the right wing. Wing hinge `(388,405)`. The body is the photo minus the wings. - **Following:** - The fly follows the pointer with ease `1 − e^(−(28 − 20·recoil)·dt)`. - Buzz jitter: `(sin(23.1B) + 0.6·sin(37.7B + 1.3))·2.2` and `(sin(29.3B + 0.7) + 0.6·sin(41.9B))·2.2`, scaled by `1 − landed`. - It turns along its motion above 60 px/s. - **Landing:** after 1.2s still, `landed` ramps up 3/s (down 10/s). - **Wings:** - Flying: four ghost copies at 34 Hz (46 Hz when caught). Each wing rotates `±0.9·q` around the hinge with `scaleY(1 − 0.25q)`. - Landed: the wings fold. - **Shadow:** `rgba(0,0,0, 0.2 + 0.18·landed)`, blur `3 + 9y`, offset `(3 + 14y, 5 + 26y)`, with a bob of `sin(6B)·1.2·y`, where `y = 1 − landed` is the hover height. - **Hiding:** the fly fades out over buttons, links, inputs and `[data-no-spider]`, where the system pointer shows instead. ## 8. Silk - **Threads:** - Verlet ropes of 12 segments (13 points). - Damping 0.975, gravity `110·dt²`. - Wind `(sin(0.45B)·0.6 + sin(1.3B + 1.7)·0.4)·(0.6 + 0.4·sin(1.1B + 0.012y + phase))·22·dt²` on x. - Four constraint passes with both ends pinned. Rest segment length `distance/12 × 1.01–1.015` gives a slight sag. - The pointer pushes rope points within 36px. - **Live thread:** runs from the last anchor to the spinneret, thickness 1.25. - **Anchor points:** points sampled every 7px along the visible outline of every `[data-web-anchor]` element. - **Text:** each glyph is rasterised to a canvas in its computed font and the edge pixels (alpha > 128) are kept. - **Images:** the alpha edge (alpha > 140). - **Boxes:** rounded-rect perimeters. - These silhouettes are also kept as a mask canvas. - **Attaching:** 1. When the spinneret comes within 70px of an outline point, at least 30px from the live thread's start and more than 54px from it, the live thread is pinned there. 2. That thread gets dew drops. 3. A radial thread (thickness 0.7) joins this point to the nearest earlier anchor within 288px. 4. With 75% probability, another thread (0.85) joins it to the nearest outline point within 204px (not within 45px). 5. A new live thread starts, and the web vibrates in a 60px radius at strength 1.2. - **Free space:** with no anchor elements on the page, a point is dropped every 120px. - **Vibration:** points within a radius get random kicks of `strength·(1 − d/r)`. The whole rope is shaken a little when an end is near. Dew drops on a shaken thread start sliding with a 35% chance. - **Rendering each thread:** 1. A halo: alpha 0.06, width 4×thickness. 2. The main strand per segment: width `thick·(0.9 − 0.35·sin(πi/12))`, alpha 0.8, silk colour `rgba(255,255,255,0.75)`. 3. An iridescent overlay `hsl(190 + 150P, 100%, 74%)` at alpha `0.12 + 0.3P³`, with `P = 0.5 + 0.5·sin(2·angle + 0.3B + phase)`. 4. Two wavy sub-fibres offset ±1.1 / 0.9 × thickness, alpha 0.38, width 0.45. 5. Micro-hairs: about 3 per 1.1px (40% on touch screens), length 0.5–2.7 × thickness, alpha 0.55, width 0.35. 6. Fluff: 40% of threads carry 1–2 clumps, either 5 grey-brown dust dots (`#8a7a6a`) or 10 curling cream fibres (`rgba(240,232,220)`). 7. Dew drops: count `floor(length/55·(0.4 + rand))`, radius 1.6–6.2, drawn with a 64px glass-bead sprite (radial gradient rims, warm caustic `rgba(255,210,150,.45)`, white specular). 8. A white glint segment travels along each thread at 0.6 per second. - Threads fade to 50% over 90s. - Each anchor point gets 30 tiny hair tufts and a 3px bead. - **Shadows:** all threads and drops are drawn in black on an offscreen canvas with shadow `rgba(8,14,70,.42)`, blur 3.5, offset (7, 11). That canvas is masked (`destination-in`) by the anchor silhouettes, so web shadows fall only on letters and objects, never on the blue. - **Drops:** - Sliding drops move with the slope (`du += slope·9dt`, ×0.95). - They fall off when the slope is steep, when they reach the ends, or randomly when they are big. - Falling drops use gravity 1100. - A drop that lands on an object or letter silhouette after falling more than 10px becomes a splat: a squashed bead with a soft shadow. At most 400 splats. ## 9. Objects react The images that are anchors (mug, iBook, book, t-shirt and the nav icons) wobble as the spider walks past. - Within `260K` of the image box, at speed over 40: - Torque `cross(offset, velocity)/size²`, clamped ±2.5, ×120·dt. - Push `0.85·velocity·dt`. - Damping `e^(−2.8dt)`. Angle spring beyond 24° (×8) and offset spring beyond 50px (×8). - The t-shirt (`data-stick="bottom"`) pivots at `50% 100%`, never translates, and springs back harder beyond 8° (×20). - Applied through CSS `rotate` and `translate`. - Anchors are re-sampled 0.3s after everything stops moving. - A jump landing spins nearby objects by ±16–28°. ## 10. Input - **Mouse click** (or double-tap on touch), anywhere except controls: the spider pounces at the fly. - It lands where its mouth (heading × 360K) meets the fly, travelling at most 360K. - Duration `clamp(distance/1100, 0.28, 0.6)` s, ease-in-out quad. - Jump height `max(22, min(0.3·distance, 130))`, shown as scale and shadow. - On landing: squash, web vibration (140, 3) and nudged objects. - **Catching:** if the fly is within `55·flySize` of the mouth, it is caught for 3–4.2s. - It trembles at 47 and 31 Hz and its wings buzz. - It is wrapped in a silk cocoon: 7 ellipse strokes of radius `30·flySize` drawing on progressively, plus 70 short fibres. - Then it breaks free and is flung 150px away, while the cocoon fades. - **Delete / Backspace** (outside inputs): clear the web. - Every dew drop falls, the threads fade out at 2.6 per second and the web shakes hard. - Splats drop off-screen, and a fresh live thread starts from the spinneret. - **Touch:** hold 650ms to clear the web (with a 30ms vibration), double-tap to move the fly and jump. - **Pointer leaving the window:** the fly disappears and the spider stays put. ## 11. Loop and setup - **Canvas:** DPR capped at 2, sized by a ResizeObserver. - **Anchors** are sampled on resize, on `document.fonts.ready`, on `load` and after 600ms. - **Frame order:** 1. Update the fly. 2. Update the image nudges. 3. Update the spider (intro, jump, follow, feet). 4. Update the rest and sleep state. 5. Update the anchoring and the silk physics. - **Draw order:** 1. Web shadows. 2. Threads, splats and drops. 3. The spider through its shadowed offscreen. 4. The z letters. 5. full_prompt:
# Prompt: Halden Stories interactive map hero

Build a single-file, one-screen **interactive storytelling map hero** for a fictional climate publication, **Halden Stories** ("Discover stories across North America"). Use plain HTML, CSS, inline SVG and vanilla JS, with no framework and no build step. The look is a light "field notes" atlas: a thin ink-line vector map of North America on warm off-white paper, small terracotta dots, monospace labels and a bold sans headline. Hovering a region fills it with a moving photo, and clicking opens a horizontal, draggable slider of coloured story cards.

## Media

- **Landscape grid photo:** `https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/1571669e-4604-4c0d-9e0d-5e50b819d55d.jpg` (2336×1744). One image holding a 3×2 grid of six landscape photos separated by white gutters. The cell edges are columns 0–766, 786–1551, 1571–2336 and rows 0–862, 880–1744.
  - **Top row:** a California reservoir with a dam; Midwest crop circles from the air; a solar farm in pine forest by a river.
  - **Bottom row:** offshore wind turbines and a lighthouse at sunrise; a hydro dam in autumn boreal forest in Québec; a spare cell (wind turbines over forest, unused).
- **Grid video:** `https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/efc53bc3-598a-4b28-b2a1-e72355301bac.mp4` (1664×1244, 4s, muted, loops seamlessly). The same grid with motion inside every cell: clouds and reflections, wheat, glints across the panels, turbines spinning, water pouring through the dam.
  - The last second crossfades into the first, so it loops without a jump and never plays in reverse.
  - Its cells sit at columns 0–545, 558–1104, 1117–1663 and rows 0–615, 626–1243.
- **People:** one photo per story, each a 3:2 documentary portrait in plain workwear (no logos):
  - Midwest: `https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/a72ef465-56f3-46e7-b441-8628db42c855.jpg`
  - Canada: `https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/39c763e2-0cef-4ad2-ae51-fa174d35220d.jpg`
  - West: `https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/91ef8d93-34e6-4167-93f5-db69e2be5c22.jpg`
  - South: `https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/b28bb368-0471-49a1-bb89-82fbd7898009.jpg`
  - Northeast: `https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/eb40a5b6-4553-4d6a-8681-5dc064fbfbc4.jpg`
- **How photos are drawn:** one hidden `<video>` (not `display:none`) plays the grid. Every photo on the page is a `<canvas>` that draws its cell from that video each frame with cover-crop maths. Use the still grid image until the video has data.
- **Rule:** nothing in the photos is drawn or animated in code. All motion inside them comes from the video.

## The map (real vector geography, inline SVG)

- **Source data:** generate the paths at build time from public data, not by tracing:
  - us-atlas `states-10m` (US states)
  - world-atlas `countries-10m` (Canada)
  - Natural Earth 50m lakes (Great Lakes, Winnipeg, Great Slave, Great Bear, Athabasca, Reindeer, Nipigon, Mistassini, Smallwood, Great Salt Lake and others)
- **Projection:** Lambert conformal conic (standard parallels 29.5° and 45.5°, central meridian 106°W). It's fitted by least squares to a 1440×810 frame so that, for example:
  - the Washington/BC coast sits at about (539, 343)
  - San Diego at (539, 600)
  - the tip of Florida at (1009, 733)
  - eastern Maine at (1107, 402)
- **Lines:** simplify every path to about 0.35px and drop islands smaller than 1.6px.
- **What is drawn:** 1.4px ink lines (`#1C1A17`, round joins, `vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke`):
  - Canada's coast, including the Arctic islands and Hudson Bay
  - the US outline (lower 48 plus the Alaska coast)
  - the borders between the four US Census regions: **West, Midwest, South, Northeast**. Merge states by dropping any arc shared by two states of the same region.
  - the lake shores
- **Cleanups:**
  - Drop the duplicate Canada/US border lines, and the straight Alaska–Yukon line.
  - Mask the country lines out of the lakes (a black-filled, 3.2px-stroked lake mask).
- **Clip shapes:** each region (and Canada) also exists as a clip path (`clipPathUnits="objectBoundingBox"`, scaled 1/1440 × 1/810), so an HTML layer can be clipped to the exact shape.
- **Entrance:** the lines draw themselves (`pathLength="1"`, stroke-dashoffset 1 → 0 over 1.7s, staggered).

## Frame and scaling

- **Frame:** one **1440×810 (16:9)** frame, scaled to fit the viewport and centred.
- **Overflow:** the map and story layer bleed past the frame to the screen edges, so there are never bands.

## Type and colour

- **Colours:** paper `#F6F3EA`, ink `#1C1A17`, secondary text `#3B3731`, terracotta `#C35933`.
- **Headline:** **Source Sans 3** 700, 54px on a 50px line, tracking −.022em. Card body text: Source Sans 3 400.
- **Mono:** **IBM Plex Mono** 400/500/600 for the eyebrow, paragraph, coordinates, zone list, card labels and city names.

## Map view (1440×810)

- **Intro block** at (60, 219):
  - eyebrow "HALDEN STORIES" (11px, tracking .24em)
  - headline "Discover **stories** / across North / America", with "stories" in terracotta
  - a four-line mono paragraph at 13.2px on a 24px line: "Five regions, five people cutting / carbon where they live and work. / Hover a zone to look closer, then / open the story behind it."
- **Coordinates:** top right, two mono lines at 10.2px: the active zone's lat/long, then a fixed "48° 21' 36" N, 100° 27' 12" W".
- **Zone list:** right side. "CHOOSE ZONE" at y = 443, then a right-aligned mono list at 25px on a 45px line: Midwest, Canada, West, South, Northeast. The active zone is terracotta.
  - Beside the list, a 230px vertical ruler with fine ticks. A terracotta marker slides along it to the active name.
- **Dots** (16px terracotta, with a pulsing soft halo):
  - Canada (668, 238), West (599, 492), Midwest (808, 482), South (814, 626), Northeast (1022, 463).
- **Active zone** (Midwest by default):
  - **Photo fill:** its photo fills the region shape, fading in over 650ms. The others fade out over 450ms.
  - **Ring:** its dot becomes a 62px off-white disc with a plus. Around it, "DISCOVER STORIES · DISCOVER STORIES ·" runs on a 45px-radius circle (`textLength` fitted to the circumference) and spins every 14s. The ring pops in with an expo ease.
- **Interaction:**
  - **Hover:** hovering a region, a dot or a list name activates that zone.
  - **Click:** clicking any of them opens its story.

## Story view

- **Transition** (1.25s, quintic in-out):
  - The map slides 520px left.
  - A story layer slides in from the right and stops beside a 72px paper strip, which shows a slice of the map lines and a "‹ Back" button.
- **Slider:** five stories in a row. Each story is a full-height **landscape photo panel** (0.74 × height) followed by a **colour card** (0.69 × height).
  - **Card contents:**
    - a "01 —— 05" counter with a progress line
    - the person photo inset at the top
    - "FIGHTING CLIMATE CHANGE", then the city in Plex Mono 600 at 42px, then a two-line body
    - the region's own outline faintly in the bottom right
    - a spinning "Discover stories" badge with a plus
  - **Card colours:**
    - Midwest (Des Moines): cobalt `#2F55D4`
    - Canada (Québec): ink `#23201C`
    - West (Sacramento): terracotta `#C35933`
    - South (Austin): forest `#1F4A35`
    - Northeast (Portland): mustard `#D99A2B` with ink text
  - **Entrance:** the card's photo wipes up while scaling down from 1.25, and its text rises in a stagger.
- **Dragging:**
  - Drag the track with the pointer. It rubber-bands at the ends, has momentum, and snaps to the nearest story with an expo ease over 900ms.
  - Photos parallax slightly inside their panels.
  - On fine pointers, the cursor over the track becomes an 80px cream disc reading "‹ DRAG ›", which shrinks while pressed.
  - Arrow keys move between stories. Esc or "‹ Back" returns to the map.
- **Timing:** all motion runs on the page's own clock (a long Web Animation's currentTime), so the scene can be recorded frame by frame.

## Phones and portrait tablets

- **Layout:** no frame scaling.
- **Intro:** at the top, over a paper fade.
- **Map:** scaled to fit the middle.
- **Zones:** a row of pill chips at the bottom that scrolls to the active one.
- **Stories:** full width, with the photo at the top 42% and the card below.

## Acceptance check (1440×810)

- The map lines match real geography and draw in on load.
- Hovering West, then South, fills each region with its moving photo, and the ring, list highlight, ruler marker and coordinates follow.
- Clicking South slides into the Austin story. Dragging left snaps to Portland, and Back returns to the map.
- **Content:** no real brands or logos.

The look is a sunny hand-painted anime (Ghibli-like) afternoon: a boy and his beagle lie on a grassy hillside looking up at a big blue sky full of cumulus clouds, with a green valley far off on the right.

## Scene

- **Plate:** the whole scene is ONE 9:8 background image (2160×1920): `https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/3ca5d10d-ea2f-4907-876f-33bde169469e.jpg`.
  - **Sky:** a deep-to-light blue sky across the top 60%, with a tall cumulus cloud on the left, another on the right, and wispy streaks top-right.
  - **Hillside:** the boy (messy brown hair, white shirt, blue shorts, hands behind his head) and a brown-and-white beagle lie at the left, looking up. Grass and wildflowers fill the bottom third, softly blurred at the very bottom.
- **Motion:** the scene moves only through a looping video of the same plate: `https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/d2cb5bef-f92b-4e91-ae93-8dc6555e56ac.mp4` (960×960, 5s, muted, loops; first frame = last frame).
  - The grass ripples in steady waves, daisies nod, the boy's hair and shirt flutter, the dog's ears lift, and the clouds drift right.
  - The video was rendered square from the plate mirror-padded 120/1920 at the top and bottom. Lay it over the plate at **100% width, 112.5% height, top −6.25%** so its middle sits exactly on the plate.
- **Rule:** nothing in the scene is drawn or animated in code.

## Frame and scaling

- **Frame:** the hero is **one 1440×1280 frame** (9:8) that scales with the viewport width: `--u = 100vw/1440`, height 1280u. On a 1440×900 screen the headline, buttons and the boy and dog show first, and the chapters row sits just below the fold.
- **Placement:** every element below is placed in frame units.

## Type and colour

- **Display:** **Grandstander 900**, a rounded, slightly bouncy display face, all white. It's used for the logo, the kicker, the headline and the section title.
- **Everything else:** **Inter** 400/500. Self-host the latin woff2 files.
- **Colours:** text is white with a soft blue shadow `0 4u 18u rgba(28,70,120,.28)` on the headline. Button text green is `#5b875c`.

## Layout (1440×1280 frame)

- **Nav:**
  - **Logo:** "Meadowbell" 29.5px with a small white two-leaf sprout icon, at (31, 23).
  - **Nav pill:** a translucent sage pill `rgba(173,196,174,.45)` with backdrop blur, 546×50 at (443, 13), radius 25. Inside: Farm · Gear · Chapters · Our Crew, Inter 500 19.5px, 54px apart, starting 49px in.
  - **Join us:** a white pill, 105×45 at (1311, 14), green Inter 500 18.5px.
- **Copy, centred:**
  - **Kicker:** "HOLLYOAK'S" 40.5px, cap top at y = 203.
  - **Headline:** **"PLUCKY / SPROUT SQUAD"**, 143.5px on a 118px line pitch, cap top at y = 261.
  - **Subline:** Inter 21.2px / 27px, three lines: "Learn the Ways of the Meadow with / Hollyoak's Plucky Sprout Squad! Each chapter is / packed with play, chores, and wonder."
  - **Join us button:** white pill, 144×59 at (550, 617), green 22px.
  - **Watch preview button:** translucent mint pill `rgba(204,218,173,.6)` with blur, 184×58 at (707, 619). It has a white rounded play triangle and white 19.5px text.
- **Chapters row:**
  - **Title:** "CHAPTERS" 36px at (137, 866).
  - **Link:** "browse all chapters ›" 22px, right-aligned to x = 1308.
  - **Cards:** three 378×273 cards at x = 133, 531, 929 (y = 913), radius 15, soft shadow, each with a white rounded play triangle 20px in from the bottom-left. Card art:
    - a vegetable garden with tomato stakes and a cottage: https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/cd2d844f-ae3f-4fa9-8067-b077530b6e71.webp
    - a boy and dog on a hill path among sheep above the sea: https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/48f5b97e-c27c-4afd-9427-eb35aebd1751.webp
    - a girl in a straw hat flying a kite on a breezy hill: https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/cde5384e-ce4d-423f-925a-451b779066e0.webp

## Motion (UI only)

- **Entrance**, one Web Animations timeline, run once:
  - the logo, nav and Join us drop in
  - the kicker un-blurs
  - each headline line springs up out of a blur, 0.16s apart
  - then the subline, both buttons, the chapters title and link, and the three cards rise in turn
- **Hover:** the cards lift 8u and their art zooms to 1.05. The pills rise 2u, and the chevron nudges right.
- **Reduced motion:** no video and no transitions.

## Phones (≤ 820px)

- **Nav:** compact, with the logo and Join us.
- **Copy:** stacked and centred in flow, with the headline at 51px.
- **Chapters:** a swipeable row of cards.
- **Scene:** the 9:8 plate and video sit in one 9:8 box sized to the hero's height and shifted so the boy and dog stay in view (left 18%, translateX(−18%)).

## Acceptance check (1440×1280)

- The text, pills and cards sit at the coordinates above over the hillside scene.
- The grass visibly ripples, the boy's hair and the dog's ears move, and the clouds drift.

full_prompt:
## Prompt

Build a single-page React + Vite + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS site with exactly two full-screen sections (Hero and Capabilities). The page is a dark, cinematic web design agency landing page with "liquid glass" morphism UI elements and smooth blur/fade animations using Framer Motion.

---

### Fonts (Google Fonts)

Load via `<link>` in `index.html`:
- **Instrument Serif** (italic) -- used for all headings (`font-heading`)
- **Barlow** (weights 300, 400, 500, 600) -- used for body text (`font-body`)

Tailwind config extends `fontFamily`:
```js
heading: ["'Instrument Serif'", 'serif'],
body: ["'Barlow'", 'sans-serif'],
```

Base CSS: `html, body { background: #000; color: #fff; font-family: 'Barlow', sans-serif; }`

---

### Liquid Glass CSS (in index.css)

Two variants defined as plain CSS classes:

**`.liquid-glass`** (subtle):
- `background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.01)` with `background-blend-mode: luminosity`
- `backdrop-filter: blur(4px)` / `-webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(4px)`
- No border; `box-shadow: inset 0 1px 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.1)`
- `position: relative; overflow: hidden`
- `::before` pseudo-element creates a gradient stroke border:
- `position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: inherit; padding: 1.4px`
- `background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.45) 0%, rgba(255,255,255,0.15) 20%, rgba(255,255,255,0) 40%, rgba(255,255,255,0) 60%, rgba(255,255,255,0.15) 80%, rgba(255,255,255,0.45) 100%)`
- Masked with `-webkit-mask: linear-gradient(#fff 0 0) content-box, linear-gradient(#fff 0 0); -webkit-mask-composite: xor; mask-composite: exclude;`
- `pointer-events: none`

**`.liquid-glass-strong`** (bolder):
- Same structure but `backdrop-filter: blur(50px)`
- `box-shadow: 4px 4px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.05), inset 0 1px 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.15)`
- `::before` gradient uses 0.5 alpha at edges, 0.2 at 20%/80%

---

### FadingVideo Component

A reusable `<video>` component accepting `src` (string or string[]), `className`, and `style`. It:
1. Starts with `opacity: 0`
2. On `loadeddata`, fades in over 500ms using `requestAnimationFrame`
3. On `timeupdate`, when remaining time <= 0.55s, fades out over 550ms
4. On `ended`, if single source: resets `currentTime` to 0, replays, fades back in. If array: advances to next index (cycling).
5. Video is `autoPlay`, `muted`, `playsInline`, `preload="auto"`

---

### BlurText Component

A word-by-word staggered blur-in animation component using Framer Motion:
- Splits `text` prop by spaces
- Each word is a `motion.span` with `display: inline-block`, `marginRight: 0.28em`
- Triggers on IntersectionObserver (threshold 0.1)
- Each word animates: `filter` from `blur(10px)` to `blur(0px)`, `opacity` 0 to 1, `y` from 50 to 0
- Duration 0.7s per word, stagger delay of 100ms per word index
- Container uses `display: flex; flexWrap: wrap; justifyContent: center; rowGap: 0.1em`

---

### Section 1: Hero

- Full viewport height (`h-screen`), `overflow-hidden`, `bg-black`
- **Background video**: Single `<FadingVideo>` with:
- `src="https://d8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/hf_20260619_191346_9d19d66e-86a4-47f7-8dc6-712c1788c3b2.mp4"`
- Positioned: `absolute left-1/2 top-0 -translate-x-1/2 object-cover object-top z-0`
- Inline style: `width: 120%; height: 120%`

- **Content** (`relative z-10, flex flex-col h-full`):

**Navbar** (fixed, `top-4 left-0 right-0 z-50`, flex between, `px-8 lg:px-16`):
- Left: `liquid-glass` circle (h-12 w-12 rounded-full) with italic "a" in `font-heading text-2xl`
- Center (hidden on mobile, `md:flex`): `liquid-glass rounded-full px-1.5 py-1.5` pill containing links ["Work", "Studio", "Services", "Journal", "Contact"] as `px-3 py-2 text-sm font-medium text-white/90 font-body` + a white CTA button "Start a Project" with ArrowUpRight icon
- Right: empty `h-12 w-12` spacer div

**Main content** (centered, `flex-1 flex flex-col items-center justify-center pt-24 px-4 text-center`):
- **Badge** (motion.div, delay 0.4): `liquid-glass rounded-full` pill with a white "New" badge inside + text "Booking Q3 2026 engagements -- limited capacity"
- **Headline** (mt-6, max-w-3xl): `<BlurText>` with text "Crafted Digital Experiences Built to Outlast Trends", classes: `text-6xl md:text-7xl lg:text-[5.5rem] font-heading italic text-white leading-[0.8] tracking-[-4px]`
- **Subtext** (motion.p, delay 0.8, mt-4): "We are a small studio of designers and engineers shaping brand-defining websites for ambitious companies. Precise typography, cinematic motion, and code you can be proud of." -- `text-sm md:text-base text-white max-w-2xl font-body font-light leading-tight`
- **CTA buttons** (motion.div, delay 1.1, mt-6, flex gap-6): "Start a Project" in `liquid-glass-strong rounded-full px-5 py-2.5` with ArrowUpRight + "Watch Showreel" plain text with Play icon
- **Stats cards** (motion.div, delay 1.3, mt-8, flex gap-4): Two `liquid-glass p-5 w-[220px] rounded-[1.25rem]` cards:
- Card 1: ClockIcon, "6 Weeks", "Average End-to-End Launch Time"
- Card 2: GlobeIcon, "140+", "Brands Shipped Across Four Continents"
- Numbers: `text-4xl font-heading italic tracking-[-1px] leading-none mt-4`

**Bottom trust bar** (motion.div, delay 1.4, flex-col items-center gap-4 pb-8):
- `liquid-glass rounded-full` pill: "Trusted by founders, operators, and creative directors worldwide"
- Logo names in a flex row (gap-12 md:gap-16): ["Aeon", "Vela", "Apex", "Orbit", "Zeno"] each as `font-heading italic text-2xl md:text-3xl tracking-tight`

- **All motion elements** use shared initial/animate: `{ filter: 'blur(10px)', opacity: 0, y: 20 }` -> `{ filter: 'blur(0px)', opacity: 1, y: 0 }`, duration 0.8s, easeOut

---

### Section 2: Capabilities

- `min-h-screen`, `overflow-hidden`, `bg-black`, relative
- **Background video**: `<FadingVideo>` with:
- `src="https://d8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/hf_20260622_093722_ccfc7ebf-182f-419f-8a62-2dc02db7dd9d.mp4"`
- `absolute inset-0 w-full h-full object-cover z-0`

- **Content** (`relative z-10 px-8 md:px-16 lg:px-20 pt-24 pb-10 flex flex-col min-h-screen`):
- **Header** (mb-auto):
- Label: `text-sm font-body text-white/80 mb-6` -- "// Capabilities"
- Heading: `font-heading italic text-6xl md:text-7xl lg:text-[6rem] leading-[0.9] tracking-[-3px]` -- "Studio craft,\nend to end"

- **Cards grid** (mt-16, `grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3 gap-6`), three cards:
1. **Design** -- Icon: ImageIcon (filled image icon), Tags: ["Brand Systems", "Art Direction", "Visual Identity", "Motion"], Body: "We shape identities and interfaces that feel unmistakably yours -- typographic systems, component libraries, and art-directed pages that scale without losing soul."
2. **Engineering** -- Icon: MovieIcon (film/clapboard), Tags: ["React", "Next.js", "Headless CMS", "Edge-Ready"], Body: "Production-grade front-ends built on modern stacks. Performant, accessible, and instrumented -- with code your team will enjoy extending long after launch."
3. **Growth** -- Icon: LightbulbIcon, Tags: ["SEO", "Analytics", "A/B Testing", "Retention"], Body: "Launch is the starting line. We partner with your team on conversion, content, and iteration loops that turn a beautiful site into a compounding asset."

- Each card: `liquid-glass rounded-[1.25rem] p-6 min-h-[360px] flex flex-col`
- Top row: icon in a nested `liquid-glass h-11 w-11 rounded-[0.75rem]` square + tags (flex-wrap, gap-1.5) right-aligned, each tag is `liquid-glass rounded-full px-3 py-1 text-[11px] text-white/90 font-body whitespace-nowrap`
- Spacer: `flex-1`
- Bottom: title in `font-heading italic text-3xl md:text-4xl tracking-[-1px] leading-none` + body in `text-sm text-white/90 font-body font-light leading-snug max-w-[32ch]`

---

### Custom SVG Icons (no external icon library needed for these)

- **ArrowUpRight**: 24x24, stroke, paths "M7 17L17 7" and "M7 7h10v10"
- **Play**: 24x24, filled polygon "6 4 20 12 6 20 6 4"
- **ClockIcon**: 24x24, stroke (1.5), circle r=9 + "M12 7v5l3 2"
- **GlobeIcon**: 24x24, stroke (1.5), circle r=9 + horizontal line + two arc paths
- **ImageIcon**: 24x24, filled Material-style image icon
- **MovieIcon**: 24x24, filled Material-style movie icon
- **LightbulbIcon**: 24x24, filled Material-style bulb icon

---

### Dependencies

- react, react-dom
- framer-motion
- tailwindcss, postcss, autoprefixer
- vite, @vitejs/plugin-react
- typescript

---

### Key Design Principles

- Everything is on a pure black (#000) background
- All text is white; subtle text uses `white/80` or `white/90`
- Liquid glass elements have near-invisible fills with gradient-stroke borders via CSS masks
- Videos cover sections as atmospheric backgrounds, fading in/out smoothly
- Typography: heading font is always italic with very tight tracking (negative), body font is light weight
- Responsive: nav links hidden on mobile, grid collapses to single column, text sizes scale with breakpoints
- Animations: staggered blur-in on load for hero content, intersection-triggered for BlurText

full_prompt:
Create a single-page dental clinic landing page using **React + Vite + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS**. No external UI libraries, no icon libraries. Everything lives in one `App.tsx` file. The page has 3 full-screen sections, a splash screen, and a fixed navbar. --- ### SETUP **Font:** "Open Sauce One" loaded via these exact links in `index.html` ``: ```html ``` **Title:** "Dental Health - Quality Healthcare" **Global CSS (index.css):** ```css @tailwind base; @tailwind components; @tailwind utilities; @layer base { html, body, #root { height: 100%; margin: 0; padding: 0; } body { font-family: 'Open Sauce One', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, sans-serif; -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; -moz-osx-font-smoothing: grayscale; } } ``` **Tailwind config:** Default, no extensions. Content: `['./index.html', './src/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}']`. --- ### IMAGE URLS (use these EXACT URLs) ```ts const HERO_IMAGE = 'https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20260624_113640_ccf3cf97-d447-425b-a134-d7b09fc743fc.png&w=1280&q=85'; const SECTION2_IMAGE = 'https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20260624_114219_414dfe80-f15c-4e25-bf52-b13721f4bd88.png&w=1280&q=85'; const SECTION3_IMG1 = 'https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20260624_115253_c19ab167-8dd5-48b4-967d-b9f0d9d6e8fb.png&w=1280&q=85'; const SECTION3_IMG2 = 'https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20260624_115237_fc519057-6e87-4abf-999a-9610b8b085b4.png&w=1280&q=85'; const SECTION3_BG = 'https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20260624_114355_752ba9e6-0942-4abb-9047-5d9bb16632e9.png&w=1280&q=85'; ``` --- ### DATA CONSTANTS ```ts const featureBars = ['Advanced Dentistry', 'High Quality Equipment', 'Friendly Staff']; const services = [ { name: 'Dental\nVeneers', num: '01', active: true }, { name: 'Dental\nCrowns', num: '02', active: false }, { name: 'Teeth\nWhitening', num: '03', active: false }, { name: 'Dental\nImplants', num: null, active: false }, ]; ``` --- ### CORE TECHNICAL CONCEPT: "MASKED CARDS" Sections 1 and 2 use a single large background image shared across multiple cards. Each card shows a different "window" into the same image, creating a cohesive mosaic effect. Implementation: **`useMaskPositions` hook:** - Takes a ref to the section container and a ref to an array of card elements. - Uses `ResizeObserver` on the section container. - For each card, computes `{ x, y, sw, sh }` where x/y is the card's top-left offset relative to the section, sw/sh is the section's width/height. **`useImageWidth` hook:** - Loads the image in a `new Image()` object. - Calculates: `renderWidth = img.naturalWidth * (sectionHeight / img.naturalHeight)`. - Returns how wide the image would be if scaled to fill the section height. **`MaskedCard` component:** - Props: `bgImage`, `position` (from useMaskPositions), `imageWidth` (from useImageWidth), `focalX` (0-1 float), `className`, `children`, `cardRef`, `style`. - Calculates `overflow = imageWidth > position.sw ? imageWidth - position.sw : 0`, then `focalOffset = overflow * focalX`. - Applies inline style: ``` backgroundImage: url(bgImage) backgroundSize: auto [position.sh]px backgroundPosition: -[position.x + focalOffset]px -[position.y]px backgroundRepeat: no-repeat ``` - `focalX` values: Section 1 mobile=0.7, desktop=0.8. Section 2 mobile=0.65, desktop=0.8. **`useIsMobile` hook:** - Listens to `window.matchMedia('(max-width: 767px)')` change events. - Returns boolean. --- ### ANIMATION: `useStaggeredReveal` hook - Takes `count` (number of elements) and `threshold` (IntersectionObserver threshold, default 0.15). - Returns `{ containerRef, getAnimStyle }`. - `containerRef` is attached to the section; when it crosses the threshold, `visible` becomes true (fires once). - `getAnimStyle(index)` returns: ```css opacity: visible ? 1 : 0 transform: visible ? 'translateY(0)' : 'translateY(24px)' transition: opacity 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) [index*120]ms, transform 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) [index*120]ms ``` --- ### SPLASH SCREEN - Fixed overlay covering viewport, `z-[100]`, white background. - Number counter displayed at **bottom-left** (`items-end justify-start`). - Counter style: `text-7xl md:text-9xl font-bold tabular-nums p-6 md:p-10 leading-none`, black text. - Counts from 0 to 100 over exactly 2000ms (20ms per step, 100 steps). - After reaching 100: wait 200ms, then set `exiting=true` which triggers `opacity-0` with `transition-opacity duration-700`. - After 900ms total from reaching 100, call `onComplete()` which removes splash from DOM. --- ### NAVBAR **Container:** `fixed top-0 left-0 right-0 z-50`, `flex items-center justify-between`, `px-4 md:px-6 py-2 md:py-3`, `bg-white/80 backdrop-blur-md`. **Logo (left side):** - Two lines stacked: "Dental" and "Health" - Wrapper: `flex flex-col` - Text: `text-xl md:text-2xl font-extrabold uppercase tracking-tight leading-none` - Second line has `-mt-1.5 md:-mt-2` for tight spacing - Below logo text: "quality healthcare" in `text-[8px] md:text-[9px] font-medium leading-none mt-1.5 md:mt-2` **Desktop nav (hidden on mobile with `hidden md:block`):** - "Menu" button: `px-6 py-3 bg-white rounded-full border border-black text-sm font-semibold`, hover: `hover:bg-black hover:text-white transition-colors duration-200` - "Dental Emergency" text: `text-sm font-semibold text-black` **Mobile hamburger (visible only on mobile with `md:hidden`):** - Container: `w-10 h-10 flex items-center justify-center`, `relative` - 3 spans, each: `absolute h-0.5 w-6 bg-black rounded-full` - title: Mindloop Landing
description: Dark monochrome landing page called Mindloop — a newsletter/content platform. Use React + Vite + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui + Framer Motion. Features real-time liquid glass refraction with chromatic lens effects, scroll-driven kinetic animations and staggered choreography with precision layout polish.
full_prompt:
Build a dark monochrome landing page called Mindloop — a newsletter/content platform. Use React + Vite + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui + Framer Motion. Fonts: Inter (sans) and Instrument Serif (serif, used for italic accent words). The entire theme is pure black (#000) background with white foreground — no colors or gradients beyond monochrome. Install hls.js and framer-motion.

Design System (index.css)
All CSS variables in HSL (no hsl() wrapper in the variable, just the values):

--background: 0 0% 0%
--foreground: 0 0% 100%
--card: 0 0% 5%
--card-foreground: 0 0% 100%
--primary: 0 0% 100%
--primary-foreground: 0 0% 0%
--secondary: 0 0% 12%
--secondary-foreground: 0 0% 85%
--muted: 0 0% 15%
--muted-foreground: 0 0% 65%
--accent: 170 15% 45%
--accent-foreground: 0 0% 100%
--border: 0 0% 20%
--input: 0 0% 18%
--ring: 0 0% 40%
--hero-subtitle: 210 17% 95%
Liquid Glass Effect (global CSS class .liquid-glass)

.liquid-glass {
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.01);
  background-blend-mode: luminosity;
  backdrop-filter: blur(4px);
  -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(4px);
  border: none;
  box-shadow: inset 0 1px 1px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1);
  position: relative;
  overflow: hidden;
}
.liquid-glass::before {
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  border-radius: inherit;
  padding: 1.4px;
  background: linear-gradient(180deg,
    rgba(255,255,255,0.45) 0%, rgba(255,255,255,0.15) 20%,
    rgba(255,255,255,0) 40%, rgba(255,255,255,0) 60%,
    rgba(255,255,255,0.15) 80%, rgba(255,255,255,0.45) 100%);
  -webkit-mask: linear-gradient(#fff 0 0) content-box, linear-gradient(#fff 0 0);
  -webkit-mask-composite: xor;
  mask-composite: exclude;
  pointer-events: none;
}
Animation Pattern
All sections use a reusable fadeUp helper with staggered delays:

const fadeUp = (delay: number) => ({
  initial: { opacity: 0, y: 20 },
  whileInView: { opacity: 1, y: 0 },
  viewport: { once: true, margin: "-100px" },
  transition: { duration: 0.6, delay, ease: "easeOut" },
});

Page Structure (top to bottom)
1. Navbar (fixed, transparent)
Left: Logo (concentric circles icon — outer w-7 h-7 with border-2 border-foreground/60, inner w-3 h-3 with border border-foreground/60) + "Mindloop" bold text.
Center-left: Nav links ["Home", "How It Works", "Philosophy", "Use Cases"] separated by • dots. Links are text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground.
Right: 3 social icons (Instagram, Linkedin, Twitter from lucide-react) in liquid-glass circular buttons (w-10 h-10 rounded-full).
No background — fully transparent, fixed top-0 z-50, padding px-8 md:px-28 py-4.

2. Hero Section (full viewport height)
Background: autoplaying looping muted MP4 video covering the entire section.
Video URL: https://d8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/hf_20260325_120549_0cd82c36-56b3-4dd9-b190-069cfc3a623f.mp4
Bottom gradient: h-64 bg-gradient-to-t from-background to-transparent for smooth fade to black.
Content (centered, z-10, pt-28 md:pt-32):
Avatar row: 3 overlapping circular avatars (-space-x-2, w-8 h-8 rounded-full border-2 border-background) + "7,000+ people already subscribed" in text-muted-foreground text-sm.

https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Anton&family=Condiment&display=swap


COLOR SYSTEM (Tailwind config)

Background: #010828 (deep dark navy blue)

cream: #EFF4FF (off-white, used for all text)

LIQUID GLASS CSS EFFECT

Applied via a .liquid-glass class. This is used on the navbar, social icon buttons, NFT cards, and card overlays:

.liquid-glass {
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.01);
  background-blend-mode: luminosity;
  backdrop-filter: blur(4px);
  -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(4px);
  border: none;
  box-shadow: inset 0 1px 1px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1);
  position: relative;
  overflow: hidden;
}
.liquid-glass::before {
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  border-radius: inherit;
  padding: 1.4px;
  background: linear-gradient(180deg,
    rgba(255,255,255,0.45) 0%, rgba(255,255,255,0.15) 20%,
    rgba(255,255,255,0) 40%, rgba(255,255,255,0) 60%,
    rgba(255,255,255,0.15) 80%, rgba(255,255,255,0.45) 100%);
  -webkit-mask: linear-gradient(#fff 0 0) content-box, linear-gradient(#fff 0 0);
  -webkit-mask-composite: xor;
  mask-composite: exclude;
  pointer-events: none;
}

### SECTION 1: Hero (Video Background + Overlaid UI)

**Desktop (non-touch):**
- Videos are NOT auto-played. They are scrubbed based on cursor X position via `requestAnimationFrame`.
- Dead zone: `Math.max(30, width * 0.05)` pixels from center
- If cursor is in dead zone, keep current video at `currentTime = 0`
- If cursor moves left of dead zone: show RIGHT video, scrub it based on distance from center-left-edge to left edge
- If cursor moves right of dead zone: show LEFT video, scrub it based on distance from center+deadzone to right edge
- `activeSideRef` tracks which side was last active, only changes when cursor exceeds dead zone
- Progress calculation: `(distance from dead zone edge) / (available range)` mapped to `0...video.duration`

  - For each row `r`, compute primary column: `a = (r * 2 + (r % 2)) % cols`
  - Place one image at column `a`
  - Every 3rd row (`r % 3 === 0`), place a second image at `b = (a + 2) % cols` (or `(a+1)%cols` if same as a)
  - Empty cells get `-1` (rendered as empty spacer divs)

#### Card Behavior
- Each card has class `bp-card`, `will-change: transform`
- `transform: scale(0)` initially
- `transform-origin`: cards in left half of grid get `right bottom`, right half get `left bottom`
- Scale is computed per-frame in RAF based on card's vertical position:
  - **Enter**: `Math.min(1, (vh - top) / (vh * 0.6))` -- scales from 0 to 1 as it enters viewport
  - **Exit**: `Math.min(1, bottom / (vh * 0.4))` -- scales from 1 to 0 as it exits top
  - Final scale: `Math.min(enter, exit)`
  - If card is fully off-screen (bottom <= 0 or top >= vh): `scale(0)`

#### Scroll Phases (RAF-based, NOT scroll events)
- **Phase 1** (scrollY 0 to vh): Panel slides up. Cards are computed with panelOffset = `vh - scrollY`
- **Phase 2** (scrollY > vh): Panel is fixed at top. Inner wrapper translates up: `translateY(-(scrollY - vh))`. Cards recomputed with phase2 offset.
- **Outro** (scrollY > vh + maxScroll): White overlay fades in, product info slides up by `outroOffset` px, "view" button scales from 0 to 1, footer fades in. Progress: `(scrollY - vh - maxScroll) / (vh - 100)`

#### Spacer Height Calculation
- Set dynamically: `vh + maxScroll + 2 * vh` where `maxScroll = wrapScrollHeight - vh`

---

### CSS (index.css)

```css
@import "tailwindcss";

.bp-card {
  will-change: transform;
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .bp-card {
    will-change: auto;
  }
}
```

---

### Responsive Breakpoints
- **Mobile**: < 640px
- **Tablet**: 640px - 1024px
- **Desktop**: >= 1024px

---

### Key Design Principles
- All text overlays use `mix-blend-mode: exclusion` to remain visible against both light and dark backgrounds
- No visible scroll bar interaction -- entirely RAF-driven position tracking
- `pointer-events-none` on all overlaid UI elements
- `user-select: none` on root container
- Videos hidden (`visibility: hidden`) once scroll passes first viewport height
- Circle symbol randomizes on scroll (throttled to 80ms)
- Entry animations staggered: logo (0s), nav (0.15s), caption (0.3s), product info (0.45s)

full_prompt:
# Prompt: MK Consulting legal studio hero ("Rust Orange")

Build a single-file, one-screen **legal-studio hero** for a fictional firm, **MK Consulting** ("Legal studio for creatives"). Use plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JS, with no framework and no build step. The look is street-art industrial: a burnt-orange graffiti concrete wall and a giant condensed white "MK CONSULTING" title. Below it, a huge rusted steel ring hangs from four chains, with ten construction workers standing on its rim and orange graffiti sprayed along its side.

## Media

- **Wall:** `https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/a9f1e939-234a-4481-9706-3b0675e7aed2.webp` (3344×1882). Orange concrete with darker sprayed graffiti shapes and drips; cover the page.
- **Ring:** `https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/f14add82-809a-41e1-a456-f47b8e57984b.webp` (1446×1685, transparent). The riveted rusty ring is seen slightly from above, with four chains rising to one shackle and workers in hard hats on the rim.
- **Rule:** the scene is still. Only the UI animates.

## Frame and scaling

- **Units:** design units `--u` from a 1672×941 reference (full width).
- **Title row:** the title and nav pin to the top.
- **Bottom group:** the ring and tagline form a group that grows into any spare height and is centred.
- **Portrait:** a single-column layout.

## Type and colour

- **Title:** Anton (288.6u, white, each glyph pinned to its measured box).
- **Nav:** Roboto Condensed, uppercase, white, with thin 1.4u rules between items.
- **Tagline:** Big Shoulders Display 900, uppercase.
- **Graffiti:** Permanent Marker.
- **Colours:** text white, page `#1e0a00` behind the image, graffiti orange gradient `#C2410C` → `#F97316` → `#FB923C` with an orange glow.

## Layout

- **Nav:** spread across the top edge, "ABOUT US — SERVICES — OUR CASES — BLOG — CONTACTS — VACANCIES", with flexible hairline rules between items.
- **Title:** "MK CONSULTING" spans the full width under the nav.
- **Ring:** hangs centred below the title, about 886u wide; the chains rise behind the title letters.
- **Graffiti:** "WE BUILD YOUR CASE" in spray-paint lettering follows the curve of the ring's front band, using an SVG `textPath` on a quadratic arc with a grainy turbulence and glow filter.
- **Tagline:** "LEGAL STUDIO FOR / CREATIVES" centred under the ring.

## Motion (UI)

- **Entrance:**
  - The nav fades in, then the title letters wipe up one by one.
  - The ring fades in.
  - The graffiti draws left to right with a clip.
  - The tagline lines wipe up.
- **Magnet ring:** the hanging ring (with its workers, chains and graffiti, as one layer) follows the mouse slightly, like a magnet.
  - **Pivot:** it swings from the point where the chains fade out at the top (`transform-origin: 50% 33%`), so the chains stay attached.
  - **Pull:** measure the pointer's offset from the ring's centre (50% across, 66% down the ring box). The pull fades smoothly to zero beyond about the ring's width. Up close it moves toward the pointer by up to 34px (vertical movement at 45% of horizontal) and leans up to 3.5° toward it, pendulum style: pointer on the right swings the bottom right.
  - **Easing:** each frame eases toward the target with a frame-rate-independent factor `1 − e^(−dt/140ms)`, so it glides with no jitter, and drifts back to rest when the pointer leaves the window.
  - **Clock:** time comes from a long Web Animation clock rather than wall-clock time.
  - **Limits:** only on fine, hover-capable pointers; off on touch and for reduced motion.
- **Hover:** nav links dim to 70%.
- **Reduced motion:** no entrance and no magnet.

## Phones

- **Nav:** wraps into two compact rows.
- **Title:** stacks as "MK / CONSULTING".
- **Ring:** shows its full hoist chain.
- **Tagline:** sits at the bottom.

## Acceptance check (1440×960)

- The orange graffiti wall fills the page and MK CONSULTING spans the top.
- The rusty ring with workers hangs below on chains, with "WE BUILD YOUR CASE" sprayed along its band.
- The tagline is centred beneath it.
- **Content:** no real brands and no gibberish graffiti.

Over it the content scrolls up normally: first only the scene, then a big 4-line headline rising up the train's axis, then a mirrored features block, and then the clouds take over and fade into a plain text testimonial section.

## Media

- **Pull-up clip:** one clip, 1920×1080, 24 fps, 5.04 s, no audio. Encoded with a keyframe every 4 frames so it seeks instantly.
  - **1080p:** https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/e02bb27f-80d8-445f-a03e-1b609dac4261.mp4

- **Poster:** the clip's first frame, https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/5e018553-cb8a-420a-819f-fcdfa08e5df0.jpg
- **Clip content:**
  - 0–2.3 s: the camera climbs over the train, which stays on the vertical centre line, with wisps of mist.
  - From about 2.3 s: white clouds slide in from the edges.
  - Last frame: almost all white/grey cloud.
- **Rule:** the video is never played, looped or faded. It is only scrubbed (`currentTime`). Nothing in the scene is drawn or animated in code.

## Type and colour

- **Headline:** Exo 2 ExtraBold 800, uppercase.
- **UI text:** Public Sans 700 for titles and the eyebrow, 400 for body.
- **Colours:**

## Scale and structure

- **Unit:** the design is drawn on a 1280×800 frame. `u = min(100vh/800, 100vw/716)`. 800 design px equals one viewport height, so vertical positions are written as `N/8 vh`.
- **Track:** `.track` (relative, height set by JS). Inside it:
  - `.scene`: `position:sticky; top:0; height:100vh` (100lvh). It holds the `<video>` (object-fit cover), and a very light top/bottom tint (black at 2–12%).
  - `.content`: an absolute layer the full height of the track, holding the scrolling blocks.

## Scrolling blocks (desktop, positions from the top of the track)

- **Intro, top 940/8 vh** (enters after 140 design px of scroll). Centred, 1280u wide:
  - eyebrow "WHY US": 7.4u, tracking .304em
  - headline "LOGISTICS / THAT WORKS / AS HARD AS / YOU DO.": 56u on a 62u line, one span per line, nowrap

  - a body of 12.3u on a 15.4u line, three lines

  | 2 | 1759/8 vh | right-aligned, 88u left of the axis | left-aligned, 88u right of it |
