  1. **One point of contact** (dotted ring around a white globe): "No more chasing multiple vendors. One / team manages your entire end-to-end flow, / origin to destination."
  2. **Full supply chain visibility** (three stepped container blocks): "Track your freight in real time and get / proactive updates before issues become / delays."
  3. **Compliance you can trust** (dotted ring around a white disc with a dark check): "Licensed customs brokers keep your / shipments moving within every regulatory / requirement, border to border."
  4. **Competitive, transparent pricing** (bold "$" stroke): "No hidden fees. Clear, competitive pricing / backed by responsive sales support / throughout the shipment."
  5. **Fast issue resolution** (double chevron): "When something unexpected happens, we / do not point fingers, we solve it. Our team / acts at once to protect your timeline."

## Scroll → clip mapping (JS)

- **Track length:** `end = lastBlock.bottom + 0.75 × viewport`, and track height = `end + viewport`.
- **Progress:** `p = clamp((scrollY − track.top) / end)`.
- **Two-part mapping:** `knee = lastBlock.bottom / end`.
  - While `p < knee`, clip progress = `p / knee × 0.46`, so the camera only climbs over the train while text is on screen.
  - After that, it runs from 0.46 to 1, so the clouds take over once the last block has left.
- **Time:** target time = progress × (duration − 1/48).
- **Smoothing:** each frame, `cur += (target − cur) × 0.22`. Set `currentTime` only when the video isn't already seeking and the difference is more than 1/60 s, and re-seek on `seeked`.
- **Recorder mode (`?rec=1`):** a 6.5 s Web Animation drives the progress: hold to 3%, one even ease (cubic-bezier .45,.05,.55,.95) to 94%, then hold. It runs past the end of the track by 0.9 viewport so the testimonial section scrolls in. `window.__recTime(video, t)` scrolls the page to that progress and returns the matching clip time, so a frame-by-frame recorder is deterministic.

## After the clouds: testimonial section (text only)

- **Placement:** a `<section class="trust">` right after the track, pulled up 34vh over the end of the sticky scene. It starts with a 34vh gradient from transparent to `#e2dedd`, so the white clouds run straight into the page. Ink `#141516`.
- **Container:** max 1120px wide, centred, 64px side gutters, 140px bottom padding.
- **Header:** a two-column grid (1fr and 300px).
  - Left: "TRUSTED / BY BUSINESSES / ACROSS THE REGION" in Display 800 at clamp(34px, 4.4vw, 60px), line-height 1. The last line is grey `#8f8b8a`.
  - Right: a 13px note at 70% ink: "From first-time importers to high-volume shippers, our customers stay because every consignment is treated like it matters."
  - A 1px rule (ink at 16%) under the header.
- **Quotes:** three rows, each a grid of 260px and 1fr, 44px vertical padding, with a 1px rule under each. No photos.
  - Left: the name in 13px bold uppercase, the role in 12px at 60% ink.
  - Right: the quote in UI 400 at clamp(17px, 1.6vw, 21px), line-height 1.42, max 680px.
  - Thomas Reid, Director, Harbour Fit Group: "My business would not function without this team. They treat every consignment on its own merits, and our account managers know our business well enough to answer before we ask. We have never had that from a bigger carrier."
  - Ana Park, Supply Chain Lead, Northline Projects: "As a first-time shipper on a major infrastructure job, we were in unfamiliar territory. They planned the whole route with us, flagged every risk early, and our first delivery reached site on the day they promised."
  - Liam Carter, Operations Manager, Coastline Foods: "One contact, one dashboard, no surprises. When a vessel slipped two days, we heard about it before our customers did, and the new plan was already in place."
- **Portrait:** the header and each quote stack to one column (18px and 14px gaps), 22px side gutters.

## Portrait (≤ 609px wide, or any portrait aspect)

- **Unit:** `u = min(100vw/390, 1.6px)`.
- **Content:** one centred column with 112vh top padding:
  - headline at clamp(34px, 46u, 72px)
  - each feature centred with its icon above, the first 24vh below the headline, then 16vh apart
  - title lines and body lines flow inline
- **Overflow:** no sideways scroll.

## Acceptance check (1440×960)

- **On load:** only the train close-up.
- **Headline:** rises up the train's axis and exits the top.
- **Features:** the 2×2 block and the centred fifth block scroll through, mirrored across the train, while the camera climbs.
- **End:** once the last block has gone, clouds roll in, the frame ends in white cloud, and the testimonial section rises out of it.

title: Freight Services Hero
description: Single-file scroll-driven freight hero for a fictional freight group, KV, in plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JS, with no framework and no build step. It's a clean product-render story on a white page. Features scroll-driven kinetic animations and staggered choreography, cinematic looping background video integration with precision layout polish.
full_prompt:
# Prompt: KV freight services scroll hero

Build a single-file **scroll-driven freight hero** for a fictional freight group, **KV**, in plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JS, with no framework and no build step. It's a clean product-render story on a white page.

1. A teal reach-stacker lifts a navy container off a stack, turns, and lowers it onto a black semi-truck's trailer.
2. The camera pulls back and a black band rises until the truck sits on its top edge.
3. Huge light-grey "OUR SERVICES" letters slide past *behind* the truck while a dark-band strip (a headline, then five service cards) slides in from the right.

Scrolling drives everything. The scene is one sticky viewport.

## Media

- **Handling clip:** one scrubbed clip, a continuous 4.04s shot at 24fps (97 frames), muted, every 4th frame a keyframe for fast seeking.
  - 1080p: https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/409763c0-95f4-49d3-a601-dc564d55072b.mp4
  - 720p, used at 900px wide and below: https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/b3718419-7a0a-478d-bfb0-0ff8bef7f3f7.mp4
  - Poster (first frame): https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/2307e4bf-be39-42b4-b579-e168aeccabf0.jpg
- **Clip content:** pure white background with a flat near-black ground band (#111). Its top edge sits at 82.9% of the frame height until about 3.1s.
  - The stacker lifts, turns toward camera and lowers the container onto the arriving truck.
  - The spreader releases and leaves top-left.
  - The camera pulls back, and by 3.75s the band edge is at 44.8%, with the truck's wheels on it. The rig spans about 16–66% of the frame width.
  - The last ~0.3s holds.
- **Rule:** the vehicles are never drawn or moved in code; all their motion is in the clip. No opacity transitions on the video. It is never played, only scrubbed.

## Type and colour

- **Anton** for the big caps (headline, card titles, giant letters).
- **Archivo** (variable, 400–600) for body, nav and pill.
- **JetBrains Mono** 400 for the speed readout.
- Self-host latin woff2.
- **Colours:** white #fff, ink and band #111, cobalt #2f63ff, giant letters #e9e9e9.
- **Unit:** u = min(100vw/1440, 100vh/960).

## Structure

- **Track:** `.track` (white), whose height is set by JS to (1 + A + B) × viewport.
  - A = 2.4 viewports for the clip.
  - B = (strip width + 0.45 × vw) / vw × 1.1 viewports for the services strip.
- **Nav:** absolute at the top of the track, so it scrolls away.
  - Left: "KV" (Archivo 600, 30u, tracking −.06em).
  - Right: "→ Menu", "Follow", and an outline pill "Work with us" (Archivo 500, 10u, uppercase, tracking .1em).
- **Scene:** `.scene` is sticky at top:0, 100vh (100lvh), overflow hidden. Its background is white above and #111 below a line placed inside the clip, which only matters where the clip doesn't cover the screen.
- **Layers, bottom to top:**
  1. **The `<video>`**, absolutely sized by JS.
     - Wide screens: cover (scale = max(vw/1920, vh/1080), centred).
     - Portrait or narrow screens (below 768px, or vw ≤ vh): width 155vw, horizontally positioned so 40% of the frame sits at mid-screen, and vertically so the final band edge lands at 36% of the viewport.
  2. **Giant letters:** "OUR SERVICES" in Anton at 330u, line-height .8, #e9e9e9, nowrap. Its bottom sits on the final band edge (JS writes `--edge-px` = clip top + 0.448 × clip height). It has **`mix-blend-mode: darken`**, so it only shows where the clip is white. The truck and container, whose silver tops out around #e5, always win, so the letters read as behind the truck. Phones: 180u.
  3. **Speed readout:** top-left (26u, 52u), "NN KM/H" in mono at 10.5u. It shows the smoothed scroll speed (|Δy|/Δt ÷ 32, capped at 99, two digits) and appears once the truck has settled.
  4. **Band:** from `--edge-px` to the bottom, holding the horizontal strip and the "Our services" outline pill. The pill sits centred 36u from the bottom; once the truck settles it fades and rises 24px into place.

## The strip (dark band, slides left)

- **Placement:** a flex row, top 76u, gap 120u, white text.
- **Lead block** (gap 64u):
  - Headline "EVERYTHING YOUR / FREIGHT NEEDS. / UNDER ONE GROUP." in Anton 64u, line-height .98. The third line is cobalt.
  - Beside it, a 250u column of two small paragraphs (Archivo 12u, white at 62%):
    - "From air to sea, from customs clearance to the last mile, we bring decades of practice to every freight discipline."
    - "One integrated network means one partner, one point of contact and full visibility from origin to destination."
- **Five cards**, each 270u wide with 30u side padding and a 1px divider (white at 12%) on the left; the first has no divider. Each has a 38u white line icon, a two-line Anton title at 26u, and Archivo body at 12.4u:
  - **Air freight** (plane): "Express, priority and deferred options across global lanes, booked and tracked end to end."
  - **Ocean freight** (ship): "FCL and LCL sailings on every major trade lane, with carrier choice based on cost and transit time."
  - **Customs brokerage** (document with check): "Licensed in-house brokers for classification, duties and inspections, so goods clear first time."
  - **Warehousing and 3PL** (warehouse): "Bonded and general storage, pick and pack, and distribution that plugs straight into transport."
  - **Project cargo** (crane hook and load): "Oversized and heavy-lift moves, engineered, permitted and escorted from factory to foundation."
- **Card reveal:** title and body use a background-clip:text gradient: white up to (s − 34%), cobalt at (s − 6%), transparent at (s + 26%). Here s = clamp((0.98 − cardLeft/vw) / 0.3, −0.4, 1.6) × 100%, so each card's text sweeps in from blue to white as it travels in from the right.

## Scroll mapping (JS, one rAF loop)

- **Clip time:** q = clamp(scrollY / (A·vh)), and target time = q × (duration − 1/48). Ease toward it each frame (cur += (target − cur) × 0.2). Seek only when the video isn't already seeking and the difference is more than 1/60s, and re-seek on `seeked`.
- **Settled flag:** when q ≥ 0.94, set `--ph = 1`. This shows the readout and the pill.
- **Strip:** r = clamp((scrollY − A·vh) / (B·vh)).
  - Strip translateX = vw − r × (stripWidth + 0.45·vw).
  - Giant letters translateX = vw − r × (lettersWidth + vw).
- **Recorder mode (`?rec=1`):** an 11s Web Animation drives progress (hold to 4%, ease cubic-bezier(.4,.05,.55,.95) to 96%, then hold). `window.__recTime(video, t)` scrolls to that progress, updates the readout from the scripted speed, and returns the clip time, so a frame-by-frame recorder is deterministic.

## Phones (below 768px, or any portrait screen)

- u = min(100vw/430, 1.4px). The clip is framed as above, with white above and black below it.
- **Strip:** top 44u, gap 56u, 22px left padding. The lead block stacks the headline (46u) over the paragraphs (300u wide, 13u).
- **Cards:** 250u wide, titles 26u, body 13u.
- **Readout:** 11px at (20px, 22px). The nav hides "Follow".
- **Overflow:** no sideways scroll.

## Acceptance check (1440×960)

- **On load:** the stacker holds the navy container over the stack, under the KV nav.
- **Handling:** scrolling lifts the container, turns the stacker, loads the truck, and pulls back until the truck sits on the black band.
- **Services:** "OUR SERVICES" then slides past behind the truck, with no letters showing through the container or cab. The headline enters from the right, followed by the five cards sweeping from blue to white. The KM/H number follows scroll speed.
- **Scrubbing:** scrolling back reverses everything.
- **Content:** no real brands or logos.

# Prompt: Mindora mental-health hero

Build a single-file, one-screen **hero for a fictional AI mental-health app, Mindora**. Use plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JS, with no framework and no build step. # Prompt: Gridwork Co create-account hero

Build a single-file, one-screen **create-account onboarding hero** for a fictional freelance marketplace, **Gridwork Co**. Use plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JS, with no framework and no build step. The look is fresh and botanical: a large photo card of a young woman tending plants in a bright glass greenhouse on the left, and a clean off-white form on the right asking "What tools do you use?", with sage and forest-green accents.

## Media

- **Photo:** `https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/61db05ee-e08b-47b7-8ab6-541c5c510237.jpg` (1356×1528). A woman with dark hair in a low bun, a cream knit sweater and an olive apron, working with leafy plants in a sunlit greenhouse with hanging plants.
- **Motion:** a muted 10s loop of the same shot plays over the photo with identical cover rules: `https://d2ol7oe51mr4n9.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/221f7a06-5ecc-40b6-9ece-26f1f982db64.mp4` (1020×1150).
  - The camera dollies in and orbits around her until she faces the lens, while her hands lift and part the leaves and the hanging plants sway. The clip plays forward then reversed, so it loops without a jump.
  - Fade it in (0.8s) once its first frame is ready.
- **Rule:** nothing in the photo is drawn or animated in code. Only the UI animates.

## Scale

- **Units:** every size is in reference pixels of a 1447×1087 artboard, multiplied by `--u = clamp(.7px, min(100vw/1447, 100vh/1087), 2.4px)`.
- **Grid:** the shell fills the viewport. Columns are `minmax(0,1fr)` for the photo and `max(508.7u, 45%)` for the form. Padding is 11.5u top, 15.7u bottom and 15.6u left, so the photo card keeps an even margin to the edges.

## Type and colour

- **Font:** **Inter** 400/500/600/700 everywhere.
- **Colours:**
  - page `#FDFEFD`
  - ink `#101A20`; secondary text `#6E767C`, `#8A9196`
  - lines `#DCE0DD`
  - forest green `#1F4D37` (wordmark, log-in link) and `#1D4A35` (selected border and check)
  - button `#20513A`, hover `#2A6247`
  - sage tint `#ECF2EC` for selected cards

## Photo card (left)

- **Shape:** fills the left column. Top-left corner square; the other corners have a 24u radius. Photo `object-fit:cover`, position 50% 22%.
- **Tile pattern** in the top-left corner, on a 61u grid (4×4 cells):
  - six frosted tiles (61u, radius 15u, `rgba(255,255,255,.5)` with an 8u blur) at column/row (2,0), (3,1), (0,2), (2,2), (1,3) and (3,3)
  - page-coloured cut-outs: cell (0,0) and the rounded notches along the card edge, so the pattern reads as squares punched out of the corner
- **Bottom glass:** a 360u band with a 22u backdrop blur and a forest tint gradient (0 → .30 → .22), masked in from transparent.
- **Testimonial:** white, 40u side padding.
  - Quote: Inter 500, 31.35u on 45.5u, max 772u wide: "I landed multiple paid projects within a couple of days–way more traction than I ever got elsewhere. Definitely my go-to freelance platform now!"
  - Name "Sofia Hernández" (600, 20.5u) and role "Garden Designer, Portland, OR" (500, 16.25u).
  - Two 59u round outline arrow buttons (white 1.5u circle and arrow) at the bottom right, 31u apart.

## Form (right)

- **Column:** 432u wide, centred vertically and horizontally.
- **Wordmark:** a two-leaf mark (dark and mid forest green, with a thin pale vein) and "Gridwork Co" in Inter 600, 24u, forest green.
- **Heading:** "What tools do you use?" in Inter 700, 26u, tracking −.65u, 50.5u below the wordmark. Below it, "We’ll connect you with the best jobs." (17.15u, grey).
- **Tool grid:** 2×3, 34u below the subline, gaps 19u × 18u. Each card is 130.5u tall, radius 11u, with a 1u inset line. Contents:

  - a 20u round checkbox at the top right
- **The six tools use their real app icons:**

  - **Framer:** the white glyph on black
  - **Adobe XD:** pink `#FF61F6` "Xd" on plum `#470137`
  - **Webflow:** the white W on blue `#146EF5`
  - **Relume:** the dark hexagon-cube on pink
  - **Canva:** the teal-to-violet gradient circle with the white script, on white
- **Selected state:** Figma, Webflow and Relume start selected. A selected card gets the sage fill, a 2u forest border and a filled forest checkbox with a white tick. Cards toggle on click.
- **Button:** a full-width 53u pill "Create account", 43u below the grid. Below it, "Already have an account? **Log in**" with the link in forest green, underlined.

## Motion (UI)

- **Entrance:** one Web Animations timeline, about 2s, started when the fonts are ready. The photo and its pattern never move.
  - The quote wipes up out of a top-down clip; its footer follows.
  - The wordmark rises, then the heading wipes up and the subline rises.
  - The tool cards rise row by row (155ms per row, 55ms per column), then the button, then the log-in line.
- **Hover:** the arrows get a faint white fill; the button lightens.
- **Reduced motion:** no entrance and no video.

## Tablet and phone

  - a short photo card with the quote clamped to 3 lines
  - compact horizontal tool cards in 2 columns

full_prompt:
Build one standalone HTML file, a single full-viewport hero for Atelier Unit. No external CSS, no frameworks, no extra sections, no headings outside the page itself. Output only the complete document. Use these values exactly. Do not round, rename classes, restack the layout, or substitute a different video.

Document
- lang="en"
- charset utf-8
- viewport: width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover
- theme-color #0d0905
- title: Atelier Unit — Craftwork, Technology, Design
- html and body: margin 0, padding 0, height 100%, background #130e09

Fonts
- Family name "AU Grotesk"
- Regular: @font-face src url(assets/au-grotesk-regular.woff2) format("woff2"), weight 400, font-display:block
- Bold: @font-face src url(assets/au-grotesk-bold.woff2) format("woff2"), weight 700, font-display:block
- These are a Latin subset of TeX Gyre Heros (Helvetica / Neue Haas grotesque). Do not swap in Inter, Roboto, or a Google font.
- Body stack: "AU Grotesk", "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
- color #ffffff
- -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; -moz-osx-font-smoothing: grayscale; text-rendering: geometricPrecision; font-kerning: normal
- links and buttons inherit color and font; links have no underline; buttons have no background, border, or padding, cursor pointer
- :focus-visible is a 1px solid white outline, offset 3px

Scale
Design frame is 1280 × 800. One design pixel equals --u, the largest uniform scale that fits the whole frame in the viewport.
- --vh: 1vh, and 1dvh where supported
- --ink: #ffffff
- --base-bot: #130e09
- --rule: rgba(255,255,255,0.115)
- --grid: rgba(255,255,255,0.0265)
- --menu-bg: #fcfcfc
- --menu-ink: #141414
- --small-min: 10px; at min-height 480px, --small-min becomes 11.28px
- --u: min(100vw / 1280, var(--vh) * 100 / 800)
- --small: max(var(--small-min), 12.6 * var(--u))
Heights map 1:1 to the screen. Extra width is absorbed by edge-anchored elements and the extended backdrop. Box-sizing border-box on everything.

Stage
.hero is position relative, isolation isolate, overflow hidden, width 100%, height 100vh and 100dvh, min-height 320px.
Its background is this exact vertical gradient:
linear-gradient(180deg, #0d0905 0%, #0f0a05 15%, #0d0a05 30%, #0d0905 45%, #0e0a06 60%, #0f0c07 75%, #130e08 90%, #130e09 100%)

Background video
Use this CloudFront URL and no other asset, local or remote:
https://d8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/hf_20261005_143740_52dbf3ef-ea20-4594-a1ad-91d6c2970159.mp4
It is a muted, looping, autoplaying, playsinline video of a figure seen from behind in a dark coat and a polished black mirrored helmet, with a thin amber arc behind the shoulders and low haze. Do not replace it with an image.

.hero__photo is role="presentation", position absolute, z-index -3.
- --pw: max(min(100vw, 1536 * var(--u)), var(--vh) * 160)
- --fade: clamp(0px, 100vw - var(--pw), var(--pw) * .08)
- top: var(--photo-top, 0px)
- left: (100vw - var(--pw)) * .5293, so the helmet stays at 52.93% across
- width var(--pw), aspect-ratio 16/10
- horizontal mask: transparent, black at --fade, black until 100% - --fade, transparent
The video fills the plate: display block, width and height 100%, object-fit cover, object-position center center.

Grid
48 hairline columns over the whole hero, z-index -1, pointer-events none.
Each column is an empty <i>. A 2px line sits at left: calc(75% - .5px), full height, color var(--grid). The first line is at three quarters of a column (20px at 1280).
Mask the grid with radial-gradient(ellipse 62% 95% at 50% 62%, rgba(0,0,0,0.83) 0%, #000 100%) so the lines recede behind the subject and headline.

Top bar
Logo: an <a href="#" class="logo" aria-label="Atelier Unit — home"> containing an inline SVG, viewBox 0 0 142.60 30.00, shape-rendering geometricPrecision, fill var(--logo-ink, #ffffff). Seven white squares, each 8.2 × 8.2:
- 0.00, 0.00
- 19.20, 0.00
- 76.80, 0.00
- 115.20, 0.00
- 57.60, 10.90
- 134.40, 10.90
- 0.00, 21.80
Logo position: left 20.65 * --u, top 12.8 * --u, width max(142.60 * --u, 96px).

title: AXON
description: Single full-screen dark page: a GPU particle cloud shaped like a sculpted logo form fills the viewport, stirred by the cursor through a fluid simulation, with a thin monospace UI layer on top (brand, tag chips, a scrollable column of video cards on the left, a text column on the right, a round counter top-right). Pure black background. Features interactive cursor/mouse tracking and scrub-driven interaction, hardware-accelerated WebGL / Three.js 3D rendering with precision layout polish.
full_prompt:
# AXON — Motion research hub: recreation brief

Build a single full-screen dark page: a GPU particle cloud shaped like a sculpted logo form fills the viewport, stirred by the cursor through a fluid simulation, with a thin monospace UI layer on top (brand, tag chips, a scrollable column of video cards on the left, a text column on the right, a round counter top-right). Pure black background. No scrolling of the page itself.

## 1. Media

| Use | URL | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Card 1 video | https://pub-86dc5b5484314368ac5436a674b0d919.r2.dev/aaaf/oraciteslArea.mp4 | "Lattices / zone" |
| Card 2 video | https://pub-86dc5b5484314368ac5436a674b0d919.r2.dev/aaaf/facet-glass-hero.mp4 | "Prism / shell" |
| Card 3 video | https://pub-86dc5b5484314368ac5436a674b0d919.r2.dev/aaaf/stellarmind-hero.mp4 | "Nebular / loop" |
| Card 4 video | https://pub-86dc5b5484314368ac5436a674b0d919.r2.dev/aaaf/thedropthroughArea.mp4 | "Fall / forward" |
| Particle sprite matcap | 64×64 PNG, a soft grey sphere shading (a generic matcap). Any soft spherical matcap works; embed as a data URI. | Sampled per point sprite |
| three.js | https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.150.1/build/three.min.js | UMD build, global `THREE` |

All videos: `autoplay muted loop playsinline preload="metadata"`, `object-fit: cover`.

## 2. Fonts

System monospace stack, no web font: `"SF Mono", "Menlo", "Consolas", "Liberation Mono", monospace`. All UI text is uppercase, 13 px, line-height 1.35, letter-spacing 0.02em.

## 3. Head and tokens

- `<title>AXON..</title>`
- `<meta name="description" content="AXON is a motion research studio: an open logbook of real-time rendering studies in particles, fluids and signed surfaces.">`
- Viewport meta, charset UTF-8.

```
--accent: #aa88ff   (headings, chip highlight)
--text:   #dddddd
--muted:  #8a8a8a
--chip:   #1c1c1c
--line:   #2a2a2a
body background #000, html/body height 100%, overflow hidden
```

## 4. Layers

1. `canvas#bg` fixed, full viewport, z-index 0. WebGL renderer, pixel ratio min(devicePixelRatio, 2), clear colour black.
2. `.ui` fixed inset 0, z-index 1, `pointer-events: none` (links and the card list re-enable pointer events). Text blocks use `mix-blend-mode: plus-lighter` so they glow over the particles; the video cards do not blend.

## 5. UI DOM, in order, desktop measurements

**Brand** `.brand` absolute top 24 left 24, flex row gap 14.
- A 40×40 SVG mark: 18.5 px radius circle stroke white 1.6, plus a white 8-point star polygon inside.
- Name "AXON" 20 px white; subtitle "Motion research" 11 px muted, margin-top 2.

**Counter** `.counter` absolute top 24 right 24: 44×44 circle, 1 px `--line` border, background #0a0a0a, text "07" 14 px white centred.

**Tags** `.tags` absolute top 120 left 24 width 320, flex wrap gap 6. Chips: background `--chip`, padding 5px 9px, 11 px, colour #cfcfcf. First chip "All" is active: background #e6e6e6, colour #000. Chips in order: All, Light, Physics, Fluids, Grid, Audio, Volumes, Particles, Capture, Render.

**Card list** `.list` absolute top 250 left 24 bottom 0 width 320, vertical scroll, scrollbar hidden. Each `.card`: padding 18px 0, 1 px top border `--line`.
- `.thumb` height 160, radius 2, background #0a0a0a, overflow hidden, video cover-fitted.
- `.meta` flex space-between gap 16, margin-top 10, 12 px. Left column white, right column muted and right-aligned; both two lines (`white-space: pre-line`).
- Cards: Lattices / zone · Ambient light / study — Prism / shell · Dispersion hero / render — Nebular / loop · Procedural hero / sequence — Fall / forward · Dolly track / study.

**Text column** `.about` absolute right 90, top 50% translateY(-50%), width 380. Blocks separated by 2.2em. Headings `h2` 13 px accent colour, margin-bottom 1em. Paragraphs justified, margin-bottom 1em. Lists `list-style: inside`. Links block-level, underlined, margin 4px 0, hover opacity .7 over 300 ms.

```
[info]
Studies are published as they are built and may not run on every device.

[aims]
An open logbook of real-time rendering research: surfaces, fluids, fields, and the little tools we build to shape them.
It is here to keep the work in view and to give each new project a place to grow.

[exploring]
• Signed surfaces  • Cursor turbulence  • Compute passes  • Type in 3D space

[connect]
Index -> AXON              (href "#")
Mail -> hello@axonlab.dev  (mailto)
```

## 6. Responsive

- ≤1100 px: text column right 24, width 320.
- ≤760 px: hide `.list` and `.tags`; text column becomes left 24 / right 24 / bottom 24, no transform, paragraphs left-aligned.

## 7. Particle system (the hero)

**Scene.** Perspective camera FOV 30, near 0.1, far 1000, base position (-1.17, 0, 6) looking at the origin. A group holds the points at position (0.343, 0.16, -1), rotation in degrees (-28.4, 390, 4.92), scale (5, 5, 6).

**Gaze camera.** Each frame the target position is base + (mouse.x mapped 0..width → -1..1) × (-1) on x and (mouse.y mapped 0..height → -1..1) × 2 on y; the camera lerps to it at 0.05 and looks at the origin.

**Count.** 262,144 points on desktop (512×512 position texture), 16,384 on mobile. Each point has a `random` vec4 attribute in 0..1 and looks up its position from a float RGBA texture using `position.xy` as UV.

**Simulation (ping-pong float render target, one fullscreen pass per frame).** Inputs: current position texture, origin texture (initial random positions uniform in [-1,1]³), random attribs, `time` (s), `HZ` (= dt × 60), fluid velocity texture, fluid density texture, projection matrix (camera projection × inverse camera world), model matrix (group world), normal matrix (camera world). Per particle:

```
if (length(pos) > 0.7) pos /= 2.0;
pos += curlNoise(pos * 0.1 + time * 0.05) * 1.0 * 0.0002 * HZ;        // uCurlNoiseScale 1, uCurlTimeScale 0.5, uCurlNoiseSpeed 1
vec3 gradient = sdfNormal(pos);   // central differences, step 0.001
float sdf = sdfShape(pos);
pos += cross(normalize(pos), normalize(gradient)) * 0.0005;           // swirl along the surface
pos += -gradient * sdf * 0.5;                                          // pull onto the surface
pos += (origin - pos) * 0.0002 * HZ;                                   // spring back to origin
// mouse fluid
vec2 screenUV = project(model * pos) → 0..1
vec3 flow = vec3(texture(fluidVelocity, screenUV).xy, 0.0) rotated by the camera's world rotation
pos += flow * 0.0001 * HZ * 0.4 * texture(fluidDensity, screenUV).r;  // uMouseStrength 0.4
```

**Shape.** A smooth, organic sculpted form about 0.7 units across: a bent, hollow ring/torus-like mass with one large opening and softer lobes, defined as a signed distance function. (The original uses a small sine-network SDF; any closed, smooth, slightly twisted ring with one big hole gives the same read. Before evaluating, mirror the depth axis: `p.z = sqrt(p.z*p.z + 0.0215) - sqrt(0.012)` so the form is symmetric front/back with a soft seam, and rotate `p` by the quaternion (0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5). Outside radius 0.8 return `length(p) - 0.7`.)

**Curl noise.** Analytic curl of three sine-sum potentials (Bridson-style), normalized.

**Point rendering.** Additive blending, transparent, depth test on, depth write off. Vertex: `pos *= mix(1.0, 1.5, pow(random.y, 150.0))`; `scale = smoothstep(3, 15, distToCamera) * mix(0.5, 1.0, random.z)`; `gl_PointSize = 0.04 * DPR * 2.0 * scale * (1000 / viewDistance)`. Fragment: discard outside a circle; discard when scale < 0.1; base colour `mix(0.0, 0.2, random.x)` grey, mixed to lavender (0.6, 0.45, 1.0) by `pow(random.z, 100)`; sparkle `0.5 + (0.4 + sin(time*4 + random.y*20)) * pow(random.z, 10) * 2.5`; matcap sampled with the sprite UV rotated by `sin(time + random.z*20)*0.5 + 1`, blended soft-light 0.8 then overlay 0.2; alpha 1.

## 8. Fluid simulation (drives the cursor interaction)

Classic GPU fluid (curl → vorticity → divergence → pressure → gradient subtract → advect velocity → advect density → display), half-float ping-pong targets.

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Sim resolution | 256 × 256 |
| Dye resolution | 512 × 512 |
| Velocity dissipation | 0.98 |
| Density dissipation | 0.97 |
| Pressure dissipation | 0.95 |
| Pressure iterations | 5 |
| Curl | 30 |
| dt | 1/60 |

**Mouse input each frame.** `len` = cursor distance moved since last frame (px). Splat radius = clamp-map(len, 0..5 → 0..60) × 0.6 (× 0.8 on mobile); force multiplier = clamp-map(len, 0..15 → 0..10). When len > 0.01: splat a line from the previous point to the current with colour (dx × mult, -dy × mult, 1) into velocity (additive) and white into density, radius/200 in UV units, aspect-corrected. If more than 50 ms passed since the last splat, the line starts at the current point.

The density texture, rendered to a viewport-sized target with alpha = max(r, g, b), is the mask that limits the push to where the cursor has been.

## 9. Interactions and motion summary

- Cursor move anywhere: fluid splat → particles swirl and drift along the flow, then heal back onto the shape within ~1–2 s.
- Cursor move also pans the camera slightly (gaze).
- Touch: `touchstart`/`touchmove` feed the same mouse position.
- Resize: renderer, camera aspect and the fluid mask target follow the window.
- Links: hover fades to 70 % over 300 ms.
- No entrance animation; the cloud forms from random positions over the first ~3 s of simulation.

## 10. Acceptance checklist

- [ ] Black page, no scrollbars, canvas fills the viewport at any size.
- [ ] A dense white-grey particle cloud with sparse lavender points forms a hollow, twisted ring form, centred slightly right of the UI columns.
- [ ] Moving the cursor across the cloud visibly stirs it; it settles back within two seconds.
- [ ] Camera drifts a little with the cursor.
- [ ] Brand, counter, 10 chips, 4 video cards (all playing, muted), and the four text blocks with the exact copy above.
- [ ] Headings in #aa88ff; text blends additively over the particles; videos are opaque.
- [ ] Below 760 px the chips and cards hide and the text column sits at the bottom.
- [ ] No console errors; all four video URLs return 200.

Build a single-screen hero for a fictional independent press and bookshop, **Folio**. Use one HTML file with plain HTML and CSS plus a Three.js module (r160 from jsDelivr through an import map: `three` and `three/addons/`).

| 11 | 1952, 586, 382, 572 | `#f57664` | Velvet Static / Remy Cole — pink-orange grainy gradient |
| 12 | 3, 1167, 383, 574 | `#f3f3f3` | Lessons in Gravity / Noor Haddad — falling figure on white |
| 13 | 394, 1167, 381, 574 | `#2a2929` | THE ARCHIVE / Felix Brandt — brutalist type |

| 17 | 1952, 1167, 382, 574 | `#1c565e` | Northern Lights Hotel / Hugo Berg — snowy hotel under aurora |

**Order:** books use cover index n (0 to 17 from sheet A, 18 to 35 from sheet B) in this order, front to back:

`0, 22, 5, 30, 9, 13, 26, 2, 19, 11, 33, 7, 15, 24, 4, 28, 17, 21, 1, 31, 14, 8, 25, 35, 3, 18, 10, 29, 16, 23, 6, 34`

## Fonts and colour

- **Fonts:** Google Fonts **Libre Caslon Display** 400 for the wordmark and logo, **Inter** 400 and 500 for the UI.
- **Colours:** background `#000`, text white. The logo mark is a `#b8a58a` rounded tile with a `#16120d` bar. The pill is white with black text.

## Layout (all fixed, the page never scrolls)

### Nav (z 5)

- **Box:** left 23.3vw, right 23.4vw, top 4.6vh, height 4.4vh; font `max(11px, .78vw)` Inter 500.
- **Logo:**
  - A 2.1vw × 2.4vw tile with a dark vertical bar (left 32%, 24% wide, 64% tall).
  - Next to it, "Folio" in Libre Caslon Display `max(17px, 1.55vw)`, with "independent press" in Inter `max(8px, .6vw)` at 70% under it.
- **Centre links**, 2.3vw apart, starting 11.4vw after the logo: "Books ⌄", "Authors", "Journal", "More ⌄". The chevrons are small stroked svgs, and the links sit at 88% opacity, going to 100% on hover.
- **Right side**, 2.4vw apart:
  - "Sign in".
  - A white pill "Start reading": radius .4vw, padding .55vw 1vw, lifting 1px on hover.

### Wordmark (z 1)

- **Text:** "Folio", centred, `--fs: min(46vh, 32vw)`, `font: 400 var(--fs)/1 Libre Caslon Display`, letter-spacing −.02em.
- **Position:** `top: calc(46.5vh − var(--fs)·.8)`, so its baseline sits at about 46vh.

### Link row (z 1)

- **Box:** top 51.1vh, centred, gap 2.1vw, Inter 500 `max(10px, .74vw)`.
- **Links:** "New Releases, Bestsellers, Fiction, Nonfiction, Poetry, Classics, Independent Voices, Gift Cards".

### Canvas (z 2)

A full-screen transparent WebGL canvas above the wordmark and links and below the nav.

## Three.js scene

### Renderer

- `antialias`, `alpha`, pixel ratio `min(dpr, 2)`.
- ACESFilmic tone mapping at exposure 1.05, sRGB output.

### Lighting

- **Environment:** `PMREMGenerator.fromScene(new RoomEnvironment(), .04)` with `environmentIntensity .55`.
- **Key:** DirectionalLight `#fff3e4`, 2.4, at (−4, 6, 6).
- **Rim:** `#bfd2ff`, 1.1, at (6, 3, −4).
- **Ambient:** white, .12.

### Camera

- PerspectiveCamera with fov 19.5 (40 when width < height) at (3.6, 2.15, 7.4), looking at (−1.4, .05, −.6).

### Books

- **Geometry:** one shared `BoxGeometry(1, 1.5, .2)`. Face materials in order +x, −x, +y, −y, +z, −z:
  1. **Fore-edge:** MeshStandard, roughness .9, with a 256px canvas of cream `#efe7d6` and 1px brown lines every 2px (alpha .05 to .17), horizontal.
  2. **Spine:** MeshPhysical in the cover's spine colour ×.62, roughness .55, clearcoat .3.
  3. **Top** and 4. **Bottom:** the same page texture with vertical lines.
  5. **Cover:** MeshPhysical with the cover texture, roughness .42, clearcoat .55, clearcoatRoughness .35.
  6. **Back:** spine colour ×.62, roughness .6.
- **Groups:** each book is a mesh inside a group.
  - Group position: `(1.55 + i·(−.5), −1.12, .9 + i·(−.2))` with `rotation.y = .32`, where i = 0 is the front book at the bottom right.
  - The mesh moves inside the group for the lift.

## Motion

### Pointer wave

- **Projection:** each frame, project the point (0, .1, 0) of each book mesh to screen pixels (sx, sy).
- **Influence:** with `s = max(innerWidth, innerHeight)·.085`, `influence = exp(−((sx−x)² + ((sy−y)·.55)²) / s²)`.
- **Target lift:** `.78·influence`, or 0 when the pointer has left the window or the window is blurred.

### Springs

Every book has a vertical spring and a forward spring (target `lift·.35` in local z), both with `K = 70`, `C = 12.5`.

- Integrate in 4 sub-steps per frame, with `dt` capped at .05s: `v += ((target − y)·K − v·C)·h; y += v·h`.
- `mesh.rotation.x = −v·.012`, so a book leans slightly while it moves.

### Intro

- **Books:** start at y = −3. Each one's target stays −3 until `t > .25 + (32 − i)·.035` seconds, so the row rises from the back to the front, each book springing up.
- **Wordmark:** Web Animations API, 1400ms after a 150ms delay: opacity 0 → 1, translateY(4vh) → 0, blur(14px) → 0, with `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)`.
- **Nav:** fades down from −1.2vh at 700ms (900ms long).
- **Link row:** fades up from 1.2vh at 850ms (900ms long).

### Touch and idle

On `(pointer: coarse)`, or after 4s without pointer movement, a virtual cursor sweeps along the row with `u = (sin(t·.45) + 1)/2`, between book 29 and book 1 projected to the screen.

## Phones (≤760px)

- **Nav:** left and right 5vw, top 2.5vh. Only the logo and the pill stay.
- **Wordmark:** `--fs: 36vw` at top 14vh.
- **Link row:** wraps at top 36vh with 8vw side padding.
- **Camera:** fov 40.

title: Card Stack
description: Single-file portfolio home page for a fictional creative studio, OPAQUE®. The stack: on an off-white fafafa canvas, a long diagonal row of thin portrait image cards stands in 3D. Features hardware-accelerated WebGL / Three.js 3D rendering, scroll-driven kinetic animations and staggered choreography with precision layout polish.
full_prompt:
# Opaque Stack: WebGL Leaning-Card Portfolio with Fly-to-Page Transition (exact recreation prompt)

Build a single-file portfolio home page for a fictional creative studio, **OPAQUE®**.

**The stack:** on an off-white `#fafafa` canvas, a long diagonal row of thin portrait image cards stands in 3D. Each card is turned −30° and the row leans from the lower left to the upper right, seen through a very narrow 5° lens from slightly above.

- **Scroll or drag:** the row slides endlessly along its diagonal, with eased momentum.
- **Hover:** the card under the cursor slides out of the stack, and its uppercase title follows the cursor.
- **Click a card:**
  1. Every other card vanishes at once.
  2. The clicked card glides to the centre of the screen, turns to face the viewer and becomes square, while the camera flies to a straight-on view.
  3. The project page fades in over it: a centred title and description, a two-column image grid, and a "Next project" row.
- **Back:** clicking "OPAQUE® PROJECTS" (or pressing Esc) returns to the stack, and the row flies in again.

Each card's edges blur softly into the page through a custom shader: sharp in the middle, blurred towards every edge.

Use plain HTML, CSS and JS in one file, with **three.js r128** and **GSAP 3.12.5** from cdnjs. Every value below is exact. Reproduce every string, number, timing and URL as written.

---

## 1. Page basics

- `<html lang="en">`, title `OPAQUE® Projects`, viewport `width=device-width,initial-scale=1`, charset utf-8.
- **Font (Google Fonts):** `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500&display=swap`, with preconnects to `https://fonts.googleapis.com` and `https://fonts.gstatic.com` (crossorigin). The standalone version embeds the Inter latin woff2 faces (400 and 500) as base64 `@font-face` rules instead.
- **Scripts, in this order before the inline script:**
  - `https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js`
  - `https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/gsap/3.12.5/gsap.min.js`
- **Variables:** `--bg:#fafafa`, `--ink:#141414`, `--mute:#a9a9a9`, `--line:rgba(0,0,0,.08)`.
- **Reset and base:**
  - Universal `box-sizing:border-box;margin:0;padding:0`.
  - `html,body` fill the height, `overflow:hidden`, background `var(--bg)`.
  - body font `"Inter","Helvetica Neue",Arial,sans-serif`, ink colour, antialiased.
- **Utility class `.u`:** 11px, letter-spacing .02em, uppercase.
- **The body starts with class `loading`.**

## 2. The single image asset

All twelve projects come from **one 4×3 contact sheet** (2336×1744, white gutters): twelve moody editorial images.

| Row | Images |
|---|---|
| 1 | Red glossy lips with a gold ring; soft white cumulus clouds in blue sky; red neon tubes at night; a white mannequin bust in hard venetian-blind light |
| 2 | A blue-tinted woman's face close-up; a woman's silhouette against warm orange light; liquid chrome metal spheres; a glowing blue jellyfish in the dark |
| 3 | Grey concrete stairs with a hard diagonal shadow; a rainbow prism light leak; car headlights in fog; a black-and-white crashing wave |

URL (exact):

`https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20261106_084005_ab0d1fcf-a93f-4e32-a277-1523e1768fbe.png&w=2400&q=88`

**Cutting the sheet into cells:**

- Load it with `crossOrigin='anonymous'`.
- Use the sheet constants `SW=2336, SH=1744, CW=.2425, CG=.01, RH=.3244, RG=.0134`.
- Cell i is at column `c=i%4` and row `r=floor(i/4)`. With `k = naturalWidth/SW`, the cell is at:
  - x `c*(CW+CG)*SW*k`, width `CW*SW*k`
  - y `r*(RH+RG)*SH*k`, height `RH*SH*k`
- `cellCanvas(i,size)` draws a cell into a square canvas. For each project:
  - the **sharp** texture is a 512px canvas (`THREE.CanvasTexture`);
  - the **blur** texture is a 24px canvas (`CanvasTexture`, `minFilter = magFilter = LinearFilter`), so upscaling it is the blur;
  - `url` is the 512px canvas as a JPEG data URL (quality .7), used for the corner thumbnail.
- After each project, add `100/12` to the loading progress and wait 30ms.

**Projects** (name, category, year):

| # | Name | Category | Year |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Velvet Mouth | Graphic identity | 2025 |
| 1 | Cumulus | Site design | 2025 |
| 2 | No Signal | Video | 2024 |
| 3 | Still Life | 3D | 2024 |
| 4 | Memories | AI | 2025 |
| 5 | Shadowplay | Graphic identity | 2024 |
| 6 | Mercury | 3D | 2025 |
| 7 | Abyss | Site design | 2024 |
| 8 | Concrete Poem | Graphic identity | 2023 |
| 9 | Prism | AI | 2025 |
| 10 | Headlights | Video | 2023 |
| 11 | Tide | Site design | 2024 |

- **Categories:** `All, Graphic identity, Site design, AI, Video, 3D`.
- **REPEAT = 3:** the twelve projects appear three times, giving 36 cards.

## 3. Renderer and camera

- **Canvas `#gl`:** `position:fixed; inset:0`, full size, `touch-action:none`.
  - `body.hov #gl` gets `cursor:pointer`; `body.drag #gl` gets `cursor:grabbing`.
- **Renderer:** `THREE.WebGLRenderer({canvas, antialias:true, alpha:false})`, clear colour `#fafafa`, pixel ratio `min(devicePixelRatio,2)`.
- **Camera:** `PerspectiveCamera(5, innerWidth/innerHeight, .1, 1000)`.
  - `placeCamera()`: position `(0, 100/7.5, aspect<1 ? 55 : 35)`, then `lookAt(0,0,0)`.
  - On resize: set the renderer size, update the aspect and projection, and call `placeCamera()` unless a project is open.
- **Group:** one `world` group in the scene holds every card.

## 4. Card shader (ShaderMaterial, transparent)

**Vertex shader:** pass `vUv`; standard projection.

**Fragment shader**, with uniforms `uMeshSize` (vec2), `uImageSize` (vec2, set to 1,1), `uImageTexture`, `uBlurTexture`, `uOpacity`:

```
ratio = vec2(min((mesh.x/mesh.y)/(img.x/img.y),1.0), min((mesh.y/mesh.x)/(img.y/img.x),1.0))
uvCover = vUv*ratio + (1-ratio)*0.5
progress = 1.0; margin = 0.15
on each of the four edges: progress.rgb *= smoothstep(edge, edge±margin, vUv)
blur.a *= 0.75
color = mix(sharp, blur, 1.0 - progress.r)
color.a *= uOpacity
```

The middle 70% of the card is sharp, and the outer 15% on each side fades into the blurred copy.

## 5. Cards and layout

- **Sizes:** `GAP=.375`, `BE=4/3`, `SC=1-(BE-1)*.5`, `H0=1.5*SC`, `W0=1.5*BE*SC`.
- **Geometry:** `BoxGeometry(H0, W0, .0175)`, a thin portrait slab.
- **Each card is:**
  - `mesh`: the shader material, with `uMeshSize = (H0, W0)`;
  - `hit`: the same geometry with an invisible `MeshBasicMaterial` (opacity 0, transparent, no depth write), `scale.x = 1.5`, a generous hover target;
  - `inner` group: holds the mesh and slides on hover;
  - `holder` group: holds `inner` and `hit`, and is placed on the row.
- **Card state:** `{n, i, mesh, hit, inner, holder, order:n, visK:1, on:true}`.
- **Motion state:**
  - `scroll = {current:0, previous:0}`
  - `mouse = {x:-1, y:-1, drag:{x,y,active}, on:{x,y}, down}`
  - `M = 0` (eased drag)
  - `intro = {x:-20}`
  - `wrap(min,max,v)` = modulo wrap
- **layout(), every frame:**
  1. Ease the drag: `M += (drag.x - drag.y - M) * .1`.
  2. Ease the scroll: `scroll.previous += (current - previous) * .15`.
  3. Set `J = scroll.previous/25 - M/100 + intro.x`.
  4. Take the visible (filtered) cards: `N` = their count, `len = max(N,24)`, `F = len*GAP/2`, `step = len/N`. Each visible card gets `order = k*step`, which spreads a filtered set along a loop of at least 24 slots.
  5. For every card:
     - `visK += ((on?1:0) - visK) * .12`, and `uOpacity = visK`.
     - If nothing is open:
       - `x = wrap(-F, F, (order - J)*GAP)`
       - `y = -(1 - visK)*1.2`, so filtered-out cards sink
       - `z = aspect<1 ? -x*6 : -x*aspect*1.5`
       - `rotation.x = 0`, `rotation.y = -π/6`
       - visible only while `visK > .02` and `|z| < 12.5`

## 6. Interaction

- **Hover:**
  - Each frame, raycast the visible cards' `hit` meshes at the mouse NDC. Skip this before ready, while open, while dragging, or with no mouse.
  - On a new hovered card:
    - The previous card's `inner.position` goes back to (0,0), expo.out 0.5s.
    - The new card's `inner.position` goes to `x: 2/3, y: -.1`, expo.out 0.5s.
    - The body gets `hov`.
    - `#label` shows the project name.
    - `#thumb` shows its image.
- **Wheel:** `scroll.current += (deltaY + deltaX)/20`, passive, ignored before ready or while open.
- **Arrow keys:** ±12. **Esc:** closes the project.
- **Drag:**
  - pointerdown on the canvas stores `on = drag - client` and captures the pointer.
  - Once the pointer has moved more than 3px:
    - drag mode starts and the body gets `drag`;
    - `world.scale` → 0.825 (expo.out .75s);
    - `drag = on + client`.
  - On pointerup, drag mode ends and the scale returns to 1 (expo.out .75s).
  - A pointerup without a drag on a hovered card opens it.
- **Cursor label `#label`:**
  - Fixed, 11px Inter 500 uppercase ink, `pointer-events:none`.
  - Follows at `translate(x+14px, y+12px)`.
  - Opacity transition .2s.

## 7. Open a project (exact sequence)

`openTile(t)`:

1. Set `opened = t`, clear the hover, and add `opened` to the body (the side chrome fades out).
2. **Hide every other card at once.**
3. Snap `t.inner.position` to (0,0).
4. `t.holder.position.x` → 0, expo.out over `1.25/3*2` s. On each update, `z = -x*aspect*1.5`, so the card slides along the row to the centre.
5. `t.holder.rotation.y` → 0, expo.inOut 1.25s (it turns to face you).
6. `camera.position` → `(0, 0, innerWidth<640 ? 35 : 30)`, expo.inOut 1.25s, calling `lookAt(0,0,0)` on every update.
7. **When the camera tween completes:**
   - fill the page and make `#page` visible;
   - fade it `opacity 0 → 1` over 0.5s, power1.inOut;
   - then hide the card underneath.

`closeTile()`:

1. Kill the page tweens, hide the page (opacity 0, hidden), and remove `opened`.
2. Reset the card's `rotation.y` to `-π/6` and call `placeCamera()`.
3. Set `opened = null`.
4. The row flies in again: `intro.x = -20` → 0, expo.out 2s.

"OPAQUE® PROJECTS" (`#home`) calls `closeTile`.

## 8. Project page `#page`

- **Container:** fixed, inset 0, z-index 8, `overflow-y:auto`, `overscroll-behavior:none`, background `var(--bg)`, a flex column. It starts at opacity 0 and `visibility:hidden`.
- **Head section `.head`:**
  - Height 50vh (min 20rem), `margin-top:3.75rem`, content centred vertically, font-size 11px, line-height 1.0909.
  - The inner row has padding `5rem 14px`.
  - `h1` (the project name): width 12.5rem, Inter 500 11px uppercase.
  - `p` (the description): max-width 287px, padding `0 2px`.
- **Grid `.grid`:** two equal columns, no gap. Five blocks, all cut from the project's own sheet cell (as JPEG data URLs, quality .85):

  | Block | Crop (x, y, w, h of the cell) | Output size | Width | Aspect ratio |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 0, .08, 1, .84 | 1200×1000 | half | 1.2 |
  | 2 | .18, 0, .64, 1 | 900×1400 | half | .64 |
  | 3 | 0, .2, 1, .6 | 1800×1080 | full (spans both columns) | 1.67 |
  | 4 | .05, .05, .5, .5 | 1000×1000 | half | 1 |
  | 5 | .45, .45, .5, .5 | 1000×1000 | half | 1 |

  - Each block is a relative box with overflow hidden and an absolutely-filled `object-fit:cover` image.
  - Images start at opacity 0 and fade in (`.in`, .6s `cubic-bezier(.215,.61,.355,1)`) as they load.
- **Next section `.next`:** height 50vh (min 20rem), centred, padding 14px, 11px uppercase.
  - Credits row: "Category" in an 8.25rem column at 30% opacity, then the category.
  - A full-width link: "Next project" in an 8.25rem column at 30% opacity (100% on hover, .5s), then the next project's name.
  - Clicking it fades the page to 0 over .25s, refills it with the next project, scrolls to the top, and fades back in over .5s (power1.inOut).
- **Descriptions** (by project index):
  0. A campaign built from close-up texture and saturated colour, shot and graded in-house.
  1. Site design and art direction for an atmospheric weather brand, all soft light and slow motion.
  2. A night-time film series exploring signal, noise and the glow of the city after dark.
  3. Still lifes rendered in 3D, mixing studio light with synthetic materials.
  4. An AI-assisted portrait series about memory, distortion and the faces we half remember.
  5. Visual identity built from shadow and warm light, for a theatre collective.
  6. Liquid-metal forms for a product launch, modelled, lit and animated in 3D.
  7. An immersive site for a deep-sea research lab, glowing in the dark.
  8. A typographic identity cast in concrete for an architecture biennale.
  9. Generative colour studies trained on refracted light.
  10. A short film shot entirely in fog, following two headlights through the night.
  11. An editorial site for a surf brand, built around the rhythm of the tide.

## 9. Chrome (all with class `chrome`, transition opacity .6s)

`body.loading` hides it. `body.opened` hides everything except the nav.

- **Nav** (fixed at left 6px, top 6px, flex, gap 3px, z-index 10, `.u`): four tiles.
  - Labels: `OPAQUE<sup>®</sup> PROJECTS` (198px wide, ink), `Research`, `Studio`, `Contact` (122px, mute).
  - Each tile: 58px tall, padding `0 10px 10px` with the text at the bottom, radius 4px.
  - Background `rgba(242,242,241,.5)` with `backdrop-filter: blur(14px)` and an inset 1px `var(--line)` ring.
  - Hover: ink text on `#ececeb`.
- **`#thumb`:** fixed at top-right 10px, 58×58, radius 3px, cover background. Filter `grayscale(1) contrast(1.1)`. Shows the hovered project's image (Memories at start).
- **Filter chips `#chips`:** fixed at right 10px, bottom 62px, a column aligned right, gap 5px.
  - One pill per category: 30px tall, padding `0 13px`, radius 30px, background `rgba(242,242,241,.9)`, line ring.
  - Text: Inter 500 10px uppercase, mute; ink when active or hovered.
  - A count in a 7px `<sup>`.
  - Clicking sets `t.on` for the matching cards: the others sink and fade through `visK`, and the remaining ones re-spread along the loop.
- **Mode switch `#mode`:** fixed at bottom-right 10px, padding 3px, radius 4px, the same glass. Two buttons, "Overview" and "Index": 34px tall, 11px uppercase. The active one is white with a line ring.
  - **Index** shows `#index`: a list fixed at left 10px, top 96px, width `min(420px,40vw)`.
  - Each row is a grid `28px 1fr auto auto`, holding number, name (500, ink), category and year, with a top border line.
  - Row hover: ink text, padding-left 12px.
  - Hovering a row scrolls the stack to that project and sets the thumbnail; clicking a row opens it.
- **At 760px or narrower:** nav tiles are 76px (first one 120px) and the index is 80vw.

## 10. Loader and intro

1. `#loader` covers the page (bg colour) with a centred "0%" (Inter 500 11px).
2. While the textures build: `prog.previous += (current - previous)*.1` each frame, shown as a rounded percent.
3. At 100:
   - The percent fades out (.5s, delay .25).
   - The loader fades out (.5s, delay .75, power1.inOut), then is removed, and `loading` is removed from the body.
4. After 750ms:
   - Set `ready = true`.
   - **The row flies in:** `intro.x` -20 → 0, expo.out 2s.
   - `world.scale` starts at 0.825 and eases to 1 (expo.out 1s, delay 1.25s).
   - The thumbnail shows project 4.
5. **The render loop** runs `layout()`, `pick()` and `renderer.render()` on every requestAnimationFrame.

title: Designer Portfolio
description: Single-file, full-viewport portfolio hero for a fictional independent designer, Adrian Korvel. It is one screen, with no scrolling on desktop. Features hardware-accelerated WebGL / Three.js 3D rendering, cinematic looping background video integration with precision layout polish.
full_prompt: # Recreate the "Adrian Korvel" portfolio hero exactly Build a single-file, full-viewport portfolio hero for a fictional independent designer, Adrian Korvel. It is one screen, with no scrolling on desktop. The page is a deep burnt-terracotta scene. A giant, softly glowing condensed serif name sits behind an illustrated portrait of a young man with long curly hair that blows in the wind. Dark agave leaves sway in the bottom corners, and small sparkles twinkle. Around this sit small uppercase typewriter-style text blocks, a minimal nav and a strip of five badges along the bottom. Everything below must be reproduced exactly: values, text, assets, timings. --- ## 1. Assets (use these exact URLs; do not re-host, crop or re-encode) | Role | Type | URL | Size | How it is used | |---|---|---|---|---| | Scene still (background plate) | PNG, served as WebP through the image proxy | `https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20261107_011718_f1fd2b4c-d260-44ae-a0a2-8256134a4c35.png&w=2048&q=85` | 2048 × 1360 (3:2) | CSS background of the plate box, stretched to the box (`background-size:100% 100%`). Draw a full-screen triangle strip (−1,−1 / 1,−1 / −1,1 / 1,1). The vertex shader maps it to UVs with a flipped y: `v = vec2(p.x*.5+.5, .5-p.y*.5)`. The texture uses CLAMP_TO_EDGE and LINEAR filtering. Upload the current source each draw with `texImage2D`. Fragment shader: - `m = max(r, b)`, `d = g − m` - `alpha = 1 − smoothstep(0.06, 0.30, d)` - Spill clamp: `g = min(g, (r + b) × 0.52)`. full_prompt:
# Noa Ellsworth: a botanist made of 66,000 dots

Build a single-page, full-screen portfolio hero: a dark moss-black room where the head-and-shoulders bust of a fictional botanist, Noa Ellsworth, is drawn entirely from about 66,000 soft glowing dots in WebGL (three.js). Her hair is gathered into a loose bun with a small sprig of leaves tucked into its right side, a few wavy strands hang beside her cheeks and neck, she wears a linen shirt with an open pointed collar, and across her eyes sits a single wraparound visor, also made of dots, with a faint sage-tinted lens. Her face is smooth and featureless, like a clay sculpture: the likeness lives in the silhouette, the hair, the leaves and the visor, never in eyes or a mouth.

The page opens on a ring-shaped loader whose number is the real download of the 3D model. At 100 every dot leaves the ring and arcs forward into place, so you watch her assemble herself. As the last dots land, one diagonal band of light sweeps down the bust once. From then on the visitor's cursor is a small light: it lights whatever part of her it is near, and her head turns gently to look at it. Every few seconds a sage glint runs across the visor and then across the leaves. Faint dust drifts upward through the whole room and a fine film grain sits over everything. The mood is calm, quiet and premium; nothing is busy, nothing reacts loudly.

Recreate everything below exactly: every value is taken from the finished page.

---

## 1. Assets and external URLs

| What | URL | How it is used |
|---|---|---|
| The 3D bust (untextured GLB, about 1.48 MB, one mesh of about 40,476 vertices and 30,887 triangles, CORS open) | https://d8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/hf_20261115_071021_742152ba-5554-4270-9dc5-286bcff36a1a.glb | Streamed with fetch so the loader can show true byte progress, parsed with three.js GLTFLoader, then sampled into dots in the browser. The model faces +Z, Y is up, and it spans roughly x −0.75…0.74, y −0.95…0.95, z −0.42…0.42 in its own units. |
| three.js 0.170.0 core | https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js | ES module, mapped as "three" in an import map. |
| three.js addons 0.170.0 | https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/ | Mapped as "three/addons/". Use loaders/GLTFLoader.js and math/MeshSurfaceSampler.js. |
| Geist (variable, weights 100–900, latin) | https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/geist/v5/gyByhwUxId8gMEwcGFU.woff2 | Sans for the name and tagline. |
| Geist Mono (variable, weights 100–900, latin) | https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/geistmono/v6/or3nQ6H-1_WfwkMZI_qYFrcdmg.woff2 | Mono for the loader counter, the loader label, the hint and the pill. |
| Instrument Serif (400, latin) | https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/instrumentserif/v5/jizBRFtNs2ka5fXjeivQ4LroWlx-6zUTjg.woff2 | Serif for the "Noa." logo. |
| Film grain | Inline SVG data URI (no file) | An SVG of 240 × 240 with a feTurbulence filter (type fractalNoise, baseFrequency 0.85, numOctaves 3, stitchTiles stitch) followed by an feColorMatrix whose values are all zero except the alpha row "1.7 0 0 0 −0.6", applied to a full-size rect. Used as a repeating background on an overlay. |

Declare the three fonts with @font-face (font-display swap; Geist and Geist Mono with font-weight 100 900; Instrument Serif weight 400). In a single-file version, embed them as base64 data URIs.

## 2. Head and colour tokens

Title: "Noa Ellsworth". Meta description: "A point cloud portrait of a botanist, built from 66,000 dots. Move the light." Viewport meta: width=device-width, initial-scale=1. A preconnect to https://cdn.jsdelivr.net.

| Token | Value | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| --color-night | #0f110d | Page background and the WebGL clear colour |
| --color-paper | #f0e5c8 | Cream: logo, name, loader text and ring dots, and the colour the shine pulls dots toward |
| --color-dots | #c9d4b8 | The soft moss-green ink of every bust dot and of the dust |
| --color-tech | #7fa8a3 | Sage-teal: the glint colour and the lens tint |
| --color-muted | #7f8a6a | The tagline |
| --color-surface | #fff | Pill background |
| --color-ink | #111 | Pill text |
| --color-line | #1111111a | Pill hairline ring |
| --font-sans | "Geist", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif | |
| --font-mono | "Geist Mono", ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace | |
| --font-serif | "Instrument Serif", Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif | |

All elements use box-sizing border-box. html and body: margin 0, height 100%, background --color-night. Body font --font-sans with antialiased font smoothing.

## 3. DOM, in order

A single main element (class page, data-phase "loading" at first, later "ready") containing:

1. A stage div (aria-hidden) that receives the WebGL canvas.
2. The loader: a div with role progressbar, aria-label "Loading the dots", aria-valuemin 0, aria-valuemax 100, aria-valuenow updated live. Inside: an SVG ring (viewBox −110 −110 220 220), a span counter showing "000", and a span label "66,000 dots".
3. A link "Noa." (the logo, href "./").
4. An h1 "Noa Ellsworth".
5. A p "Grows quiet things with AI" (the tagline).
6. A p "Move the light" (the hint).
7. A link "How this page was made →" (the pill).

There is no navigation bar and no other text.

## 4. Desktop layout and styling

The page is position fixed, inset 0, overflow hidden, background --color-night, text colour --color-paper, cursor crosshair while loading and cursor none once data-phase is "ready" (the WebGL light replaces the pointer), touch-action none.

A ::after pseudo-element covers the page (position absolute, inset 0, pointer-events none) with the grain data URI as background, filter invert(1) and opacity 0.05.

The stage is absolute, inset 0; its canvas is width and height 100%, display block.

**Loader.** Absolute, inset 0, display grid, place-items center, pointer-events none, opacity transition 0.5 s with a 0.15 s delay; it goes to opacity 0 when the page is ready.
- The ring SVG is 220 × 220 px, centred with top 50%, left 50% and translate −50% −50%, overflow visible. It holds 96 circles placed on a circle of radius 92: circle i sits at angle (i / 96) × 2π − π/2 (starting at 12 o'clock, going clockwise), with cx = 92 cos(angle) and cy = 92 sin(angle) rounded to two decimals, and r 1.6. An unlit circle is filled with --color-paper mixed 18% into transparent. A lit circle (attribute data-on) is filled solid --color-paper with r 2.2 px. Both fill and r transition over 0.25 s. Circle i is lit while i / 96 < progress.
- The counter is Geist Mono 34 px, letter-spacing 0.02em, tabular numerals, centred at 50%/50% with translate −50% −60%. It shows the rounded percentage padded to three digits ("000" to "100").
- The label is Geist Mono 11 px, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.12em, opacity 0.5, centred horizontally at 50%/50% with translate −50% 26 px (so it sits just under the counter).

**Text.** The logo, name, tagline and hint all start at opacity 0, margin 0, position absolute, with transitions of opacity 0.9 s and translate 0.9 s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1).
- Name and tagline: Geist 400, font-size clamp(17px, 1.6vw, 24px) (24 px at 1440 wide), letter-spacing −0.01em, top 50%, starting at translate 0 calc(10px − 50%) and ending at translate 0 −50% (a 10 px rise). The name sits at left clamp(20px, 4vw, 64px). The tagline sits at right clamp(20px, 4vw, 64px), has colour --color-muted and a 0.12 s transition delay.
- Logo: Instrument Serif 26 px, colour inherited (cream), no underline, top 20 px, left clamp(20px, 4vw, 64px). It fades to opacity 0.9 when ready; on hover or keyboard focus it goes to opacity 1 with an underline offset 4 px.
- Hint: Geist Mono 11 px, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.12em, no wrapping, bottom 22 px, left 50%, starting at translate −50% 10 px with a 0.5 s transition delay, ending at translate −50% (0) and opacity 0.45.

**Pill.** "How this page was made →": position fixed, bottom 20 px, left 20 px, z-index 7, background #fff, colour #111, Geist Mono 12 px, letter-spacing 0.04em, padding 8 px 12 px, border-radius 6 px, no underline, box-shadow of a 1 px #1111111a ring plus 0 10px 24px −12px #0006. It plays one animation from 4 s: 0.6 s, cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), fill both, keyframe 0% at opacity 0 and translateY 8 px (so it fades up into place).

## 5. Mobile layout

At max-width 700 px: the name and tagline drop to 16 px, move to top 72 px, start at translate 0 10 px and end at translate 0 (so they sit side by side near the top: name on the left, tagline on the right); the hint moves to bottom 60 px.

At max-width 600 px: the pill shrinks to padding 6 px 9 px and 11 px text, sits at bottom 12 px, and moves to the right (left auto, right 12 px).

The canvas and loader stay full screen; the camera fit below keeps the whole bust visible on narrow screens.

## 6. Building the dots from the model

After the download and parse, take the first mesh in the scene, clone its geometry with the mesh's world matrix applied, and compute vertex normals if missing. Build a three.js MeshSurfaceSampler on it.

**Candidates.** Sample 330,000 candidate points (5 × 66,000) with their normals, in model units.

**Even density (so the hair doesn't swallow every dot).** Put every candidate in a 3D voxel grid of 0.022 model units. Find the smallest per-voxel cap such that the sum over voxels of min(count, cap) reaches 1.8 × the number of bust dots needed. Keep at most cap candidates per voxel (in sampling order), shuffle that pool, and take as many as needed. The 1.8 headroom keeps some extra density in the hair so it keeps its texture.

**The leaf sprig (part 2).** A candidate is a leaf when x > 0.13, y > 0.6 and (x − 0.02)² + (z + 0.06)² > 0.035 (model units). Leaf candidates skip the voxel cap: keep the first 60% of them, so the sprig is denser than its area alone would give it, the way the original draws its glasses.

**The visor (parts 3 and 4).** Drawn as its own dots, as one rigid curved shape fitted to the face:
- Build a front height map of the face: for candidates whose normal z ≥ 0.2 and that lie within x −0.32…0.32 and y 0.2…0.45, keep the highest z per 0.01 × 0.01 cell. The face height at (x, y) is the maximum over the 3 × 3 neighbouring cells.
- Half-width W = 0.215. Clearance 0.028. Top edge: y = 0.378 − 0.022 (x / W)². Lower edge: y = 0.282 + 0.032 exp(−(x / 0.034)²) + 0.026 (x / W)⁴. The Gaussian term is a notch over the nose; the fourth-power term tapers the ends.
- The lens depth is one smooth curve, z = front − wrap × x². "front" is the highest face height over x −0.06…0.06 and y 0.30…0.36, plus the clearance. "wrap" is the smallest value of (front − need − 0.7 × clearance) / x² over x from −W to W in 0.01 steps (skipping |x| < 0.05), where "need" is the highest face height between the lower and top edges at that x. Fall back to 2.4 if the fit fails. Each dot's normal is (2·wrap·x, 0, 1) normalised.
- Dots, each with a small random jitter: 950 along the top bar (x uniform across −W…W, y = top edge minus a random amount weighted toward the edge, up to 0.016; pushed 0.004 forward); 380 along the lower edge (pushed 0.002 forward); 70 at each end, filling between the two edges at x = ±W; 1,500 lens dots filling the area between the edges (part 4); and 70 per side for the arms, running from each end 0.03 outward and 0.15 back along z, 0.008 below the top edge. Frame dots are part 3; lens dots are part 4.

**Placement.** Every dot is moved into world space by x × 2.8, y × 2.8 − 0.68, z × 2.8. That puts the top of the bun near the top edge of a 1440 × 900 view and lets the bottom edge crop the shoulders.

**Total.** Exactly 66,000 dots: the visor dots, the kept leaf dots, and the voxel-thinned bust dots fill the rest. Every dot also gets aRand, a uniform random number from 0 to 1.

**Depth values (aShade).** For every final dot, look at the candidates within radius R = 0.03 (model units), using the first half of the candidates in a hash grid of cell size R.
- The ridge value is −(the average neighbour offset · the dot's normal) / R. Positive means the dot stands proud of its neighbours (bun twists, leaf edges, collar points); negative means it sits in a crease. Divide by the 90th percentile of its absolute value and clamp to −1…1.
- The thin value is 1 − neighbourCount / (0.55 × the median count), clamped to 0…1. It is high for loose strands and leaf tips.

Store both as a two-component attribute. Also record the smallest and largest world x of all non-bust dots (parts 2–4); these bound the glint sweep.

## 7. Scene, camera and renderer

Use a WebGLRenderer with antialias off and powerPreference high-performance, pixel ratio min(devicePixelRatio, 2) (called dpr below), clear colour #0f110d. Use a PerspectiveCamera with fov 30, near 0.1 and far 100, looking at the target (0, −0.15, 0).

On every resize: the camera distance is max(2.35 / tan 15°, 1.7 / (tan 15° × aspect)). Put the camera at (0, −0.15, distance) looking at the target, so the view is always 4.7 units tall, or wider when the screen is narrow. One CSS pixel at the bust's depth is 2 × distance × tan 15° / height world units. The loader ring's world radius is 92 of those pixels and its centre is (0, −0.15, 0), so the WebGL ring lines up exactly with the SVG ring.

There are three Points objects, all with transparent true, depthWrite false and additive blending, and all with frustum culling off.

**1. The bust (uniforms).**

| Uniform | Value |
|---|---|
| uTime | Seconds since start |
| uAssemble | 0 to 1 |
| uSize | 26 × dpr |
| uGlint | Glint x position; −9 when off |
| uShine | Shine band position; 99 when off |
| uHead | 2D head turn |
| uLight | Cursor light position, starting at (−1.4, 1.2, 1.6) |
| uRingCenter, uRingRadius | Set by the resize |
| uInk | #c9d4b8 |
| uBlue | #7fa8a3 |
| uCream | #f0e5c8 |

**2. The cursor light.** One point with a light shader: point size 240 × dpr × uOn / depth. Its fragment is a white core, smoothstep(0.14, 0.08, r), plus a glow, exp(−4r) × 0.45 + exp(−12r) × 0.7, where r is twice the distance from the sprite centre.

**3. The dust.** 900 points spread over x −9…9, y −6…6 and z −6…2. Each rises at 0.03 + aRand × 0.05 units per second, wrapping y through a 12-unit range. Each sways in x by sin(t × 0.2 + aRand × 40) × 0.15. Point size is 22 × dpr × (0.5 + aRand) / depth. Brightness is (0.1 + aRand × 0.18) × uOn in the bust's ink colour, with the same Gaussian falloff as the bust dots.

## 8. The bust's vertex shader, step by step

1. **Head turn.** head = smoothstep(−1.3, −0.6, y). The rotation is rotY(uHead.x × (0.25 + 0.75 × head)) times rotX(uHead.y × head), applied about the pivot (0, −1, 0) to both the position and the normal. The head turns fully and the shoulders follow at 25%.
2. **Breathing.** Each dot moves along its normal by sin(uTime × 1.4 + aRand × 60) × 0.006.
3. **Entrance.**
   - r2 = fract(sin(aRand × 91.7) × 43758.5453).
   - Per-dot progress: t = clamp((uAssemble − aRand × 0.45) / 0.55, 0, 1). Each dot starts after a delay of up to 0.45 and takes 0.55 of the assemble time.
   - Ease in-out cubic: e = 4t³ when t < 0.5, otherwise 1 − (−2t + 2)³ / 2.
   - Start point: on the ring at angle aRand × 2π, radius uRingRadius × (1 + (r2 − 0.5) × 0.06), so the ring unwinds in the same order the SVG ring filled.
   - Position: mix(start, home, e), plus an arc toward the camera: (sin(aRand × 40 + uTime × 0.3), cos(aRand × 31), 0.9 + r2 × 1.4) × sin(e × π) × 0.45.
4. **Light terms.**
   - lit = max(n · toLight̂, 0) / (1 + |toLight|² × 0.32), where toLight is the cursor light's position minus the dot's world position.
   - key = max(n · normalize(−0.5, 0.6, 0.7), 0), a soft key from the top left.
   - facing = the view-space normal's z.
   - rim = (1 − |facing|)³.
5. **Brightness.**
   - Start with b = 0.3 + key × 0.22 + lit × 1.5 + rim × 0.14. It's mostly an even tone, like a scan.
   - Multiply by mix(0.55, 1, smoothstep(−0.3, 0.25, facing)), so the far side of the head is a little darker.
6. **Depth.**
   - Multiply b by 1 + ridge × 0.7 when ridge > 0, otherwise 1 + ridge × 0.5.
   - Add thin × (0.26 + key × 0.3).
7. **Parts.** Leaf dots × 0.9. Visor frame and lens dots × 0.78. Lens dots a further × 0.7. Then every dot × (0.7 + r2 × 0.5), so no two dots are alike.
8. **Glint.** Only leaf and visor dots: glint = smoothstep(0.09, 0, |x − uGlint|), measured on the dot's home x. Add glint × 1.2 to b.
9. **Shine.** band = y − x × 0.5 − uShine, measured on the turned home position. shine = exp(−band² × 4). Add shine × 1.3 to b.
10. **Alpha.** mix(0.75, 1, e).
11. **Size.** uSize × (0.45 + r2² × 1.3) × (1 + shine × 0.6) / view depth. Most dots are small, a few up to about three times larger, and dots swell slightly as the shine passes.

**Fragment.**
- Discard outside radius 0.5.
- Alpha is exp(−16 r²) × the vertex alpha, a soft Gaussian like a lens rather than a hard pixel.
- The ink starts at #c9d4b8, mixed toward cream #f0e5c8 by shine × 0.6, then toward sage #7fa8a3 by 0.6 on lens dots, then toward sage by glint × 0.7.
- The output colour is ink × brightness × alpha.

## 9. Timeline and interactions

| Time / trigger | What happens |
|---|---|
| Page load | Ring of 96 faint dots, counter "000", label "66,000 DOTS". Cursor is a crosshair. |
| While the GLB streams | Progress = bytes received / Content-Length (if no length: min(0.95, bytes / 1.5 MB)); ring dots light up clockwise from 12 o'clock, counter counts up. |
| Download done | Parse, build the dots, set progress to 1 ("100", ring full), hold 380 ms. |
| t = 0 (renderer starts) | uAssemble = min(1, t / 2.6): over 2.6 s every dot leaves the ring and arcs into place. Light sprite and dust fade in (light: uOn eases toward min(1, 1.6 × uAssemble) at rate 4; dust: toward 1 at rate 0.8, with ease = 1 − e^(−dt × rate)). |
| uAssemble > 0.55 (t ≈ 1.43 s) | data-phase becomes "ready": loader fades out (0.5 s after 0.15 s), cursor hides, logo fades to 0.9, name and tagline fade and rise 10 px over 0.9 s (tagline 0.12 s later), hint fades to 0.45 after 0.5 s. |
| t = 2.34 s → 4.54 s | The shine: s = (t − 2.34) / 2.2; uShine = 2.8 − (1 − (1 − s)²) × 7.4 (ease-out), so one diagonal band sweeps from above the bun down past the shoulders, once. |
| 4 s | The "How this page was made →" pill fades up. |
| t = 4.6 s, then every 4.2 s | The glint: over 0.9 s uGlint runs linearly from (smallest non-bust x − 0.15) to (largest non-bust x + 0.15), i.e. across the visor first and then across the leaves. Then it resets to −9. |
| Pointer move / pointer down | Pointer position in normalised device coordinates. A ray from the camera through it hits the plane z = 2.6; the light eases toward that point (rate 5), and the head eases toward (0.5 × x, 0.18 × y) (rate 3). uHead = (head.x, −head.y). |
| No pointer (or pointer left, or 1.5 s after the last touch) | The light orbits on its own at (1.9 sin(0.45 t), 0.5 + 0.8 cos(0.33 t), 2.6), and the head eases toward (0.35 sin(0.45 t), 0.12 cos(0.33 t)) at rate 1.5. |
| Frame step | dt is capped at 0.05 s. |

Easing for all of these "eases toward" is exponential smoothing: value += (target − value) × (1 − e^(−dt × rate)), or a lerp with that factor.

## 10. Reduced motion and errors

With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, there is no 380 ms hold, uAssemble starts at 1 (no entrance), uTime stays 0 (no breathing, no drifting dust), there is no shine and no glint, the head stays still, the light snaps to its target, the dust and light start fully on, CSS transitions on the loader, logo, name, tagline and hint are off, and the pill does not animate.

If the model fails to load, the counter shows "Could not load" and the label "Refresh to try again".

## 11. Acceptance checklist

- At 1440 × 900 the bun's top sits about 36 px from the top edge, the head is centred, the shoulders run off the bottom edge, the name is at left 58 px and the tagline at right 58 px, both vertically centred.
- The loader number climbs with the real download, the dots fly from the ring into the bust, the text appears around 1.4 s, the shine runs once around 2.3–4.5 s, the glint crosses the visor and leaves every 4.2 s.
- The cursor is hidden once ready; a soft glowing point follows it, the bust brightens near it, and the head turns toward it.
- The bun's twists, the leaf edges and the collar points catch light; the area under the bun and inside the collar falls into shadow; hanging strands glow softly.
- The visor reads as one wraparound piece with a brighter top bar, a finer lower edge with a nose notch, a faint sage lens and short arms; it turns with the head.
- At 375 px wide the name and tagline sit at the top, the pill is bottom-right, there is no sideways scroll.
- No console errors; exactly 66,000 bust dots.

# Mirasol Studio — Hero + About: exact recreation brief

Build a single self-contained `index.html` (no build step) for a fictional design-engineer portfolio, **Mirasol Studio**, consisting of a full-screen **hero** and a full-screen **about** section. ---

## 1. Libraries, fonts and assets

### 1.1 Scripts (CDN, exact versions)
- **three.js 0.170.0** as an ES module through an import map:

### 1.2 Fonts (latin subset woff2; embed them as base64 `@font-face` data URIs so the file is standalone)
| Family name used in CSS | Source woff2 | @font-face settings | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|

## 2. Layout system

The whole page is designed on a **1440 × 900** frame.
- `--ux = 100vw / 1440`: horizontal unit. All x positions and horizontal gaps use it.
- `--u = min(100vw / 1440, 100vh / 900)`: size unit. All font sizes, vertical positions from the top, and element sizes use it. Because it never exceeds the height-based unit, nothing is ever cropped under the nav on short/wide windows.
- Vertical positions are written as "top N" (= N × `--u` from the section top) or "bottom N" (= N × `--u` from the section bottom).
- Every section (`.screen`) is exactly `100vh` (`100svh` where supported), `position: relative`; its `.frame` is `position: absolute; inset: 0`; every direct child of the frame is absolutely positioned.

### Colour tokens
| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| ink | `#ffffff` | All primary text |
| page / dot colour | `#091618` | `html` background, WebGL clear colour, dot-dissolve colour |
| grey | `#87999a` | About "history" paragraph text |
| line | `rgba(255,255,255,.13)` | Hero grid lines |

`html` has the page colour, `-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased`, `text-rendering: optimizeLegibility`. `body` is transparent, uses the sans stack, `overflow-x: hidden`. Links inherit colour with no underline. All elements `box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0; padding: 0`.

### Stacking
1. `<canvas id="gl">`: `position: fixed; inset: 0; 100vw × 100vh; z-index 0; pointer-events: none`, starts at `opacity 0` and fades to 1 with `transition: opacity 1s ease` when the scene is ready (class `on`).
2. `<main>`: `position: relative; z-index 1`, holding both sections, both with transparent backgrounds so the canvas shows through.
3. Fixed nav and footer: `z-index 20`, `pointer-events: none` on the bar but `auto` on their children.
