Colour tokens: paper (page background) #0A0E11, paper-deep #111920, surface #141C22, ink (main text) #EEF4F6, ink-soft #9FB4BF, ink-muted #647C8A, line rgba(238,244,246,.14), accent (underlines, focus, links; "clay" token) #3AA8D0, button blue ("btn" token) #1E86AC (hover #2597C0), aqua ("sage" token) #9ED8E4, night #05090C, on-sky text #0E2A3B (used only where text sits directly on the bright sky image). The sea image and video are unchanged; only the UI around them is dark.
- Main ease: cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1).
- Grain: an inline SVG data URI, 160×160, `feTurbulence type=fractalNoise baseFrequency=.9 numOctaves=3 stitchTiles=stitch` on a full rect. Used twice: a fixed full-page overlay (`body::before`, inset −50%, opacity .045, blend mode screen, z 200, no pointer events) and inside each scene layer (see 6).
- Page: background paper, text ink, Geist, antialiased. `html, body { overflow-x: clip; max-width: 100% }` so nothing can ever create a horizontal scrollbar. While the Home view is shown the body is `overflow: hidden; overscroll-behavior: none; height: 100svh` (the wheel spins the ring instead of scrolling).

## 4. Scaling system

One design unit: `--u = min(100vw, 160svh) / 1440` (a 1440×900 frame). Every desktop measurement below is "N u" = N × --u. At ≤820 px the unit becomes `100vw / 390` and the phone rules in section 9 apply.

## 5. Nav (both views)

A 92u-tall flex row, space-between, padding 0 46u 0 45u, z 50.

- Left: the wordmark link "Noa Ellsworth." (href #home, goes to Home). Newsreader 40u, letter-spacing −0.02em, line-height 1. It is two inline-block spans: "Noa" (class wmFirst, the fly-in target) and " Ellsworth." (fades in).
- Right: "HOME / BUILD". Geist Mono 13u, letter-spacing .1em, uppercase, ink-soft, gap 10u between items; the "/" is ink-muted. Each link has 3px bottom padding and a 1.5px accent underline (scaleX 0 → 1 from the left, .5s main ease) shown on hover and on the current page (aria-current="page"), which is also ink coloured. Home is current on load.
- During the intro, everything except "Noa" is at opacity 0 and fades in over .9s when the intro ends; "Noa" is hidden until the flying loader name lands on it.

## 6. Home view (desktop 1440×900)

The stage is a flex column, height 100svh − 92u.

**6a. Top row.** Grid with columns `1fr auto`, column gap 40u, padding 8u 46u 26u 45u, z 4.

- Sentence (left): Newsreader 400, 45u, line-height 50u, letter-spacing −0.005em, max-width 800u, three lines with forced breaks: "I craft products for **startups**⁰¹," / "showreels for **labels**⁰² and free toolkits" / "for **learners**⁰³. Or just **chat with Noa**⁰⁴." Each plain word is wrapped in a word mask (inline-block, overflow hidden, 0.08em bottom padding offset by −0.08em margin) whose inner span starts at translateY(110%). The four bold items are "choices": inline, nowrap links (startups → Build view; the others stay on Home), each containing a marker (absolute, inset .1em −.12em −.02em, background = its world colour, scaleX 0 from the left), the masked words, an underline bar (absolute, bottom .02em, height max(2px, .05em), accent colour, scaleX 0 from the left), and a superscript number 01–04 (Newsreader, max(10px, .34em), vertical-align top, nudged up .05em, ink). Punctuation directly after a choice (",", ".") is placed inside that choice so it can never wrap to the start of the next line. Each word gets a stagger delay of 0.05 s + 0.035 s × its index across the whole sentence; underlines and superscripts reuse the index at that point.
- Stats (right): a definition list with a 1px line on its left and 39u left padding; three columns, each with 28u side padding (none on the outer edges) and 1px lines between them. Each column is number above label: number Newsreader 38u, line-height 1, letter-spacing −0.02em, tabular figures; label Geist Mono 12u, letter-spacing .14em, uppercase, ink-soft, 14u gap. Values: **11.4M+** PLAYS, **38.2K** COMMUNITY, **24.9K** MEMBERS. Each column starts at opacity 0 and translateY(14px) and fades up over .9 s main ease with delays .35 s, .45 s, .55 s.

**6b. World frame (the rounded scene panel).** Fills the rest of the stage: flex 1, margin 0 16u 22u, border-radius 22u, clip-path inset(0 round 22u), background paper-deep, isolation isolate. On a 1440×900 screen it runs from about y 255 to y 878. The clip-path animates over 1.1 s cubic-bezier(.5,0,.1,1). During the intro it carries an "open" state whose clip-path is a negative inset reaching the viewport edges (top/left/right/bottom distances measured in JS and set as --ft/--fl/--fr/--fb), with no rounding, so the forming ring is never clipped; at reveal the open state is removed and the clip shrinks to the rounded frame. While entering it has z 101 and a transparent background; once not open it is overflow hidden. Layers inside, back to front:

1. Scene layer (z 0, inset −4%, so it can drift with the pointer): the sea still (object-fit cover, object-position 50% 62%) and over it the sea loop video (same fit and position, muted, loop, playsinline, preload none, opacity 0 → 1 over .8 s once it fires "playing"). A grain overlay sits on top (inset −4%, opacity .07, a 0.9 s steps(5) jitter loop through translate (0,0) → (−3%,2%) → (2%,−3%) → (−1%,−2%) → (3%,1%) → (0,0)).
2. Back petals (z 1).
3. The ring wall (z 2), see 6c.
4. Mist layer (z 3): left/right −6%, bottom −4%, height 46%, two white radial gradients (60%×70% at 18% 100%, rgba(250,252,253,.78) fading by 70%; 55%×60% at 82% 100%, rgba(250,252,253,.7) by 72%) plus a linear gradient to top from rgba(246,250,251,.55) to transparent at 75%. It starts at opacity 0 and translateY(18%) and rises to opacity .92 over 1.6 s (opacity over .9 s) at reveal.
5. Front petals (z 3) and light motes (z 4).

The scene layers (sky, mist, both petal layers, motes) stay at opacity 0 until reveal and then fade in over .9 s.

**Petals** (same data as the reference): leaf-shaped spans (border-radius 80% 0, height = 0.62 × width, opacity .85, shadow 0 1px 3px rgba(14,42,59,.18)), colours alternating white #FFFFFF and pale aqua #D6EEF3. Each item is [left %, top %, width px, duration s, delay s, layer]: back layer — [4,14,9,29,0], [14,4,7,34,−12], [24,26,8,31,−21], [36,10,6,37,−5], [46,30,9,27,−16], [56,6,7,33,−27], [66,20,8,30,−9], [76,2,6,36,−24], [86,24,9,28,−3], [94,12,7,35,−18], [30,44,6,39,−31], [60,40,7,32,−13]; front layer — [10,50,14,23,−6], [40,62,12,26,−19], [70,56,16,21,−11], [88,46,13,24,−2], [52,70,11,28,−23]. Colours by list position: white, aqua, white, aqua… (the original alternation: back items 1,3,5,7,9,11 white, 2,4,6,8,10,12 aqua; front items aqua, white, white, aqua, aqua). Every third petal (index % 3 = 0 within its layer) uses the mirrored keyframes. Drift keyframes (linear, infinite): 0% opacity 0, translate(−6vw,−12vh) rotate 0; 8% opacity .85; 50% translate(14vw,18vh) rotate 260deg; 92% opacity .85; 100% opacity 0, translate(34vw,46vh) rotate 540deg. Mirrored: 0% (6vw,−12vh); 50% (−12vw,16vh) rotate −240deg; 100% (−28vw,44vh) rotate −500deg.

**Motes**: 14 round glows (radial-gradient white f2 → #bfeaf3 at 45% → transparent at 70%), items [left %, top %, size px, duration s, delay s]: [8,62,10,14,−2], [18,40,6,18,−9], [27,70,14,16,−5], [36,52,8,20,−13], [44,30,5,17,−3], [53,66,12,15,−11], [61,44,7,19,−7], [69,74,16,14,−1], [77,36,6,21,−15], [85,58,11,16,−8], [92,46,7,18,−4], [13,82,9,22,−17], [48,84,13,17,−6], [72,22,5,23,−19]. Keyframes ease-in-out infinite: 0% opacity 0 scale .6; 20% opacity .9; 50% opacity .55, translate(14px,−9vh) scale 1; 80% opacity .85; 100% opacity 0, translate(−6px,−20vh) scale .7.

**Pointer parallax**: on fine pointers only (and not with reduced motion), pointer x and y are mapped to −1…1 across the window and smoothed by a spring (stiffness 40, damping 18, mass 1). Each layer is translated by (−x × depth, −y × depth × 0.5) px with depths: scene 10, back petals 22, mist 34, motes 40, front petals 48. The Build panel's scene and petals use the same parallax.

**6c. The ring of cards.**

Structure: the wall fills the frame (cursor grab, touch-action pinch-zoom, no text selection). Inside it a "lens" box (absolute, inset −100vh 0, carries the CSS perspective) contains the ring centre: a zero-size element at 50%/50% with preserve-3d and transform translate(--intro-x, --intro-offset) rotateZ(--intro-roll) rotateX(--intro-tilt) scale3d(s, s, --intro-sz), where s = wall-scale × --intro-scale and wall-scale = 1.1 on desktop (0.9 when the viewport is ≤760px tall, 0.8 on phones).

Cards: 16 slots, one per site. Each card is an anchor (opens the motionsites link in a new tab), height 160 px and width 160 × the site's ratio (so 284 px for 16:9, 256 px for 16:10, 240 px for 3:2), positioned with its centre on the ring centre (top −80 px, left −width/2), preserve-3d, starting at opacity 0. Inside: a tilt wrapper (preserve-3d), a frame (inset −9px, 3px border in the world colour, radius 24px, glow 0 40px 80px −30px world colour, clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0 round 24px) that opens to full in .55 s on hover), and the face (radius 16px, overflow hidden, backface hidden, navy #0E2A3B fill, shadow 0 18px 36px −24px rgba(0,0,0,.45), and a reflection below it: `-webkit-box-reflect: below 10px linear-gradient(transparent 52%, rgba(255,255,255,.32))`). The face holds the poster image (cover), the preview video (cover, muted, loop, playsinline, preload none, opacity 0 → 1 over .4 s on "playing"), a chip at bottom-left (14px in, pill, rgba(0,0,0,.45) background, white Geist Mono 13px, a 6px dot in the world colour, text "No. 01" … "No. 16"; it fades out on hover), and a label bar (12px from left/right/bottom, padding 11px 14px, radius 12px, world colour background, `--on` text; contents: world label in Geist Mono 500 12px .12em tracking, the site title in Newsreader 22px truncated, and an "↗" that springs from translate(−6px,6px) to 0 over .5s cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1) with .15 s delay; the bar is revealed by clip-path from the left over .5 s with 50 ms delay on hover). A paper-coloured overlay on the face rises to opacity .6 on cards whose world is not the one currently focused by the sentence hover.

Slot → site mapping: slot e shows site `((e − a·16 + min(3, N−1)) mod N + N) mod N`, where a = floor((360e/16 + rotation + 180) / 360) and N = 16 (with exactly 16 sites this is a stable offset of 3; during the intro rotation is treated as 0). Slot angle: `angle(e) = ((((360e/16 + rotation + 180) mod 360) + 360) mod 360) − 180`.

Ring geometry for expansion e ∈ [0,1] (e = 0 small intro ring, e = 1 final ring):
- tilt = −22 × (1 − e) degrees
- radius = 460 + 1340 × e
- anchor = −radius × sin(tilt) + 460 × sin(−22°) × (1 − e)
- perspective = 1000 + (760 − 1000) × e (final camera distance 760)
- roll = −20 × (1 − e) degrees
- card scale = 0.52 + (2.3 − 0.52) × e²

Card placement for a slot with angle r and formation f ∈ [0,1]: n = ((r + 180) mod 360), a = n/360, i = clamp((f − 0.7a)/0.3, 0, 1), s = 1 − (1 − i)³, yaw l = −180 + n × s, effective radius c = radius − (1 − s) × a × 24, x = −sin(l) × c, z = −cos(l) × c, appear = min(1, 2.5 i). The card transform is translate3d(x, 0, z) rotateY(l deg) scale(card scale) and its opacity = appear. A card is hidden if z × cos(tilt) ≥ perspective − 70 (behind the camera), or, once the intro is complete, if |r| > 96°. If z > radius² / perspective, the face is flipped with rotateY(180deg).

Per-frame camera values (A = wall-scale × (fit + (1 − fit) × e), fit = min(1.05, (innerWidth − 32)/1240, 0.66 × innerHeight/800) ÷ wall-scale, introOff = 0.44 × innerHeight − frame centre y): --intro-offset = introOff × (1 − e) + anchor × A px; lens perspective = perspective × A px; lens perspective-origin = 50% calc(50% + introOff × (1 − e) px); --intro-tilt, --intro-roll in degrees; --intro-x = 160 × sin(roll) × A px; --intro-sz = A; --intro-scale = fit + (1 − fit) × e. (So during the intro the small ring sits centred at 44% of the viewport height, tilted and rolled, slightly to one side, and it grows into the frame.)

Rotation: a target value m and a displayed value g that follows m with a spring (stiffness 150, damping 27, mass 1). Every frame (frame factor k = dt in ms ÷ 16.67, capped at 3): an easing factor E moves toward 0.2 when the mouse is over a card (checked every third frame with elementFromPoint) and toward 1 otherwise, by min(1, 0.08 k) of the gap. If not dragging, not focused inside the wall and not reduced motion, m increases by 0.3 × E × k degrees once the intro is complete; during the intro by 0.3 × (0.5 + 0.5e) × clamp((78 − m)/20, 0, 1) × E × k (so it spins until about 78° and eases off).
- Wheel (window listener, non-passive, Home view only, ignored over inputs or with Ctrl/Meta; it always prevents page scroll): delta = the larger of deltaY/deltaX, ×16 for line mode or ×innerHeight for page mode, then m += 0.5 × clamp(delta, −480, 480). Only after the intro completes.
- Drag (mouse button 0 on the wall, after the intro): m = start m + 0.2 × (the larger-magnitude of dx, dy); moving more than 4 px marks it a drag, and a click right after a drag (within 50 ms) is cancelled; cursor shows "grabbing".
- Touch (one finger, not starting on a card or input): same 0.2 factor.
- With reduced motion the spring jumps straight to the target.
- Card hover tilt: on mouse move over a card, normalised x/y in −0.5…0.5 set targets rotateX = −20 × y, rotateY = 24 × x, translateZ = 45 px, each on its own spring (stiffness 180, damping 24); leaving resets them to 0. Applied to the tilt wrapper.
- Videos: a card's preview video plays only when formation > 0.5, |angle| ≤ 78°, the tab is visible, the Home view is shown and reduced motion is off; its src is set the first time it needs to play; it pauses otherwise. When a slot's site changes, the video is paused, its src removed and reloaded.

**6d. Sentence hover and preview card.** Only after the intro has entered. Hovering a choice marks it active and the sentence "hovering": all words drop to opacity .28 except the active choice, whose words turn the `--on` colour while its marker sweeps in (scaleX 0 → 1, .5 s main ease) behind it in the world colour. For build/brand/learn the stage gets a focus attribute that dims every card of another world (a page-black overlay to .6). A preview card follows the pointer: a fixed anchor translated to the pointer by springs (stiffness 260, damping 28, mass 0.6), holding a 260 px card (radius 16px, surface background #141C22, shadow 0 30px 60px −28px #000 and a 1px rgba(238,244,246,.1) ring), placed so it always stays fully on screen: by default its bottom-left corner sits 18 px right of and 22 px above the pointer; if there is not room above (it would come closer than 12 px to the top edge) it flips to 22 px below the pointer, and if there is not room on the right it flips to the left side (18 px gap); a 24 px hysteresis stops it flickering on the threshold, and the final position is clamped 12 px inside every viewport edge; its transform-origin follows the corner nearest the pointer; opacity 0/scale .85 → 1/1 (.25 s / .35 s). Its media area is 146 px tall, shows that site’s poster as its background (and as the video poster) straight away, and plays the first site of that world (Look Circle for brand, Video Studio for build, Sphere Gallery for learn); below it a meta block (12px padding 14px, 12px Geist, line-height 1.5): a Geist Mono 500 11px .1em line with an 8px world-coloured square, "BRAND · LOOK CIRCLE" style text, then the world blurb. For "chat with Noa" the card turns night (#05090C), the media hides, and it shows "Ask me anything" in Newsreader 28px white with a 2px aqua caret blinking every 1 s (step-end), label "NOA'S ASSISTANT", blurb in #9fb4bf. Leaving the sentence clears everything and pauses the preview video. Clicking "startups" opens the Build view.

## 7. Build view (desktop)

A flex column, min-height 100svh − 92u.

- Panel: margin −15u 22u 0 24u (it starts at about y 77), height 716u, radius 24u, clip-path inset(0 round 24u), overflow hidden, background paper-deep, flex column centred. Inside: the same scene layer (sea still + sea video, object-position 50% 70%, grain, parallax depth 10) and a back petal layer containing all 17 petals.
- Headline: two lines "I take startups" / "from sketch to ship.", centred, Newsreader weight 460, 88u, line-height 76u, letter-spacing −0.015em, colour #0E2A3B (dark navy: it sits directly on the bright sky, so it stays dark in dark mode for contrast), margin-top 86u. Each word is masked and rises from translateY(110%) over .8 s main ease with delay 0.15 s + 0.06 s × index when the view is entered. A visually hidden line reads "Build: software for startups".
- Brief card: margin-top 60u, width 542u, padding 28u 30u 25u, radius 16u, dark glass: surface #141C22 at 86% (color-mix) with 10px backdrop blur, shadow 0 40px 80px −40px rgba(0,0,0,.8) plus an inset 1px rgba(238,244,246,.08) ring; all its text uses the light ink tokens, column gap 14u. It fades up (opacity 0, translateY 16px → 0 over .9 s, delay .45 s). Contents:
  - Kicker "SHARE WHAT YOU'RE CREATING": Geist Mono 11u, .1em, uppercase, ink-soft.
  - Sentence in Newsreader 25.5u, line-height 41u, three lines on desktop: "I'm creating [a booking app for gyms]" / "for [coaches in Porto], and I want it" / "[in 6 weeks] by next May / when it's ready." The blanks are text inputs styled as underlines (width = characters × 0.5em, with 23 and 17 characters; 1.5px ink-muted bottom border that turns accent on focus; placeholder ink-muted). The timeline is a radiogroup of three buttons ("in 6 weeks" checked by default, "by next May", "when it's ready", with a space before the second and " / " before the third); each button is ink-muted with a button-blue (#1E86AC) highlight behind it (inset .12em −.1em .04em, radius .22em, scaleX 0 → 1 from the left over .5 s) shown on hover and when checked, which also turns its text white; clicking selects it.
  - Note "GOES TO ME@NOAELLSWORTH.COM. NOA REPLIES, ALWAYS." in the kicker style.
  - Actions row (gap 14u): two 44u round ghost buttons (inset 1px line ring, ink-soft icon 20u, ring 1.5px ink on hover) — an eight-ray asterisk ("Copy this brief": copies the composed sentence to the clipboard and shows "Brief copied" in accent mono 11u for 1.6 s) and a target/orbit icon ("Share this brief": the Web Share API, or copy as a fallback) — then the send button "Send to Noa ↗": 40u tall pill, padding 0 22u, button-blue #1E86AC background (hover #2597C0), white Geist Mono 13u. The button is magnetic: on mouse move it translates by 0.3 × the x offset and 0.4 × the y offset from its centre, resetting on leave. Submitting opens `mailto:me@noaellsworth.com` with subject "A new brief" and body "Hi Noa, I'm creating <what> for <who>, and I want it <when>. Could we talk?" (empty blanks fall back to their placeholders).
- Under the panel: "WORKED AT" kicker (padding 24u 53u 26u) and two wordmarks 48u apart, Newsreader 27u: a wave line icon + "Fernway" and a peak line icon + "Quill Labs" (icons 42u wide, ink-soft, 1.6px strokes). Fades up with .7 s delay.

## 8. Opening sequence (Home)

| Time | What happens |
|---|---|
| 0 | Full-screen loader (fixed, z 100, page-black #0A0E11 background, light #EEF4F6 text). Top-left (3.2vh, 4vw), "Noa." in Newsreader clamp(64px, 9vw, 150px), line-height .95, −0.03em: each letter is in a mask and rises from translateY(105%) rotate(8deg) to rest over 1 s main ease with delays 0.10 / 0.18 / 0.26 / 0.34 s. Bottom-right (4vh, 5vw): the caption types "LOADING SITES" one character every 45 ms starting at 350 ms (Geist Mono 12px, .14em, ink-soft); below it a three-digit odometer (Geist Mono clamp(80px, 12vw, 180px), −0.09em tracking, each digit a column of 0–9 that slides .7 s main ease; unused leading digits hidden) rises into its mask over .9 s with .2 s delay, followed by a small "%". Bottom-left: a 44px round skip button "↗". |
| 0–2.6 s | Formation goes 0 → 1 linearly over 2.6 s: cards sweep around the small tilted ring one after another (placement formula above) above the loader (the wall and frame are z 101 with the frame clip open and its scene layers hidden). Meanwhile the odometer counts to (posters loaded ÷ 16) × 100, each change tweened over .65 s main ease; a 9 s failsafe forces 100%. |
| reveal (formation done and all posters loaded) | The loader fades out over .9 s and is removed after 1 s; the odometer slides up out of its mask (.5 s, cubic-bezier(.6,0,.8,.4)); the frame drops its open clip and animates to the rounded frame (1.1 s); its scene layers fade in (.9 s) and the mist rises (1.6 s); expansion goes 0 → 1 over 1.9 s with cubic-bezier(.5,0,.15,1); the loader "Noa." flies to the nav's "Noa" over 1.3 s with cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1) (translate to the target's top-left and scale by the ratio of font sizes) while its "." fades out over .5 s; when it lands, the real wordmark and nav fade in and the flying copy is removed. |
| reveal + 1.05 s | The page is marked "entered": sentence words rise (staggered), underlines draw in (1 s, delayed .35 s after each word), superscripts fade in, stats fade up. |
| reveal + 1.9 s | Expansion complete: the ring becomes interactive (wheel, drag, hover), its slot mapping follows rotation, and the constant 0.3°/frame auto-spin starts. |

Escape, Tab or the skip button (1px rgba(238,244,246,.16) ring) jumps straight to the final state. With reduced motion, or when the page is opened directly on #build, the intro is skipped entirely.

## 9. Views and routing

The two views are sections with ids view-home and view-build (not "home"/"build", so the #build hash never scroll-jumps). Links carry data-go="home"/"build"; clicking one shows that view, hides the other, plays a .6 s opacity fade-in on the shown one, updates aria-current in the nav, pushes #home or #build to history (back/forward work), scrolls to top, re-runs the Build entrance when entering Build, and switches the sea video so only the visible view's video plays (it starts loading the first time its view is shown). Opening the URL with #build lands on Build.

## 10. Phone and tablet (≤ 820 px)

Unit becomes 100vw/390. Nav 64 px tall, padding 0 16px, wordmark 24px, links 11px with 7px gap. Home: top row becomes one column (14px row gap, padding 4px 16px 16px); the sentence is clamp(26px, 7.4vw, 32px) with line-height 1.12, the forced line breaks and superscripts are removed so it reflows naturally; stats lose the outer line, columns get 16px side padding and a 6px gap, numbers 26px, labels 10px. The frame gets margin 0 10px 10px and radius 20px; the ring's wall-scale is 0.8. Build: panel margin 0 10px, auto height with min-height 100svh − 170px, bottom padding 22px, radius 20px; headline 46px/42px with 34px top margin and 12px side padding; the brief is full width minus 24px, padding 20px 18px, radius 14px, gap 12px, kicker 10px, sentence 22px/36px with its desktop line breaks removed and blanks at 0.44em per character; ghost buttons 40px (18px icons); send 40px tall, 12px text, padding 0 18px, never wrapping; "worked at" padding 18px 20px 24px, wordmarks 22px with 34px icons and 28px gap. There is no horizontal scrolling at any width from 320 px up.

## 11. Reduced motion

`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` hides the loader, stops the petals, motes and grain jitter, shows all text instantly with no transitions on masks, underlines, markers, frames or labels, keeps the scene as the still image (videos never play), keeps the ring static at its final shape, and makes wheel/drag move it directly without the spring. Changing the setting live re-applies this.

## 12. Acceptance checklist

- At 1440×900 after the intro: the sentence occupies three lines between about y 100 and y 225, the stats sit at the right behind a vertical line, the frame starts near y 255, and about seven landscape cards are visible in a gently curved row over the water with reflections, the outer ones larger and cut by the frame edge.
- The intro reads in order: name rises, count runs to 100, ring forms tilted above the loader, loader fades while the ring opens around you, the clip closes to the rounded frame and "Noa." lands in the nav.
- Wheel and drag spin the ring with spring easing; hovering a card slows the spin, tilts the card toward the cursor and reveals its frame and label; clicking opens the motionsites page.
- Hovering each sentence choice dims the rest, sweeps its marker, dims other worlds' cards and shows the matching preview; "chat with Noa" shows the dark assistant card.
- Build shows the centred headline, the brief with working blanks, radio chips, copy, share, magnetic send and mailto.
- The sea video loops on whichever view is showing; the still shows until it plays.
- No horizontal scrollbar at any size; layouts hold at 320, 390, 768, 1024×768 and 1440×900.

title: Shelf Hero
description: Give me the superdetailed exact prompt to recreate this page exactly as it is, including the correct asset URL, all elements, animations, and fonts. Single-screen filmography hero for a fictional film director, Leon Vasari. Features interactive cursor/mouse tracking and scrub-driven interaction, physical spring dynamics and kinetic damping with precision layout polish.
full_prompt:
# Prompt: Leon Vasari, VHS filmography shelf hero

Give me the superdetailed exact prompt to recreate this page exactly as it is, including the correct asset URL, all elements, animations, and fonts. This is that prompt.

## What it is

Build a single-screen **filmography hero** for a fictional film director, Leon Vasari. Use plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript in one file, with no framework, no build step and no libraries.

The page is a warm off-white sheet of paper. Across its middle runs a long, endless shelf of worn VHS tape boxes standing side by side, spine out. One tape, the active film, is pulled out of the shelf and **physically turned in 3D** so its illustrated front cover faces you. It is tilted a few degrees, lifted slightly and pushed towards the viewer.

- **Changing film:** click any spine, the arrows, a decade tab, scroll, drag or use the keyboard. The shelf slides, the open tape turns back into a spine, and the new one turns out to show its cover.
- **Caption:** the film's title, romanised Japanese title, kanji title and year sit under the shelf and slide up through a mask whenever the film changes.
- **Cursor:** a large custom ring cursor follows the mouse. It shrinks over spines and becomes a filled cobalt "OPEN / 開く" disc over the active cover.
- **Opening a film:** click the cover, the play ring or press Enter. A sheet of paper grows out of the cover, rotating from the cover's tilt to straight, until it fills the screen. It becomes a detail page whose poster bleeds in like ink blots spreading on paper, while each line of text rises out of its own mask.

Everything is driven by one `requestAnimationFrame` loop plus the Web Animations API, with no CSS keyframes. There is no opacity fade anywhere; every reveal is a mask slide, a clip or a scale.

### How the images are used

Put the two tables into JS as `SHEET[id] = [url, W, H]` and `CROP['spine-<id>' | 'cover-<id>'] = [sheet, x, y, w, h]`.

- **Spines and covers** are drawn as a cropped background on the box faces. For a box `x, y, w, h` on a sheet of size `W × H`, set:
  - `background-image: url(sheet)`
  - `background-size: (W/w·100)% (H/h·100)%`
  - `background-position: (x/(W−w)·100)% (y/(H−h)·100)%`

  The crop is stretched to fill the face exactly, so the spine is exactly `--ws` wide and the cover exactly `--d` wide.
- **The detail poster** is an SVG `<image>` of the cover's sheet, inside a `<g clip-path>` with a 474 × 900 rect, so the ink mask can still be applied.
  - Set the image's `href` to the sheet URL, with `x = −x·474/w`, `y = −y·900/h`, `width = W·474/w` and `height = H·900/h` (`preserveAspectRatio="none"`).
  - Only the cover's box then shows, stretched to 474 × 900.
- **Preloading:** preload the four sheet URLs as `Image()` objects on start, so the first turn never shows an empty face.

## Layout, top to bottom (desktop)

Everything is `position: fixed` and positioned from the centre of the viewport using `--H`, so the composition is identical at any desktop size.

### 1. Top bar

- **Bar:** 84px tall, 32px side padding, a 3-column grid `1fr auto 1fr`, items centred vertically.
- **Left:** a boxed label link "BACK / 戻る", aligned to the start, ink colour, no underline.
- **Centre, the logo:** a two-line stack centred with a 5px gap, all cobalt.
  - Line 1: "莱昂·瓦萨里" in Noto Serif SC 700, 22px, letter-spacing `.04em`.
  - Line 2: "LEON VASARI" in Inter Tight 600, 9px, letter-spacing `.34em`, with matching left padding so it is optically centred.
- **Right:** "CAREER 1958年〜1989年" as a `.lbl`, aligned to the end.

### 2. Decade tabs

- **Position:** centred horizontally, top at `50% − H/2 − 86px`, so they float just above the shelf.
- **Buttons:** five boxed `.lbl` buttons in a row, each 23px tall with 0 11px padding and a 1px border. `margin-left: −1px` makes neighbours share one border. Labels: "ALL / すべて" (written "All / すべて" and uppercased by the label style), "1950s", "1960s", "1970s", "1980s". Labels never wrap.
- **Indicator:** a cobalt block, absolutely positioned behind the buttons. It is the full 23px tall, and its `width` and `transform: translateX()` are set to the active tab's `offsetWidth` and `offsetLeft`. Both transition over `.6s var(--ease)`, so the cobalt block slides and stretches from decade to decade.
- **Active tab:** its text turns white via a `.45s` colour transition.
- **Which tab is active:** always the decade of the active film. For example, Noon in Ashes (1971) highlights "1970s". "ALL" is never highlighted.

### 3. The shelf (3D stage)

- **Section:** full width; top at `50% − H/2 − 40px`; height `H + 80px`.
- **Perspective:** `perspective: 2200px`, `perspective-origin: 50% 50%`, `touch-action: pan-y`.
- **Stage:** a zero-size `.stage` at `left 50%; top 50%` with `transform-style: preserve-3d`, holding every tape.
- **Tape element:** `.tape` is a zero-size box at the stage origin, with `transform-style: preserve-3d`, `will-change: transform` and two faces.

**Box dimensions**, measured from the real `--H` at load and on resize. Measure it by inserting an off-screen probe element with `height: var(--H)` and reading its height.

| Name | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| H | resolved `--H` in px | Tape height |
| ws | `H × 142 / 840` (≈ 0.169 H) | Spine width (front face) |
| d | `H × 474 / 900` (≈ 0.527 H) | Cover width = box depth |
| gap | `H × 0.03` | Gap between spines |

`ws` and `d` are written onto the stage as the CSS variables `--ws` and `--d`.

**Faces.** Each face is absolutely positioned, `H` tall, top at `−H/2`, with `backface-visibility: hidden` and a 2px radius.
- **Spine face `.sp`:** width `--ws`, left `−ws/2`, `transform: translateZ(d/2)`. This is the front of the cuboid.
- **Cover face `.cv`:** width `--d`, left `−d/2`, `transform: rotateY(90deg) translateZ(ws/2)`. This is the right-hand side of the cuboid. It also has `box-shadow: 0 30px 60px −28px rgba(20,16,10,.55)` so the pulled-out tape casts a soft shadow on the paper.
- **Shading:** each face has an `::after` overlay of solid black whose opacity comes from a `--shade` variable. As the box turns, the spine darkens to 55 % and the cover brightens from 50 % dark to fully lit. It reads as light falling across a turning object.

**Endless shelf.**
- **Copies:** render the 12 films **three times**, 36 tapes with virtual index `v = copy × 12 + i`. Wrapping then always happens far off-screen.
- **Relative position:** each tape's position comes from its relative index `r` to the current scroll value `s`. Take `(v − s)` modulo 36 into the range −18 … +18.
- **Culling:** tapes whose computed x is more than `W/2 + 1.5 d` from centre get `visibility: hidden` and are skipped.

**Horizontal placement.**
- **Formula:** the centre of a tape at relative index `r` sits at `x = F(r) = r·(ws + gap) + (d − ws + 1.6·gap)·B(r)`.
- **The smooth step `B(r)`:** for `|r| < 1` it is `(r + sin(πr)/π) / 2`, otherwise `±0.5`.
- **Effect:** spines step by spine width plus gap, and the open cover pushes neighbours apart by exactly half its extra width on each side. Because `B` is continuous, a fractional `s` slides everything smoothly with no jumps.

**Turning a tape.**

| Quantity | Formula |
|---|---|
| Openness `o` | `smoothstep(max(0, 1 − |r|))`, where smoothstep(x) = x²(3 − 2x). 1 for the active tape, 0 for spines; in between while the shelf moves, so tapes the shelf passes half-open and close |
| rotateY | `−90°·o + tiltY·o` (the box turns left until its right side, the cover, faces front) |
| rotateX | `tiltX·o` |
| rotateZ | `−4.5°·o` (the pulled-out cover leans slightly anticlockwise, like the reference) |
| translateZ | `o · 0.2 H` (pulled towards the viewer, so it looks bigger than the spines) |
| translateY | `−o · 0.025 H − lift · 0.045 H` (raised slightly; hovered spines rise more) |
| Transform order | `translate3d(x, y, z) rotateZ() rotateX() rotateY()` |
| z-index | `round(100 − |r|·4)`, so nearer tapes stack on top |
| `--shade` | Spine face: `o × .55`. Cover face: `(1 − o) × .5` |

**Hover lift.**
- **When it lifts:** hovering any tape that is not the active one (`|r| > .5`) sets that tape's lift target to 1. It eases towards the target at `1 − e^(−12·dt)` per frame, so the spine rises by 4.5 % of H, like a finger pulling it halfway out.
- **Tracking:** hover is tracked with `pointerenter` / `pointerleave` on each tape.

**Tilt towards the cursor.**
- **When the cursor is "on the cover":** within `0.55 d` horizontally of screen centre, within `0.55 H` vertically of the shelf centre, not in the detail view, and the shelf almost settled (`|T − s| < .3`).
- **On the cover:** `tiltY` targets `(mx − W/2) / (0.55 d) × 9°` and `tiltX` targets `−(my − cy) / (H/2) × 6°`.
- **Elsewhere:** `tiltY` drifts to `(mx − W/2)/W × 5°` and `tiltX` to 0.
- **Smoothing:** both ease at `1 − e^(−7·dt)`. The open cover leans gently towards the mouse like a card held in the hand.

### 4. Play ring

- **Shape:** a fixed 42px circle with a 1px cobalt border, cobalt colour, `rgba(237,235,230,.75)` fill, and a 12px solid play triangle nudged 2px right.
- **Position:** centred on the active cover's lower-left corner, at `left = W/2 − 0.5 d − 6px` and `top = shelf centre + 0.36 H`.
- **Scale:** `smoothstep(max(0, 1 − |T − s|·3))`. It pops in once the shelf settles and shrinks to 0 while the shelf moves or the detail is open.
- **Action:** clicking it opens the detail.

### 5. Caption

- **Position:** a centred stack, top at `50% + H/2 + 30px`, 9px gap, `pointer-events none`.
- **Masked lines:** each line is an `overflow: hidden` mask, `width: min(92vw, 760px)`, centred text.
  - **Title:** Newsreader 400, 31px, line height 1.12, letter-spacing −.01em (e.g. "Noon in Ashes").
  - **Subtitle:** a `.lbl` in cobalt at weight 500: romaji, " / ", kanji (e.g. "HAI NO SHOGO / 灰の正午").
  - **Year:** Inter Tight 500, 11px, letter-spacing .08em (e.g. "1971").
- **Swap animation, whenever the active film changes:**
  - A new span is appended. Its siblings are absolutely positioned over the first, so the two overlap inside the mask.
  - The new span slides from `translateY(dir × 105%)` to 0.
  - Every older span that is not already leaving slides from its current transform to `translateY(−dir × 105%)` and is removed when done.
  - Timing: 650ms, `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)`, `fill: both`.
  - `dir` is the direction of travel: +1 going right, so text comes up from below; −1 going left, so it comes down from above.
  - When you flip quickly through several films, each intermediate title passes through the mask in turn.
  - Calling setActive also updates the decade indicator.

### 6. Arrows

- **Buttons:** two 44px buttons at the caption title's height (`top: 50% + H/2 + 40px`), 20px in from each side.
- **Icons:** 18 × 10 SVG arrows, a 1.2px stroke in currentColor. Left: a chevron `M5 1 L1 5 L5 9` plus a shaft to x 17. Right: the mirror image.

- **Element:** 58 × 58px, fixed, centred on the pointer with −29px margins, `z-index 100`, shown only on fine pointers.
- **Parts:**
  - A 1.5px ink ring (border radius 50 %).
  - A 6px ink centre dot.
  - A hidden label "OPEN" over "開く" in Inter Tight 600, 10px, line height 1.25, letter-spacing .1em, white, centred.

| State | When | Ring | Dot | Label |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| default | anywhere else | scale 1, ink border, transparent | scale 1 | hidden (scale 0) |
| `.spine` | over a non-active tape | scale .72 | 1 | hidden |
| `.btn` | over any button or link outside the shelf | scale .55 | scale 0 | hidden |

## Motion engine

### State
- `s`: the current scroll position in tape units.
- `T`: the target.
- `hover`: the hovered virtual index, or −1.
- `active`: the film index currently in the caption.
- `mx, my`: the raw pointer; `cx, cy`: the smoothed cursor.
- `tiltX, tiltY`, `onCover`, `isOpen`.

### Each frame
- **Time step:** `dt` is clamped to 50ms.
- **Spring:** `s += (T − s) × (1 − e^(−k·dt))`, with `k = 5.2` normally and `18` while dragging. It snaps when within 1e−4. A one-step move settles in about 0.9s, and multi-step jumps glide through every tape in between.
- **Normalising:** if `s` drifts beyond ±4 full loops, both `s` and `T` shift by whole loops.
- **Caption:** the active film is `round(s) mod 12`. When it changes, run the caption swap with `dir = sign(T − s)`.

### Inputs
- **Click a tape:** if it is the active one (`|r| < .5`), open the detail. Otherwise set `T = round(T + r)`, so the shelf glides that tape to the centre.
- **Arrows:** `T = round(T) ± 1`.
- **Keyboard:** Left and Right do the same. Enter opens the detail when focus is on the body. Escape closes it.
- **Decade tabs:** jump to the first film of that decade by the shortest way round the loop. "ALL" jumps to The Silent Valley.
- **Wheel:** both axes; use whichever delta is larger. `T += delta / (ws + gap) × 0.5`. After 160ms of no wheel input, `T` snaps to the nearest integer. Wheel input is ignored while the detail is open.
- **Drag:**
  - `pointerdown` on the shelf records the start x and `T`.
  - Once the pointer moves more than 5px it becomes a drag: `T = T0 − dx / (ws + gap)`, with the faster spring.
  - `pointerup` snaps `T` to the nearest integer.
  - A drag suppresses the click on the tape it ended over.

## Opening a film: paper sheet and ink reveal

The detail is a fixed full-screen `.detail` dialog (`z-index 60`, `--sheet` background, `visibility hidden` until opened).
- **Grid:** two equal columns with a `4vw` gap and padding `110px 6vw 56px 7vw`.

### Contents

- **Close button:** a boxed `.lbl` "CLOSE / 閉じる" at the top left (32px, 31px).
- **Logo:** a copy of the cobalt logo, centred in an 84px top band.
- **Left column**, centred vertically, `max-width 520px`, 18px gap, top to bottom. Every line is wrapped in its own overflow mask:
  1. The cobalt subtitle `.lbl`, "ROMAJI / kanji".
  2. The title, Newsreader 400, `clamp(44px, 5.4vw, 84px)`, line height 1, letter-spacing −.025em.
  3. The meta `.lbl` in muted grey, "YEAR / GENRE / N MIN" (e.g. "1971 / WESTERN / 112 MIN").
  4. The synopsis, Newsreader 400, 17px, line height 1.5, `max-width 42ch`.
  5. An italic credit, Newsreader italic, 15px, muted: "Written and directed by Leon Vasari. 監督作品".
  6. A 44px boxed button, cobalt border and text, 0 20px padding, 10px top margin: "WATCH THE FILM / 映画を見る".
- **Right column: the poster.** Height `min(100%, 78vh)` with aspect ratio 474/900, centred.
  - It is an inline SVG with viewBox `0 0 474 900` holding one clipped `<image>` of the film's cover crop (see Media), masked by an ink mask.
  - **The ink mask:** a `<mask>` in user space (−200, −200, 874 × 1300) containing a group of seven white circles.
  - **Ink filter on that group:** `feTurbulence` fractalNoise, baseFrequency .011, 3 octaves, seed 7, feeding an `feDisplacementMap` with scale 120 on the R and G channels. The circles' edges become ragged, bleeding blots.

| Blob | cx | cy | Delay (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 150 | 330 | 0 |
| 2 | 340 | 600 | 120 |
| 3 | 250 | 120 | 220 |
| 4 | 90 | 760 | 300 |
| 5 | 400 | 250 | 360 |
| 6 | 260 | 860 | 420 |
| 7 | 230 | 470 | 180 |

### Open sequence (`openDetail`)

1. **Prepare.**
   - Snap `T` to an integer and fill the detail texts from the active film.
   - Point the poster `<image>` at its cover's sheet, positioned so only its crop box shows (see Media).
   - Reset all blob radii to 0.
   - Read the screen rect of the active tape's cover face (`getBoundingClientRect`, which gives the projected 3D box).
2. **The sheet grows out of the cover.**
   - Make the dialog visible and set its `transform-origin` to the cover's centre.
   - Animate it with the Web Animations API over **1050ms**, `cubic-bezier(.76,0,.18,1)`, `fill both`.
   - From `clip-path: inset(top right bottom left round 3px)`, matching the cover rect, with `transform: rotate(−4.5deg)`.
   - To `clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0 round 0)` with `rotate(0)`.
   - A blank rectangle of paper the exact size and tilt of the cover straightens and expands until it covers the screen.
3. **Text rises.** Every masked line slides from `translateY(110%)` to 0 over **900ms**, `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)`. Delays are `620ms + index × 75ms`, so the lines arrive one after another.
4. **The poster bleeds in.**
   - Starting 520ms after open, a rAF loop grows each circle's radius from 0 to 720 over **1250ms** after its own delay, with an ease-out cubic `1 − (1 − p)³`.
   - The cover appears as spreading ink blots that merge into the full poster.
   - The loop stops after 2.4s.
5. **Hide the rest.** The play ring scales to 0, and the cursor drops its OPEN and spine states while over the sheet.

### Close (`closeDetail`: the Close button or Escape)

- Animate the sheet back from full screen to the current cover rect, with `rotate(−4.5deg)`, over **850ms** with the same ease.
- When it finishes, hide the dialog and cancel all its animations so the next open starts fresh.

## Responsive (≤ 767px)

- `--H: min(60vw, 40svh)`. Every tape dimension follows from it.
- **Top bar:** 64px tall, 16px padding. The logo becomes 17px over 7.5px. Labels are 9px. **The career label is hidden.**
- **Tabs:** sit at `50% − H/2 − 70px`, with 0 7px padding and 9px text.
- **Caption title:** 24px.
- **Arrows:** 6px from the edges.
- **Footer:** 16px sides, 18px bottom, 9px labels.
- **Detail:** a single column that scrolls vertically.
  - Padding `84px 22px 40px`, 24px gap.
  - The poster moves first and is `46svh` tall.
  - Title 42px, synopsis 16px. The Close button sits at 16px, 21px, and the logo band is 64px.
- **Touch:** the custom cursor is not shown. Dragging the shelf with a finger scrubs it, because the shelf uses `touch-action: pan-y`.

## Reduced motion

With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`:
- The scroll spring and hover lift become instant (k = 1), so tapes snap between states.
- Caption swaps replace the text without sliding.
- The sheet open, close and text rises run with 1ms duration and no delay.
- The ink starts 5s in the past, so the poster is fully visible at once.

## Accessibility

- The tabs are a `<nav aria-label="Decades">` and the shelf is a `<section aria-label="Filmography shelf">`.
- The caption container is `aria-live="polite"`, so film changes are announced.
- Arrow and play buttons have `aria-label`s ("Previous film", "Next film", "Open film").
- The detail is `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"`. The poster SVG is `aria-hidden`.
- All controls are real `<button>`s and links.

## Acceptance checklist

- On load, Noon in Ashes is turned out at the centre: tilted −4.5°, lifted and casting a shadow. The other eleven spines repeat endlessly on both sides, about 13 visible at 1440px.
- Clicking a spine two places to the right glides the shelf: the open tape turns back into a spine while the next ones turn out in passing, and the caption rolls through each title.
- The cobalt tab block slides to the new decade.
- The cursor ring shrinks over spines and becomes a cobalt "OPEN / 開く" disc over the cover, which leans towards it.
- Clicking the cover grows a tilted sheet of paper out of it to full screen. The detail text rises line by line, and the poster bleeds in as ragged ink blots.
- There are no opacity fades anywhere.

full_prompt:
# Recreation prompt — "Kai Renn / KR.ST" dark three-view portfolio

Build a single-page, dark-mode portfolio for a fictional motion and brand designer called Kai Renn (wordmark "KR.ST"). It has three views switched by a floating dock: (1) Gallery, a WebGL sphere of looping website preview videos that you spin, zoom into and open an overview for; (2) Projects, a WebGL grid of the same videos with glass-lens edges, frosted labels and hover-to-play; (3) About, a WebGL page where a chrome robot head floats over a centred serif headline and a horizontal, endlessly looping text track slides past it, each line of text pulling away from the head like a magnet. Everything below is exact: reproduce every value.

The whole thing is one HTML file. Three.js 0.160.0 (ES module from jsDelivr, via an import map that maps "three" to https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js and "three/addons/" to https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/) and GSAP 3.12.5 (https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/gsap/3.12.5/gsap.min.js, global) are the only libraries. No sound.

---

## 1. Media (all are MotionSites preview videos, 16:9 MP4, H.264, CORS `*`)

The Gallery uses items 1–20; Projects uses items 1–24. Six more (a/3dcha "Character Studio", designs/finsmith-fish-3d "FinSmith", aaaf/vante-ribbon-hero "Vante Ribbon", designs/honey-bee-melli-landing "Melli", aaaf/oraciteslArea "Oracite", aaaf/fernhollow "Flower Valley") exist in the data list but are not shown.

Every video keeps its native 16:9 aspect ratio everywhere. Nothing is cropped to portrait.

## 2. Fonts

Self-host three latin WOFF2 files from Google Fonts (or load the same families from Google Fonts):
- "Geist", variable weight 100–900, normal (https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/geist/v5/gyByhwUxId8gMEwcGFU.woff2).
- "Newsreader", weights 300–500, normal (https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/newsreader/v26/cY9AfjOCX1hbuyalUrK4397yjA.woff2).
- "Newsreader", weights 300–500, italic (https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/newsreader/v26/cY9CfjOCX1hbuyalUrK439vCjohC.woff2).

Stacks: sans = "Geist", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif. Serif = "Newsreader", ui-serif, Georgia, serif. All WebGL text is drawn into canvases with these fonts after document.fonts.ready.

## 3. Head and tokens

Title "Kai Renn — Motion & Brand Designer". Meta description: "Kai Renn is a motion and brand designer. A spinning sphere of interactive website work, a curated project index and a studio page." Viewport: width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover.

Colour tokens: --bg #0c0c0d (page and every WebGL clear colour), --ink #ededeb (all primary text), --mute #8a8a88 (secondary text), --pill #1c1c1e, --pill-h #262628, --line #232325. html and body are full height, overflow hidden, overscroll none, antialiased. Every view is a fixed full-viewport section (opacity 0, visibility hidden until shown) holding one absolutely-positioned canvas container.

Easing used in CSS everywhere: cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1). GSAP "expo.out" is the house ease for text reveals.

## 4. The dock navbar (shared)

A single frosted capsule fixed at the bottom centre: bottom 18px, centred with left 0 / right 0 / margin auto / width max-content (no transform). Padding 5px, gap 4px, radius 12px, background rgba(28,28,30,.66), backdrop blur 16px, 1px border rgba(255,255,255,.06), shadow 0 12px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.45), z-index 50. It starts at opacity 0 with no pointer events.

Contents left to right: the wordmark "KR.ST" (Geist 600, 14px, tracking −0.02em, padding 6px 10px 6px 8px, links to Gallery); a 1px × 18px divider (rgba(255,255,255,.1), 4px side margins); three tabs; another divider; the menu dot button.

Each tab is a 30px-tall flex row, padding 0 9px, radius 5px. It holds an italic Newsreader label (17px, line-height 1, max-width 0 and opacity 0 when inactive) and a Geist 500 number (12px, translateY −1px). Hover background rgba(255,255,255,.06), active background rgba(255,255,255,.1). The active tab animates its label to max-width 120px, opacity 1, margin-right 3px (max-width and margin over .7s on the house curve, opacity over .4s), while its number shrinks to 10px and lifts to translateY −6px, becoming a superscript, also over .7s. Tabs: "Gallery" 1, "Projects" 2, "About" 3.

The menu dot is a 30px square, radius 5px, with a 4px ink dot that scales ×2.2 (.5s) when open. Clicking it toggles a menu panel that opens upward: fixed, bottom 66px, centred (left 50%, margin-left −110px), 220px wide, padding 14px, radius 8px, background rgba(22,22,24,.82) with 18px blur and a 1px --line border. Closed it sits at translateY 6px, scale .98, opacity 0. Open: no transform, opacity 1, transitions .35s opacity and .5s transform on the house curve, transform-origin bottom centre. Inside: a 12px mute line "Available for select projects from January." then three serif 17px rows separated by 1px --line rules: "Studio 03", "Index 02", "Sphere 01" (the numbers are 11px Geist mute, right-aligned). Each row routes to its view.

The dock appears once: when the Gallery intro bursts into the sphere (or immediately on any other view) it tweens from y 16px, opacity 0 to y 0, opacity 1 over .9s expo.out and gains pointer events.

Routing: hash-based (#gallery default, #projects, #about). Switching fades the current view to opacity 0 (.35s power2.in), stops its render loop, hides it, then shows the next and fades it in (.5s power2.out). Each view is built lazily on first visit and keeps its state afterwards.

## 5. View 1 — Gallery (sphere of videos)

Renderer: WebGL, alpha true, antialias on non-touch devices, pixel ratio min(dpr, 2). Perspective camera, fov 60, at z 12. A conversion px(v) = v × (2 × 12 × tan(30°)) / viewportHeight turns CSS pixels into world units at the sphere's depth.

Layout constants: radiusX/Y/Z 250px (×0.8 when the viewport width is 1025–1440), planeSize 104px (×0.8 in the same range; 72px at ≤640), centerScale = planeSize × 120/82, expandHeightVh 70, expandPush 1.8, expandFade 0.1, expandDuration .8s power4.out. Twenty planes (PlaneGeometry 1×1, MeshBasicMaterial transparent, double-sided, depthWrite off, starting colour #1b1b1d until its video has a frame). Plane scale: the longer side equals planeSize, the other follows the video's aspect (16:9 → wider than tall). The texture is the full video frame: repeat (1,1), offset (0,0).

Positions: a Fibonacci sphere. For item i of N: y = i×(2/N) − 1 + (1/N), r = sqrt(1 − y²), angle = π×(3 − √5)×i, position = (cos(angle)×r, y, sin(angle)×r) times the radii. On phones (≤640) the radius is the half-width minus 24px minus half a plane. Every plane always faces the camera: its quaternion is the inverse of the sphere group's quaternion.

Spin model, every frame:
- drag: velocity += pointer delta × 0.001 (x drives yaw, y drives pitch); wheel and two-finger pinch add deltaY × 0.0002 to yaw.
- velocity × 0.94 each frame (friction); accumulated angle is smoothed with a factor of 0.11; the per-frame difference of the smoothed angle is applied as a rotation about world Y (yaw) and world X (pitch), premultiplied into the group quaternion.
- idle: an auto-spin of 0.001 rad per frame about an axis tilted 23° from vertical, which stops for good after the first user interaction.

Videos: each plane's video starts loading 200ms into the intro and plays once it has a frame. Every 300ms, videos on the far hemisphere are paused (when the plane's direction faces away: z/length below −0.25; resumes above −0.1) so only around ten decode at once. While a plane is zoomed, all others pause.

Intro sequence (first visit only):
- The centre shows the wordmark "KR.ST" drawn in Geist 600 64px into a canvas, displayed 90px wide, fading in (.6s, .2s delay).
- Side labels "Kai Renn" (left) and "Motion & Brand Designer" (right), Geist 13px, sit at 9% from each edge in overflow-hidden masks and slide up from yPercent 100 (.9s expo.out, stagger .07s, delay .5s). They are hidden at viewport ≤1024px.
- A counter at the bottom (Newsreader 14px, 3 digits, "001") slides in from below (.75s power4.out, .5s delay) and then tweens towards the share of loaded circle videos (.5s power1.out each update, capped at 099).
- After 2s, once the first ten videos have frames (or 30s pass), the counter tweens to 100 and slides out upward. The first ten planes appear on a circle of radius 240px (×0.75 on phones), starting at −90° and 36° apart, each fading in (1s power3.out) and scaling from 0.01 to 70px with back.out(1.7), staggered 0.1s. The circle spins 0.5° per frame.
- 1.3s later the spin ramps up to 7.3× over 1s (power2.in).
- 0.8s after that the wordmark fades out (0.75s power2.inOut), the side labels slide up out of view, and the ten planes collapse into the centre (1.25s power2.inOut, stagger 0.05s), stacking 1.5px apart in depth and growing to centerScale.
- 0.2s after the collapse ends, everything explodes: all twenty planes move from the centre (or from their stack position) to their sphere positions over 1s power3.out, with an overshoot multiplier of 1 + 0.1 × sin(π × t). The side labels slide back in, the dock rises in, and the "DRAG TO EXPLORE" hint (Geist 10px, tracking .24em, mute) fades in at the bottom.
Reduced motion skips the intro and shows the finished sphere with no auto-spin.

Hover: raycast on pointermove (batched once per frame). The hovered plane's title and category appear in the bottom caption (13px Geist 500 title, 14px Newsreader mute category, 6px gap); the caption text leaves upward (.25s power2.in) and the new one rises from yPercent 110 (.6s expo.out). The cursor is "pointer" over a plane, "grab" within 250px of the centre, otherwise default; "grabbing" while dragging.

Click (pointer moved under 6px and total path under 10px):
- Clicking a plane expands it: expand 0→1 over .8s power4.out. Its target height is 70% of the visible height (minus the reserved overview band), its width follows its aspect, and on phones it is capped at the viewport width minus 16px. It moves to the centre of the screen. All other planes are pushed outward ×1.8 and fade to 10% opacity. Its video plays. A cursor label "Overview" (Geist 500 12px, dark text on rgba(237,237,235,.92), radius 4px, offset 14px from the pointer) follows the mouse via gsap.quickTo (.5s power3.out) and scales from .6 to 1 (.6s power4.out) while over the zoomed plane.
- Clicking the zoomed plane again opens its overview: a reserved band of 290px opens at the bottom (factor 0→1, .8s power4.out), shifting the plane up by half that band and shrinking it to 70% of the remaining height. The overview panel (max 600px wide, centred, bottom 78px) fades up from y 16 (.7s expo.out, .12s delay). It shows the title (Geist 500 15px) with "Category, Year" (Newsreader 15px mute), a Close button (12px, 26px tall, --pill), the description (Newsreader 17px, line-height 1.35, #cfcfcc, max 54ch) and three 11px tags on --pill: "Preview video", "MotionSites", "Live WebGL". The cursor label changes to "Close".
- Clicking the zoomed plane while its overview is open closes the overview. Clicking anywhere else, pressing Esc or using the Close button collapses the zoom.

## 6. View 2 — Projects (WebGL grid)

Renderer: antialias, opaque, clear colour #0c0c0d, pixel ratio min(dpr, 2). Perspective camera fov 35, placed at (width/2, −height/2, height/2 / tan(17.5°)), looking at (width/2, −height/2, 0), so one world unit equals one CSS pixel and the page runs downward along −y.

Layout (in px): columns 3 above 1024px, 2 at 641–1024px, 1 at ≤640px. Page padding 8, column gap 8, row gap 40. Tile width = (viewport − 16 − gaps) / cols; tile height = width × 9/16 (tiles are 16:9). The headline sits 200px from the top and is centred: "A Curated Selection of " (Geist 500 16px, tracking −0.16px) followed by "Motion and Interactive Sites" (Newsreader 400 17px). On phones it breaks into "A Curated Selection of Motion and" / "Interactive Sites" with a 20px line step. The grid starts 80px below the headline. Under each tile, 12px below: the title (Geist 500 12px, ink), then 6px lower "Category, Year" (Newsreader 13px, mute). A footer, Newsreader 13px mute, sits 240px below the last row: "Kai Renn — Index 2019–2026" centred (on phones split as "Kai Renn" left and "Index 2019–2026" right).

Tile shader: each tile samples a still (uTex) and its video (uTex2) and crossfades by uMix. Before its media lands it shows a skeleton of grey 0.085 with a diagonal shimmer band (sweep = fract(time × 0.6), band = smoothstep(0.18, 0, |(u+v)/2 − sweep|) × 0.035). uReveal fades from skeleton to media.

Loading: a tile starts loading when it is within 1.6 viewports below or 0.6 above the visible area. It creates its video (preload auto), seeks to min(1.2s, 30% of the duration), draws that frame into a 480px-wide canvas as the still, and reveals it (uReveal 0→1 over .8s power2.out).

Chip: at the tile's top-left (8px inset) sits a frosted label "01  Motion" (index two digits, two spaces, category; Geist 500 12px, padding 8px sides, 6px top, 4px bottom, radius 4px). Its shader blurs the tile's own media under it with a 32-tap golden-angle spiral (radius 40px), mixes that toward rgb 0.05 by 45%, and draws the label text on top. It follows the same still/video crossfade as the tile.

Glass-lens post pass: the scene renders into a 4×-multisampled render target, then a fullscreen pass refracts the top and bottom 8% of the screen. Inside a band, t runs 0 at the inner edge to 1 at the screen edge, sag(t) = 1 − sqrt(1 − t²), and the sample is pushed toward the inner edge by sag × band × strength (1). Inside the bands a 16-sample spectral dispersion spreads samples along y by (t − 0.5) × 0.01 × distortion × 30 with red/green/blue weights smoothstep(.8,.2,t) / smoothstep(0,.5,t)×smoothstep(1,.5,t) / smoothstep(.2,.8,t). The result is converted to sRGB at the end.

Scroll: wheel adds deltaY to a target; touch drags add the finger delta with inertia (velocity × 0.95 per frame). The rendered offset eases toward the target by 0.12 per frame and clamps between 0 and page height minus viewport height.

Hover (desktop wider than 1024px): the hovered tile's video starts playing and uMix tweens to 1 (.45s power2.out); leaving tweens it back to 0 and pauses. A 64px round "View" bubble (italic Newsreader 16px, dark on rgba(237,237,235,.94)) follows the pointer through gsap.quickTo (.5s power3.out) and scales .6→1 with opacity (.75s power4.out on enter, .6s on leave). On touch or ≤1024px, the tile closest to the viewport's vertical centre plays instead.

Entrance: the headline pieces fade in (.3s) while their letters resolve out of random ". : · , ; _" glyphs over 1.1s (power2.out; each character resolves once progress passes 0.7 × its position + 0.3 × random). Tiles, chips, titles and categories fade in and rise 60px (opacity .9s power2.out, position 1.2s expo.out), delayed .35s + .08s per column + .06s per row.

Click a tile: a lightbox fades in (.45s) over a rgba(8,8,9,.86) backdrop with 14px blur. It holds the video at up to 1100px wide and 70vh tall (16:9, contain, radius 6px) rising from scale .94, y 20 (.9s expo.out). Below it: the title (Geist 500 15px) with "Category, Year" (serif mute), the description (serif 17px), and a Close button. Esc, Close or clicking the backdrop closes it and unloads the video.

## 7. View 3 — About (chrome bot + horizontal magnetic text track)

Renderer: antialias, opaque, clear colour #0c0c0d, scene background #0c0c0d, output sRGB, no tone mapping, pixel ratio min(dpr, 2). Camera fov 45 at z 13. A half-float render target the size of the canvas holds the scene without the bot and the lens disc, for the click effect.

Environment (for the chrome): a PMREM of a small black room (background #0a0a0b) lit by emissive white panels: a 14×5 ceiling panel at y 6 (intensity 1.1), a 3.2×10 strip at x −6 (1.0), a 2.4×10 strip at x 6 (0.85), a 12×2.2 panel behind at z −6, y −1.5 (0.6), a 5×4 panel in front at (3, 2.5, 6) (0.8) and a 14×6 floor at y −6 (0.22). Keeping every panel at or below about 1.1 is what avoids bloom-like blocks.

The bot (own model, built from primitives and centred on its bounding box):
- Head: a sphere of radius 1 scaled (1.1, 1, 0.98) in chrome (MeshPhysical, white, metalness 1, roughness 0.07).
- Visor: a front patch of the same sphere (phi from π/2 − 1.02 over 2.04 rad, theta from π/2 − 0.5 over 1.0 rad), scaled 1.5% larger, in near-black glossy material (#040405, metalness 0.3, roughness 0.12, clearcoat 1, clearcoat roughness 0.04).
- Eyes: two capsules (radius 0.075, length 0.2) at x ±0.3, y 0.03, sitting on the visor surface, flattened to 45% depth, in an unlit #f2f2ee material.
- Antenna: a chrome stem (0.022–0.03 radius, 0.42 tall) at y 1.15 with a 0.095 chrome ball at y 1.38.
- Ears: chrome tori (radius 0.2, tube 0.065) at x ±1.1 with dark visor-material caps (cylinders of radius 0.15).
- Halo: a chrome torus (radius 0.78, tube 0.05) under the head at y −1.28, tilted 0.92 × 90°, spinning at 0.35 rad/s.
- Scale: the bot is always 200px tall on screen (×0.9 at ≤1440px wide, ×0.85 at ≤1024px), placed at the screen centre, z −1.

Shader additions on all bot materials (injected with onBeforeCompile):
- Liquid-glass reveal: a front line rises from the bounding-box bottom minus the band (0.97) to the top plus 0.25 × band, wavy by value noise (amplitude 0.95 × (1 − reveal)). Fragments above it are discarded. Within one band below it the surface is mixed toward a brighter, #8fa0ff-tinted "liquid" look, with a blue (#1621ff) shimmering meniscus line (power-3 falloff, ×1.4).
- Hover glow: a #1621ff glow around the raycast hit point (radius 1.09 world units, spread 0.262, falloff power 3, brightness 0.4), multiplied by a hover factor that eases toward 1 at 0.1 per frame on hit and back toward 0 at 0.05 per frame.

The reveal runs 0→1 over 3.85s power2.out with a 1s delay on the first visit (0.45s on later visits). Clicks are ignored below 0.8.

Behaviour every frame:
- Mouse follow: the target rotation is x = clamp(vertical offset from the centre ÷ half the height, ±0.62), y = clamp(horizontal offset ÷ half the width, ±0.59), z = 0.2 × horizontal offset. The current rotation eases toward it at 1 − (1 − 0.08)^(60 × dt). Before any mouse movement on desktop the target is (−0.62, 0.59, 0.2); on phones it is 0.
- Float: y = sin(phase) × 0.2 × amplitude × reveal, where the phase advances by dt × 1.5 × speed, eased with factor 1 − (1 − 0.08)^(60 × dt).
- Blink every 3–5s: the eyes squash to 10% height over 0.18s and back.
- Sleep: after 30s with no mousemove, wheel, pointerdown, touchstart or keydown (desktop only, fully revealed), the eyes close to 20% height (1.1s power2.inOut), the rotation target tweens to (0.42, 0, 0.12) over 1.4s, and the float slows to speed 0.35 and amplitude 1.6 (1.6s). Any input wakes it: speed and amplitude return over 0.8s, the eyes snap open, and the head shakes.
- Head shake: the y offset goes +0.22 (0.09s), −0.18 (0.12s), +0.10 (0.11s), then 0 (0.18s).

Click on the bot (fully revealed, not mid-effect):
- The rotation freezes. A lens disc (a circle of radius 1 at z −8) scales from 0 to 10 world units over 4s expo.out; once it passes 6.14 it dissolves (0→1 over 0.8975s sine.inOut), then resets.
- The disc samples the background render target in screen space and pulls it toward the centre: zoom pull = 0.5 × 0.30 × nd², where nd is the distance normalised to the disc's screen radius. The rim (from nd 0.85) is pulled inward by 0.2344. Chromatic dispersion of 1.64 × 0.004 applies from nd 0.6, with 8 samples and per-channel Gaussian weights.
- Light on top: a white nova (Gaussian, size 4 × glow 11 × 0.003, intensity 0.285 × 11/17 × 1.15), a #252ba7 ring at radius 0.49, width 0.08 (×0.9 × 11/17 × 1.8) with a wide aura, a thin white rim at 0.483, and an edge ring at 0.478 (width 0.06, softness 1, intensity 1.053, #252ba7).
- Dissolve order: the light fades by 60%, the distortion by 80%, and the alpha from 80% to 100%.
- At the same time the bot plays one of two alternating hit reactions, then the head shake:
  - Recoil: rotation x −0.45 and y +0.18 (0.16s power3.out) with the eyes squashed, then back with elastic.out(1, .45) over 0.9s.
  - Spin: one full turn on y (1.1s power3.inOut) with a z wobble of 0.25 settling with elastic.out(1, .5).

Text layer: all text is drawn into canvases (software-backed 2D contexts, willReadFrequently, drawn at the renderer's pixel ratio, linear filtering, no mipmaps) on planes at z −8. One world unit equals visibleHeight(at z −8) ÷ viewport height px.

Headline: a full-viewport canvas centred on the screen. Newsreader 300 at 75px (62px at ≤640; at ≤1024 it shrinks to fit the widest word and wraps), line height 1.18, tracking −0.01em, ink. Three lines:
- "Shaping quiet systems into"
- "restless, precise and wildly kinetic"
- "Motion™ that people remember."

The "™" is Geist 400 24px (16px at ≤1024), raised by 0.2 × the font size and spaced 8px after "Motion". Fifty-six pixels below the last line, centred, is "Currently at Northfold® Studio" in Geist 500 14px (12px on phones). Hovering just "Northfold® Studio" fades a background-coloured plane over it to 50% opacity (0.55s expo.out).

Horizontal track: the wheel (whichever of deltaX or deltaY is larger) and swipes on either axis move a target. The rendered offset eases toward it at 0.12 per frame, with touch inertia of 0.95 per frame. Scrolling down or right moves the content left. Every element's x is wrapped with ((x + L/2) mod L) − L/2, so the track loops forever and the headline returns after the last stop. L = (end of the last block + 260px, or 140px on phones) + half the viewport width.

The track starts half a viewport plus 200px (70px on phones) to the right of the headline. Stops alternate between above the centre line (block bottom 78px above centre; 64px on phones) and below it (block top 78px below centre). Each stop advances x by max(0.62 × block width, 200px) + 90px (150px + 60px on phones). Blocks are left-aligned.

Every block starts with a grey heading (Geist 500 12px, mute). The ten stops, in order:
1. Paragraph, top. "Motion" over "Product films, UI motion and 3D loops that explain a product in seconds." (Newsreader 300 22px, 29px line step, wrapped at 320px; 16px below the heading).
2. List, bottom. "Interactive" over "WebGL Sites", "Scroll Stories", "Creative Development", "Prototyping" (Newsreader 400 18px, 7px gaps).
3. Chapter, top. "Part One  ·  Craft", then a numeral "I" in Newsreader 300 72px, then "Tools change every season. The habit of finishing things never ships late." in Newsreader 300 19px, 26px line step, max 300px.
4. Quote, bottom. "“Loud is easy. Calm takes work.”" in Newsreader italic 300 40px (30px on phones), 1.12 line step, max 440px, then "— Studio note, 2024" in the grey heading style.
5. Stats, top. "Recognition" over "06  Sites of the Day", "03  Motion awards", "02  Type juries", "14  Years in motion" (Geist 400 18px, 9px gaps).
6. Paragraph, bottom. "Identity" over "Brand systems and type direction that move as well as they sit still."
7. Chapter, top. "Part Two  ·  Rhythm", numeral "II", "Interfaces are music you can touch. Timing decides how a page feels."
8. List, bottom. "Selected clients" over "Halden", "Oaro", "Velmo Labs", "Fieldhouse", "Marlo Bikes".
9. Quote, top. "“Break something on purpose, then keep the best part.”" with "— Studio note, 2025".
10. Links, bottom. "Contact" over:
    - "hello@krst.example →", which opens mailto:hello@krst.example.
    - "See the full index →", which opens #projects.
    - "Booking from January", in mute colour and not a link.
    All three are in Newsreader 300 22px. Linked lines dim to 50% opacity on hover (0.55s) and show a pointer cursor.

Magnetic make-space (the key interaction): the bot owns an oval keep-out zone on the text plane, with radius X 3.4 world units and Y 4.0543 (both ×0.7875 at ≤640) and 0.35 of padding.
- Every frame, for each line of each block, take the horizontal distance from the bot to the nearest point of that line's own text: 0 if the text spans the bot's x.
- If that distance is less than the X radius, the oval's half-height there is h = Ry × sqrt(1 − (d/Rx)²) + padding. A line above the bot must keep its lower edge at least h above centre; a line below must keep its upper edge at least h below centre.
- Lines are processed from the one nearest the bot outward. Each line's need is at least its inner neighbour's current shift, so lines never overlap.
- Each shift eases toward its need with a factor of max(0.1, 0.14 − 0.012 × k), where k is the line's order from the inside, so the nearest line leads and the outer lines follow a touch later. All of them ease back to their resting place once the bot has passed.

A "SCROLL →" hint (Geist 11px, tracking .22em, mute, bottom 78px) fades in from x −8 (0.9s expo.out, 1.6s delay). Its arrow nudges 5px right in a 1.6s loop. It fades out at the first scroll.

## 8. Mobile and reduced motion

Phones: the sphere radius fits the width, plane 72px, circle ×0.75, and the side labels are hidden. Projects shows one column with the tile nearest the centre playing. On About, the headline wraps and shrinks to fit, blocks narrow to min(viewport − 56px, 300px), the band and quote shrink as noted above, and the keep-out oval is ×0.7875. The dock stays centred at the bottom.

prefers-reduced-motion: CSS transitions are off, the Gallery intro is skipped, there is no auto-spin and no Projects scramble, the About reveal is instant and the float is off.

## 9. Acceptance checklist

- The Gallery loads with the counter, circle spin, collapse and explode, then a sphere of 20 looping 16:9 videos that drag-spins with inertia, auto-spins until touched and shows a hover caption. Clicking a plane zooms it; clicking it again opens the overview; Close or Esc collapses it.
- The dock shows "KR.ST | Gallery¹ 2 3 | •" with the expanding italic label on the active tab, and its menu opens upward.
- Projects shows a 3-column 16:9 WebGL grid with refracted, colour-fringed top and bottom bands, frosted index chips, video crossfade on hover, a "View" bubble, smooth wheel scroll and a lightbox on click.
- About shows the centred serif headline with the chrome bot pouring in as liquid glass and following the mouse. The text track scrolls sideways forever, and every line slides up or down out of the bot's oval and settles back after it passes. Clicking the bot fires the blue lens burst over the text, and the bot naps after 30 idle seconds.
- There are no console errors, all three fonts load, and no request fails except a missing favicon.

# Leon Vasari: Curved VHS Archive (exact recreation prompt)

Give me the superdetailed exact prompt to recreate this page exactly as it is, including the correct asset URL, all elements, animations, and fonts. This is that prompt.

## What it is

Build a single-screen **film archive hero** for a fictional director, Leon Vasari. Use plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript in one file, with no framework and no libraries.

The page is warm off-white paper.
- **The shelf:** across the middle, worn VHS tapes stand on a **curved arc that recedes into depth**. Spines get smaller, darker and more tightly packed toward both edges, about 11 per side. They turn slightly toward the centre and sit lower as they go back, like a shelf bent into a shallow bowl.
- **The active tape:** the tape at the centre is **turned 90° in 3D** so its illustrated front cover faces you, pushed slightly forward, over a soft floor shadow.
- **Background:** two columns of giant halftone kanji, **映画** on the left and **の記憶** on the right, sit behind the shelf.
- **Caption:** under the cover, the film's title is set big and bold in cobalt, with its romanised and kanji titles, a short rule and "YEAR — GENRE". Arrows sit on either side.
- **Timeline:** a ruler from 1955 to 1990 runs along the bottom. A cobalt dot glides to the active film's year.
- **Detail sheet:** clicking the cover grows a sheet of paper out of it into a full-screen detail page. Its poster bleeds in like ink.

Everything runs on one `requestAnimationFrame` loop plus the Web Animations API. There are no opacity fades: every reveal is a mask slide, a clip or a scale.

## Media: every asset URL

All 24 images come from **four Higgsfield GPT Image 2.5 sheets** with transparent backgrounds, loaded through the Higgsfield image proxy as WebP. The art is fictional, unbranded VHS art. Each spine and cover is a rectangle cropped out of a sheet with CSS backgrounds; there are no separate image files.

**What the art looks like:**

Crop boxes are in sheet pixels, `x, y, w, h`:

**Cropping:**
- Store the tables as `SHEET[id] = [url, W, H]` and `CROP['spine-<id>'|'cover-<id>'] = [sheet, x, y, w, h]`.
- A face's background is `background-image:url(sheet); background-size:(W/w·100)% (H/h·100)%; background-position:(x/(W−w)·100)% (y/(H−h)·100)%`.

## Fonts (all embedded as base64 WOFF2)

| Newsreader (variable 200–800, roman and italic) | 400 | Detail synopsis and italic credit |

| Noto Serif SC | 700 | (embedded, not visible in this layout) |
| "Noto Sans JP Big" | 800 | The giant 映画 / の記憶 only: a Google Fonts subset of Noto Sans JP 800 with `text=映画の記憶`, `font-display:block` |

- **Serif stack:** `"Newsreader",Georgia,serif`.

--H:min(47vh,33vw);  /* tape height; min(68vw,40svh) on phones */

- `body` is paper, with hidden overflow, `user-select:none` and antialiasing. On `(pointer:fine)` the native cursor is hidden.
- **Paper grain:** a fixed full-screen layer (z 40, no pointer events, `mix-blend-mode:multiply`, opacity .6). It is a 220px SVG tile: `feTurbulence` fractalNoise (baseFrequency .85, 3 octaves, stitchTiles) through `feColorMatrix` `0 0 0 0 .45 / 0 0 0 0 .42 / 0 0 0 0 .38 / 0 0 0 .22 0`.
- **`.lbl`:** Inter Tight 600, 10.5px, line-height 1, letter-spacing .14em, uppercase.
- **`.box`:** inline-flex, 21px tall, 0 8px padding, 1px `--rule` border.

## Layout (desktop; everything fixed)

1. **Top bar:** 76px tall, 36px side padding, space-between, all cobalt.
   - **Left:** a link `.lbl` "LEON VASARI", a 40 × 1px line, then "FILM ARCHIVE", with 16px gaps.
   - **Right:** "FILMS", "ABOUT", "JOURNAL" (34px gaps), then a burger of two 1.5px lines, 26 × 12px.
2. **Halftone kanji:**
   - Fixed, z 1, `writing-mode:vertical-rl`, font "Noto Sans JP Big" 800 at `min(19vh,12.5vw)`, line-height 1.02, letter-spacing .02em.
   - The fill is a dot screen: transparent text with `background-clip:text` over `radial-gradient(circle at 50% 50%, rgba(64,82,138,.55) 0 36%, transparent 40%)` at 3 × 3px, plus a flat `rgba(110,122,160,.26)` wash.
   - **映画** sits at left 2.4vw, top 13vh. **の記憶** sits at right 2.4vw, top 9vh.
3. **Floor shadow:**
   - Position: centred at `top:calc(--cy + H×.47)`, width `min(96vw, H×3.6)`, height `H×.26`.
   - Fill: `radial-gradient(50% 50% at 50% 40%, rgba(40,32,20,.30), rgba(40,32,20,.10) 55%, transparent 72%)`.
4. **Shelf:**
   - The section spans the full width, top `--cy − H/2 − 50px`, height `H + 100px`, with `perspective:1400px` at `50% 50%`, z 10 and `touch-action:pan-y`.
   - A zero-size `.stage` at the centre has `preserve-3d`.
   - **Each tape** is a zero-size `preserve-3d` box with two faces. Faces are H tall, top −H/2, `backface-visibility:hidden`, radius 2px.
     - **Spine face `.sp`:** width `ws`, `translateZ(d/2)`.
     - **Cover face `.cv`:** width `d`, `rotateY(90deg) translateZ(ws/2)`, shadow `0 34px 60px -30px rgba(20,16,10,.6)`.
   - **Shading:** each face has a black `::after` whose opacity comes from `--shade`.
5. **Play ring:** a fixed 42px circle with a 1px cobalt border, `rgba(236,232,224,.8)` fill and a 12px cobalt triangle. It sits on the cover's lower-left corner (`left = W/2 − d/2 − 6`, `top = shelfCentre + .36H`).
6. **Caption:** a centred grid at `top: --cy + H/2 + 4.2vh`, 10px gap. Each line sits in an overflow mask, `min(80vw,640px)` wide.
   - **Title:** Inter Tight 600, `clamp(28px,3.4vw,46px)`, letter-spacing −.015em, cobalt (e.g. **Noon in Ashes**).
   - **Subtitle:** a cobalt `.lbl` at 9.5px, letter-spacing .24em, "ROMAJI / kanji" (e.g. `HAI NO SHOGO / 灰の正午`).
   - **Rule:** 18 × 1px, cobalt.
   - **Year line:** Inter Tight 500, 10.5px, letter-spacing .08em, ink, `YEAR — GENRE` (e.g. `1971 — WESTERN`).
7. **Arrows:** two 44px cobalt buttons on the title's line, at `50% ± min(19vw,250px)`. They hold 24 × 12 arrow SVGs (1.2px stroke): `M6 1L1 6l5 5M1 6h23` and its mirror.
8. **Timeline:** left and right 36px, bottom 64px, 40px tall.
   - A cobalt 1px line at 12px (opacity .75).

   - A 9px cobalt dot rides the line.

9. **Footer:** left/right 36px, bottom 24px, cobalt `.lbl`s: "© LEON VASARI. ALL RIGHTS RESERVED." on the left and "FB / TW" (links) on the right.
10. **Cursor:** 58px, fixed, z 100.
    - **Parts:** a 1.5px ink ring, a 6px ink dot, and a hidden white label "OPEN" over "開く" in Inter Tight 600 10px.

    - **States:**

## Film data (shelf order; the page opens on index 5)

| # | id | Title | Romaji | Kanji | Year | Genre | Min | Synopsis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | valley | The Silent Valley | SHIZUKANA TANI | 静かな谷 | 1958 | Drama | 104 | A schoolteacher returns to the mountain village that exiled her father, and finds the valley has kept every one of its secrets. |
| 1 | bluehour | The Blue Hour | AO NO TOKI | 青の刻 | 1962 | Romance | 97 | Over one long evening in a harbour town, a widow and a stranger trade small lies until the light runs out. |
| 2 | river | River of Salt | SHIO NO KAWA | 塩の川 | 1964 | Drama | 121 | Two brothers drag a salt barge downriver to a city that no longer wants anything they carry. |
| 3 | summer | The Last Summer | SAIGO NO NATSU | 最後の夏 | 1966 | Drama | 109 | The summer before the dam floods their village, three friends set fire to everything they cannot take with them. |
| 4 | green | The Green Road | MIDORI NO MICHI | 緑の道 | 1969 | Mystery | 101 | A surveyor mapping a forest road keeps finding the same footprints, always one day ahead of him. |
| 5 | noon | Noon in Ashes | HAI NO SHOGO | 灰の正午 | 1971 | Western | 112 | A rider crosses a white desert to settle an old debt, and learns too late who sent him. |
| 6 | observer | The Observer | KANSATSUSHA | 観察者 | 1973 | Thriller | 96 | A night watchman begins to suspect that the building he guards has started watching him back. |
| 7 | birds | The Fallen Birds | OCHITA TORI | 落ちた鳥 | 1975 | Drama | 118 | When the birds stop singing over a frontier town, the mayor’s daughter is the only one who goes looking for the reason. |
| 8 | storm | Light in the Storm | ARASHI NO HI | 嵐の灯 | 1978 | Drama | 127 | A lighthouse keeper and his son wait out a three-day storm with a shipwrecked sailor who will not give his name. |
| 9 | tide | The Long Tide | NAGAI SHIO | 長い潮 | 1981 | Drama | 99 | A fisherman’s wife counts the tides on the harbour wall while her husband’s boat fails to come home. |
| 10 | war | A Quiet War | SHIZUKANA SENSO | 静かな戦争 | 1985 | Comedy | 103 | Two neighbours fight a silent war over a garden wall for thirty years, and neither will say how it began. |
